# Lightwork — User Experience Audit (September 2026)

> Base commit `6daa3165` on `main` · prepared 2026-09-30 · companion to
> `PLATFORM_IMPROVEMENT_AUDIT.md` (September 7), `QA_FINDINGS.md` and `CODE_QUALITY_AUDIT.md`.

## What this is

An adversarial review of Lightwork **from the user's side of the screen**: the end user asking the
workforce to do work, the workspace administrator who is not a programmer, the IT/security owner,
the developer integrating with it, the compliance officer using the governance workbenches, and the
evaluator in their first hour. The mandate was to find every way the platform can be improved —
bugs, ease of use, missing customization, missing features — and to hold it to its own bar in
[`docs/customer-experience-contract.md`](docs/customer-experience-contract.md) and to the claims in
the README.

The earlier platform audit was code-first and did not reach first-run onboarding, config/wizard
parity, performance, the channels, the MCP server, the learning loop, the domain packs or the
non-CLI apps. This review started from those gaps and from the running product.

## How the evidence was gathered

- **The running product.** An isolated lab (a fresh `MAVERICK_HOME`, the dashboard on loopback and a
  deterministic OpenAI-compatible fake model that can answer, ask a clarifying question, call a tool,
  stall or fail on demand) was driven with Playwright in Chromium at desktop (1400×900) and phone
  (390×844) sizes. Every GET page in the app (160 pages, 320 loads) was crawled with axe-core, link
  checks, a copy scan and four themes. The chat, flow designer, workforce, settings, workspace and
  governance journeys were walked end to end, including crashes, restarts, provider failures and
  stops.
- **The CLI and wizard.** `lightwork init` was driven through the consumer, express, advanced,
  `--fast` and `--from-file` paths in throwaway homes; `doctor`, `preflight`, `start`, `serve`, `mcp`
  and the REST API (OpenAPI spec, curl lifecycle, MCP stdio handshake) were exercised directly.
- **The code.** Twenty-two subsystem maps (about 17,800 lines of file:line notes) were built first;
  every code-level defect in them was re-opened at HEAD and translated into what a user experiences.
- **The market.** Competitor capabilities were taken from vendor documentation fetched during the
  review (Microsoft Copilot Studio and Power Automate, Google Gemini Enterprise, Salesforce
  Agentforce, UiPath, OpenAI, Anthropic, Zapier). Pages that could not be fetched are marked in the
  individual findings.
- **The test suite.** The full suite ran at HEAD: 38,576 passed, 15 failed, 634 skipped (33 min on
  4 cores). All 15 failures were traced to this environment (missing optional `psycopg`/`sqlalchemy`,
  and user-site packages hidden from child processes by the per-test `HOME`); with those fixed all 15
  pass. Three developer-experience findings came out of that work (UX refs in the Coordinator section).

## How to read it

Every finding cites evidence a skeptic can check:

- **reproduced** — the behavior was observed in the running product or by a script (steps, output
  or screenshot path in the evidence);
- **code-verified** — the cited code was re-read at HEAD and shows the behavior;
- **gap, search basis stated** — only for missing features/customization: the exact search that
  found nothing is quoted.

Severity: **P0** data exposure, security breach or a core journey broken for most users · **P1** a
major feature broken or unusable for a persona, or a serious trust gap · **P2** significant friction,
partial breakage, misleading behavior or an important missing option · **P3** polish.

Evidence that cites `shots/…`, `u*work/…`, `C5*/…` or `map/…` refers to the review's working set
(screenshots, scripts and subsystem maps) kept outside the repository; every finding also cites the
repository file and line, the command or the page that shows the behavior.

Findings reported independently by more than one reviewer were merged into one entry that keeps
every source id and all of their evidence. Duplicates were found by clustering on shared file:line
anchors and title similarity, followed by a manual pass; a few related-but-distinct findings were
deliberately kept apart, and some residual overlap may remain.

## The verdict

Lightwork has more capability in its codebase than almost any competitor ships, and a user can feel
little of it. The product's promises — a governed, multi-tenant, provably improving AI workforce that
a non-programmer can run — break at the seams between subsystems more often than inside them. The ten
patterns below account for most of the 92 P0/P1 findings.

These patterns describe the September 30 audit baseline. Later **Current branch** notes under
individual findings record source fixes or narrowed claims; a code fix is not an installed
customer acceptance result.

1. **Workspace isolation leaks through side stores.** The world database is per workspace, but goal
   feedback (UX-001) and run-trace annotations (UX-002) were found in shared stores;
   the runtime-overrides finding (UX-016) was later reconciled as a deployment-wide
   control plane restricted to global administrators. Workspace removal and recovery once had member-access and retained-data traps (UX-005; local fix described below). The shared browser-session gap has a source fix with local isolation checks (UX-024).
2. **Secrets and keys escape.** `{{secret('NAME')}}` in a flow reads any server environment variable,
   including the platform's own model key (UX-003); test runs store the resolved value
   (UX-010) and live runs write it to the signed audit log (UX-011). "Keys
   excluded" backups historically included tenant signing and at-rest keys (UX-018; fixed in source and verified by a CLI archive check); a server-wide KMS key
   id overrides a workspace's own key (UX-019); vendor questionnaire tokens are returned
   in plaintext to any viewer (UX-026).
3. **The governance gates are uneven.** A goal routed to a specialist ignores the caller's role and
   regulatory restrictions (UX-012). The shared task-start risk gate has since been fixed
   for product entry points (UX-014). The weaker flow tool-call shield (UX-022)
   has been replaced in source by the agent's tool-call classifier; A2A, federation and the agent bus screen incoming text before any agent tool decision. Shell needs per-command approval while
   `notebook_exec` historically ran model-written Python with none (UX-025; execution gates added in source). Most settings changes
   leave no audit record (UX-023); `record verify` now requires a trusted signing key
   (UX-017). Four-eyes review is impossible in one place (UX-056) and
   unsatisfiable on single-user installs in others (UX-072).
4. **"On the models you choose" is not true yet.** On every OpenAI-family provider (OpenAI, Azure,
   Gemini, OpenRouter, DeepSeek, xAI, Moonshot, Ollama, vLLM, TGI) the orchestrator silently loses its
   spawn, specialist, tool-discovery and knowledge tools because 237 tools are truncated to the first
   128 (UX-051; the current branch now caps the agent catalog and makes overflow discoverable). The original unpriced-model path called and billed before
   refusing; the current branch guards dispatch and offers an in-product
   reviewed-ceiling path (UX-050);
   free OpenRouter models still hit that refusal (UX-206); Azure and Bedrock now have
   local Settings setup paths awaiting live tenant acceptance (UX-074); self-hosted endpoints always fail "Test connection"
   (UX-054).
5. **The first hour ends in dead ends.** Consumer setup without an isolated work area now tells users
   that file changes and program execution are off and points them to Permissions; the installed
   recovery journey still needs live acceptance (UX-047). The former
   default-on rehearsal hold is now watch-only by default; explicit Hold mode
   now routes a paused step to Approvals, with installed-app acceptance open
   (UX-048). 964 of
   2,031 specialists refuse to run under default settings and nothing says which (UX-070).
   "Results" shows 2,031 placeholders instead of the user's work (UX-069); every running chat
   says "Attachments and available evidence are ready." as its answer (UX-038); a provider
   failure reads "Lightwork stopped — internal error" (UX-066); a crash leaves chats
   "Working…" forever (UX-060).
6. **Channels do not work from the product.** The Channels page cannot produce a working channel (no
   allowed-senders field, UX-035), channels only run in a separate `lightwork serve` process
   nothing starts (UX-065), readiness passes when the chat SDK is missing (UX-037),
   people in Slack/Telegram/email never see the agent's question (UX-036), intake stops after
   about 10,000 messages (UX-059), and there is no Microsoft Teams (UX-077).
7. **Copilot is a help widget, not an operator.** The contract says Copilot must perform every
   authorized operation; it can perform none of the everyday ones (UX-082), cannot see live
   state (UX-083), relays "I completed the request" when nothing happened
   (UX-109), and forgets the conversation on every page change (UX-283).
8. **Customization stops at the deployment.** Every Settings change applies to the whole deployment;
   there is no per-workspace settings screen and no per-person layer at all (UX-363,
   UX-346, UX-359). Important controls are config-file only — the autonomy dial
   (UX-073), single sign-on (UX-075), a workspace's own AI key (UX-363) —
   and dozens of user-facing limits are hard-coded (Customization section). Several stores also hit
   hard caps with no retention path and then refuse work: channel intake at 10,000 messages, knowledge
   at 2,048 rights requests, learning promotions at 1,000 records (UX-059, UX-062,
   UX-255).
9. **The learning story overclaims.** Skills distilled from successful runs are never recalled
   (UX-049); the causal "placebo refutation" cannot fail (UX-099); snapshots and
   rollback cover six stores, not the guardrails and habits the flywheel writes (UX-247,
   UX-246); flow "hardening" can never apply (UX-090).
10. **The public story overclaims and the help is missing.** The older "hard dollar/wall-clock caps"
    claim did not match every entry path (UX-092); the docs home advertised session providers that
    did not exist (UX-091). The private-repository contact and task-report links (UX-055, UX-046)
    now have source fixes, including an in-product report draft; installed public-site acceptance
    remains open. The original audit also found no complete UI guide (UX-089) and a thin Help page
    (UX-390); their current coverage needs separate verification.

### What is genuinely strong (verified; protect these)

Governed connector writes with durable prepare/commit receipts; least-privilege specialist envelopes
with attenuation for spawned children; purpose- and consent-bound knowledge access; a signed,
hash-chained audit trail; self-hosting and air-gap operation; the learning lifecycle's snapshot,
hindsight and rollback primitives; importers for n8n, Make, Power Automate and UiPath; Ekko's
privacy-first work discovery; the external-agent governance plane; typed flow inputs, automatic
approval gates before risky flow actions, versioning with restore, and a cron-free schedule picker;
and a clean page-level accessibility baseline (no horizontal overflow at 390 px, no duplicate ids,
no images without alt, axe violations limited to nine distinct rules).

## Suggested sequence

1. **Stop the bleeding (days).** The five P0s and the P1 trust findings: per-workspace keying for
   feedback, annotations and runtime overrides; purge-or-tombstone on workspace removal and never reuse
   a removed id; a secret allow-list for flows, never persisting rendered params, and redaction in the
   audit row; escape the vendor hero; key exclusion in backups; the specialist capability intersection;
   the goal-risk gate on every entry path; one shield scan for every dispatch path; approval for
   `notebook_exec`; audit rows for every settings writer.
2. **Make the first hour work (1–2 weeks).** Tool prioritization before the OpenAI 128-tool cap;
   pre-dispatch price checks and a plain-language unpriced-model path; the Docker-less consumer default;
   rehearsal holds that create an approval instead of refusing; a readiness badge per specialist; a
   real Results inbox; provider-failure messages with a cause and remedy; orphan recovery that runs
   continuously; a pruned, append-only provider spend ledger (it slows every model call today and
   eventually blocks them, UX-088).
3. **Finish the half-built surfaces (2–4 weeks).** Channels hosted by the dashboard with a sender
   allow-list field and question round-trips; Teams; Microsoft 365 OAuth; the Automations hub script
   order; flow delete/unpublish; approvals in the inbox; Copilot bound to the shared operation catalog
   with live state.
4. **Open up customization (ongoing).** A per-workspace settings screen, a personal preferences page
   (language, time zone, notifications, default specialist), and knobs for the hard-coded limits listed
   in the Customization section — each with a wizard step, per kernel rule 6.
5. **Tell the truth in the docs.** Rewrite the headline claims that no longer hold, publish a UI user
   guide, point support links somewhere a customer can reach, and move internal audit material
   (including this document) out of the customer-shipped checkout (UX-137).

## P0 — fix before anything else

#### UX-001 · P0 · Trust · Thumbs-up/down feedback (including the free-text note) on one workspace's goal is shown on another workspace's goal with the same number

- **Who / where:** end user, workspace admin, compliance, IT/security · `GET /api/v1/goals/{id}/feedback (goal page rating widget)`
- **User impact:** In a multi-workspace (multi-client) install, a user in workspace B opening their goal #N sees workspace A's rating, reviewer name and private comment for A's goal #N, and the 'what your workforce learned' human-feedback count mixes all workspaces. This is a cross-tenant disclosure of reviewer notes, which often quote the confidential deliverable.
- **Evidence (reproduced):**
  - packages/maverick-dashboard/maverick_dashboard/goal_feedback_store.py:26-27 — one deployment-global goal-feedback.ndjson next to the dashboard overlay, not per tenant
  - packages/maverick-dashboard/maverick_dashboard/goal_feedback_store.py:51-58 — latest_for_goal(goal_id) matches on goal id only; owner/tenant ignored
  - packages/maverick-dashboard/maverick_dashboard/api.py:9518-9528 — GET checks access to the CURRENT tenant's goal N, then returns whatever row has goal_id N
  - packages/maverick-core/maverick/world_model.py:4645-4668 — each tenant gets its own tenants/<t>/world.db, so goal ids restart at 1 per workspace
  - cmd: audit/C5c_repro/r01_feedback_xtenant.py (TestClient, temp MAVERICK_HOME) → acme posts note 'ACME-CONFIDENTIAL: numbers wrong for Project Falcon' on goal 1; after switching to globex, GET /api/v1/goals/1/feedback returns 200 {"note":"ACME-CONFIDENTIAL: numbers wrong for Project Falcon","by":"operator",...} (output: audit/C5c_repro/r01.out)
  - [U2-024] packages/maverick-dashboard/maverick_dashboard/goal_feedback_store.py:26-27 — path = dashboard_overrides_path().parent/'goal-feedback.ndjson' (not tenant-scoped)
  - [U2-024] goal_feedback_store.py:51-58 latest_for_goal(goal_id) ignores owner/tenant
  - [U2-024] packages/maverick-dashboard/maverick_dashboard/api.py:9519-9528 GET returns that row ({rating, note, by, owner}) to anyone who can open the goal
  - [U2-024] goal ids restart per tenant DB on SQLite (map 04: tenants/<t>/world.db), so goal #3 in workspace A and B share a feedback row
  - [U2-024] chat_goal.html:1165-1169 pre-selects the thumb from this row on page load; also only the last 5,000 rows are read (:23), so older ratings silently disappear
- **Recommendation (effort S):** Store feedback per tenant (data_dir('goal_feedback', tenant=current_tenant)) or key rows by (tenant, goal_id, conversation owner) and filter on read; migrate the existing global file by assigning rows to the default tenant only. Add a two-tenant regression test mirroring r01. Also scope count() used by /api/v1/flywheel.
- Source: C5c-001, U2-024 · prior audit: 000-row tail, W3-27 (related: 5, W3-27 (related: same store, still present), unbounded tail) — cross-tenant keying not previously reported

#### UX-002 · P0 · Trust · Run-trace annotations written in one workspace appear on the same-numbered goal in every other workspace

- **Who / where:** end user, workspace admin, compliance, IT/security · `GET/POST /api/v1/goals/{id}/annotations (goal replay trace)`
- **User impact:** Notes a reviewer pins to steps of a run in client A's workspace show up on client B's run with the same number (and pins/saved views/gallery share the same file), exposing A's review commentary to B's users and corrupting B's trace review.
- **Evidence (reproduced):**
  - packages/maverick-core/maverick/ux_store.py:39-43 — UxStore resolves data_dir('dashboard') once at construction
  - packages/maverick-core/maverick/ux_store.py:210-216 — shared() is a process singleton; reset_shared() has no non-test caller (grep)
  - packages/maverick-dashboard/maverick_dashboard/app.py:8511-8543 — annotations read/write by goal_id through that singleton
  - cmd: audit/C5c_repro/r08_probe.py → in tenant acme POST annotation 'ACME-ONLY: step 1 leaked salary data' on goal 1 (201); switch to globex, GET /api/v1/goals/1/annotations → {"annotations":[{"seq":1,"note":"ACME-ONLY: step 1 leaked salary data",...}]} (output: audit/C5c_repro/r08.out)
- **Recommendation (effort S):** Resolve the UxStore path per call from the active tenant (cache one store per tenant id), key annotations by tenant, and migrate the existing file into the tenant that first wrote it. Add a two-tenant test.
- Source: C5c-009 · prior audit: W2-76 (Sept 2026: ux_store pins to first tenant — still present at HEAD, now shown to leak annotations)

#### UX-003 · P0 · Trust · {{secret('NAME')}} resolves ANY environment variable of the Lightwork server — including its own AI-provider key — for any user who can edit and test a flow

- **Who / where:** IT/security, workspace admin, compliance · `Flow action params {{secret('…')}}`
- **User impact:** A workspace operator can read platform credentials (provider keys, cloud keys, signing secrets in env) through a Test run or send them to any URL in a real run — a cross-workspace credential exposure in multi-tenant deployments.
- **Evidence (reproduced):**
  - Same dry run as the previous finding: secret('OPENAI_COMPATIBLE_API_KEY') returned the platform's provider key 'lab-key'; secret('MAVERICK_CONFIG') returned the config path
  - packages/maverick-core/maverick/flow/runner.py:272-282 → secret_provider.get_secret(name) (secret_provider.py:121-132) = os.environ.get(name) with no allow-list or per-workspace scoping
  - Flow editing/testing needs only 'operate' (api.py flow endpoints use require_permission(request,'operate'))
- **Recommendation (effort M):** Restrict secret() to named connection credentials registered for the workspace (an explicit allow-list in Connections), never raw process env; audit every secret() resolution.
- Source: U4-018
- **Coordinator note:** Severity raised from P1 to P0 by the coordinator: Coordinator re-verified secret_provider.py:128-132 (any name falls back to os.environ; no allow-list or workspace scope). Chained with U4-017 (a Test run stores the resolved value in run data, reproduced with the provider key) any user with 'operate' can read platform secrets such as the model API key, across workspaces on a hosted deployment.

#### UX-004 · P0 · Trust · Stored XSS: a vendor name containing HTML runs script on the vendor detail page (reproduced in the live product)

- **Who / where:** compliance, workspace admin, IT/security · `POST /api/v1/vendors (Privacy > Vendors form) -> GET /privacy/vendors/{id}`
- **User impact:** Anyone who can add a vendor (operate role), or whoever produced an imported OneTrust CSV, can run script in the browser of the privacy officer or administrator who opens that vendor, acting with their session (approve, export, change settings). A compliance tool becomes the attack path.
- **Evidence (reproduced):**
  - Live lab: registered vendor via the Privacy > Vendors form with name 'Acme <img src=x onerror="document.title=\'XSS-FIRED\'">'; opening /privacy/vendors/VMR-355d97ab65626de44c8b8974 changed document.title to 'XSS-FIRED' (script executed). screenshot: shots/U6/vendor_02_detail.png (heading shows only 'Acme ')
  - packages/maverick-dashboard/maverick_dashboard/templates/vendor_detail.html:10-11 passes vendor.name / category into hero(); templates/_hero.html:31 renders {{ title | safe }} and :33 {{ lede | safe }}
  - Vendor names also arrive unreviewed from OneTrust CSV import (maverick-core/maverick/vendor_management.py:671-730) and AI vendor onboarding intake (vendor_onboarding.py:740-745)
  - Default CSP allows script-src 'unsafe-inline' (app.py:1483-1493 per map/13c D1)
  - [C5c-002] packages/maverick-dashboard/maverick_dashboard/templates/_hero.html:31 — {{ title | safe }}; :33 {{ lede | safe }}
  - [C5c-002] packages/maverick-dashboard/maverick_dashboard/templates/vendor_detail.html:10-11 — hero('Vendor', vendor.name, lede=(vendor.category|humanize ...))
  - [C5c-002] packages/maverick-dashboard/maverick_dashboard/api.py:2569-2578 — any 'operate' user can register a vendor; api_schemas.py:866-871 only length-checks name/category
  - [C5c-002] packages/maverick-dashboard/maverick_dashboard/app.py:1483-1493 — default CSP allows script-src 'unsafe-inline', so inline handlers execute
  - [C5c-002] cmd: audit/C5c_repro/r02_vendor_xss.py → POST /api/v1/vendors name='Acme<img src=x onerror=alert(document.cookie)>' → 201; GET /privacy/vendors/VMR-… renders '<h1 class="page-title hero-title" ...>Acme<img src=x onerror=alert(document.cookie)></h1>' and '<p class="hero-lede">Saas<svg onload=alert(1)>' unescaped (output: audit/C5c_repro/r02.out)
- **Recommendation (effort S):** Remove |safe from _hero.html title/lede (pass Markup explicitly only for server-built HTML), add a regression test that renders /privacy/vendors/{id} with markup in name and category, and tighten the page CSP (drop 'unsafe-inline').
- Source: U6-005, C5c-002 · prior audit: W3-72 (raised Sept 2026, map/13c D1 / MAP.md V6 (code-verified there, now reproduced live at HEAD), still present at HEAD 6daa3165 — now shown exploitable end-to-end)

#### UX-005 · P0 · Trust · Removing a workspace keeps its records AND its member roles; creating a new workspace with the same name silently inherits both (old tasks visible, former members become admins)

- **October 4 source fix (local verification):** Existing registry tombstones, namespace claims and suffix allocation already prevented a newly created workspace from adopting a removed workspace's ID and records. Removal now revokes its direct member roles, clears saved workspace selections and the local active selection; a failed cleanup leaves the tombstone in force and can be retried. The role read boundary also ignores any legacy orphaned memberships for removed IDs. The admin Workspaces page lists removed workspaces whose records remain on disk and offers an explicit, fresh-sign-in recovery. Recovery restores the same archived workspace as **paused**, with records intact and all former memberships still revoked; an administrator must review it and grant access again. If a new workspace took the old display name, recovery assigns a distinct visible name. A removed workspace whose records were erased or whose older tombstone lacks recovery metadata cannot be restored from this page. The erase-data flow still lacks a separate UI preview, and installed multi-worker acceptance remains open.
- **Who / where:** workspace admin, IT/security, compliance · `/tenants → Remove, then Create workspace (DELETE/POST /api/v1/admin/tenants)`
- **User impact:** An agency that offboards a client and later creates a workspace with the same name (a new client, or a re-onboarding under a new contract) exposes the old client's records and gives every former member — including removed contractors — access to the new workspace, contradicting the dialog's promise that no one can open it.
- **Evidence (reproduced):**
  - cmd: create 'Gamma Client' → select it → POST /api/v1/goals 'Gamma confidential salary review' (done) → PUT roles user:former-contractor@example.com=admin → DELETE /api/v1/admin/tenants/gamma-client (204, what the Remove button sends) → POST create 'Gamma Client' again → id 'gamma-client' → GET /api/v1/goals → 'GOAL 1 Gamma confidential salary review done'; GET /api/v1/admin/tenants/gamma-client/roles → {"user:former-contractor@example.com":"admin"}
  - packages/maverick-core/maverick/tenant/registry.py:620-638 delete_tenant only drops the roster row (purge=False from UI) and does not touch tenants/<id>/ data or dashboard-tenant-roles.json
  - packages/maverick-dashboard/maverick_dashboard/api.py:1016-1020 unique_slug only avoids ids in the current roster, so the removed id is reused
  - UI confirm text: 'Remove Gamma Client from the list? No one will be able to open it any more. Its stored records stay on this computer.'
- **Recommendation (effort M):** On remove: revoke all workspace memberships and selections, tombstone the id so it is never reused (unique_slug must check tombstones and existing tenants/<id> directories), and offer an explicit 'Restore removed workspace' list plus a separate 'Erase data' action with preview. Audit the removal.
- Source: U5-016

## P1 findings

#### UX-006 · P1 · Trust · Resolved: business setup cannot replace a guarded specialist with the same name

- **Who / where:** workspace admin, compliance, end user · `/agents` business specialist setup and the approved intake save path.
- **Current-source reconciliation:** `intake.generate_profile` assigns a distinct identity if a name matches a built-in, and `intake.save_profile` refuses a direct built-in identity or an existing custom file before writing. Business setup now checks the requested name against built-in and workspace specialists before starting a draft or spending on AI. The page states the conflict plainly and keeps the existing specialist and safeguards intact; an approval-time collision also returns a specific existing-name message.
- **Verification:** `test_business_setup_rejects_existing_specialist_names_before_drafting` checks the `HR Screening` risk/persona/tool envelope remains unchanged and an existing custom file is untouched. `test_direct_save_cannot_shadow_a_guarded_builtin` covers the direct kernel call. `business_agent_collision.test.js` checks the customer sees the conflict and no draft review opens.
- **Historical finding:** U3-037 reproduced a `HR Screening` setup that changed `hr_screening` from low risk with its regulated screening persona to medium risk with a generic persona. That reproduction predates the current guards and is no longer an open overwrite path.
- Source: U3-037.

#### UX-007 · P1 · Trust · The AWS deployer IAM user can grant itself administrator rights

- **October 4 source fix (local validation, not applied to AWS):** The deployer policy no longer grants any IAM user, role or policy mutation and explicitly denies role assumption. It can pass only the stack's two ECS task roles to ECS and its CodeBuild role to CodeBuild, with service-principal conditions. ECS writes are confined to the stack's cluster, service, task family and tasks. The same managed policy now serves as the user's permissions boundary, so another identity policy cannot expand its ordinary IAM permissions. `terraform fmt` and `terraform validate` pass. A separately privileged operator must apply this IAM change once; until AWS shows the new attached policy and boundary, existing credentials retain the old risk. Subsequent image, task and service deploys remain in the deployer's scope; IAM resource changes need that privileged operator.
- **Who / where:** IT/security · `deploy/aws/terraform/deployer.tf`
- **User impact:** Anyone holding the CI deployer credentials can rewrite its own policy or attach AdministratorAccess to itself and take over the AWS account — a much larger blast radius than the security team was told.
- **Evidence (code-verified):**
  - deploy/aws/terraform/deployer.tf:89-101 — iam:CreatePolicyVersion on policy/lightwork-prod-*, iam:AttachUserPolicy/PutRolePolicy/AttachRolePolicy on user|role/lightwork-prod-* with no iam:PolicyARN condition or permissions boundary
  - map 15 #4: its own policy is lightwork-prod-deployer and its user lightwork-prod-deployer (L8-9, 110-113); header claims 'no more' than the stack
- **Recommendation (effort M):** Add a permissions boundary required on all created roles/users, condition AttachUserPolicy/AttachRolePolicy on iam:PolicyARN in an allow-list, exclude the deployer's own user/policy from its resources, and scope ecs:* / PassRole.
- Source: C5c-125

#### UX-008 · P1 · Trust · A single future-dated consent event (e.g. year 2100) freezes that person's consent as 'granted' forever; later withdrawals are ignored

- **October 4 source fix:** New events more than five minutes in the future or with non-finite timestamps are refused in the shared `record_consent` boundary, including webhook/import callers. A later valid event recomputes the durable projection from eligible history, so a legacy future grant cannot pin it. Preference, posture and export readback also ignore legacy future events and return an unknown state if no valid event survives. Historical bad events remain in the audit history for review; a dedicated admin repair screen and installed CMP acceptance remain open. Local registry cases pass.
- **Who / where:** compliance, end user · `POST /consent/webhook, OneTrust consent import, consent_registry.record_consent`
- **User impact:** One bad timestamp from a CMP bug, a misparsed OneTrust date or a typo pins a data subject as consented permanently. When that person later withdraws, the withdrawal is written to history but the register (and anything that reads it) still says 'granted' — marketing keeps processing someone who opted out, and the privacy officer has no view that shows why.
- **Evidence (reproduced):**
  - packages/maverick-core/maverick/consent_registry.py:185-187 — only recorded_at <= 0 is rejected; no upper bound
  - packages/maverick-core/maverick/consent_registry.py:209-216 — projection keeps the event with the max recorded_at, so a later real event with an earlier timestamp never changes current_status
  - packages/maverick-core/maverick/consent_registry.py:694-704 — webhook uses the event's own recorded_at when present
  - cmd: audit/C5c_repro/r03_consent_webhook.py open → deliver {status:granted, recorded_at:4102444800} then {status:withdrawn} (now); subject_preferences → {"marketing":{"status":"granted","last_recorded_at":4102444800.0}} (output: audit/C5c_repro/r03.out)
- **Recommendation (effort S):** Reject or clamp recorded_at more than a small skew (e.g. 5 minutes) beyond server time in record_consent, the webhook and the OneTrust import; add a repair action that recomputes current_status from history ignoring future events, and flag affected subjects on the consent page.
- Source: C5c-004 · prior audit: W4-9 (raised Sept 2026, still present at HEAD)

#### UX-009 · P1 · Trust · Re-enrolling (editing) an external agent silently lifts its revocation and wipes its credentials

- **October 4 source fix:** External-agent re-enrollment now updates its reach while preserving existing credential bindings, pinned identity, revocation and lifecycle limits inside the trust registry's write lock. A revoked agent remains inactive after edit; a healthy agent's token remains valid. Focused trust/external-agent checks pass (160 cases). The in-product edit warning and installed external-agent acceptance remain open.
- **Who / where:** IT/security, workspace admin · `POST /api/v1/external-agents, POST /api/v1/trust/agents, maverick external-agents enroll`
- **User impact:** A security admin revokes a compromised agent; another admin later 'updates' its allowed tools by re-enrolling, and the agent shows as active again with no revocation history — the containment guard that protects the normal restore path is skipped. The same edit also silently invalidates every token a healthy agent is using, breaking it with no warning.
- **Evidence (reproduced):**
  - packages/maverick-core/maverick/external_agents.py:377-392 — enroll builds a fresh entry (no revoked/token/pubkey fields) and calls put_agent
  - packages/maverick-core/maverick/agent_trust.py:848-871 — put_agent replaces the whole managed entry
  - packages/maverick-dashboard/maverick_dashboard/api.py:12562-12577 — un-revoking via the revoke route is guarded by revocation.shared().run_if_unprotected; enroll bypasses that guard
  - cmd: audit/C5c_repro/r07_reenroll.py → token resolves before revoke: True; after revoke: revoked=True active=(False,'revoked'); after re-enroll with an extra tool: revoked=False active=(True,'active') a2a_token='' (output: audit/C5c_repro/r07.out)
- **Recommendation (effort S):** Make enroll an explicit create-or-update that preserves revoked, credential hashes, pubkey/JWT fields and lifecycle bounds; refuse to clear a revocation except through the guarded restore path; show 'This will keep the agent revoked' / 'Existing credentials stay valid' in the edit UI. Add a regression test for revoke → re-enroll.
- Source: C5c-008

#### UX-012 · P1 · Trust · Tasks routed to a specialist pack (domain) drop the requesting user's role and regulatory restrictions and run under the pack's own tool envelope

- **Current branch:** Closed in source before this pass. `Agent._resolve_capability` narrows every explicit pack grant by the run's ambient grant; for a depth-zero specialist it mints and retains the requester's grant first when enforcement is enabled. `agent_from_profile` also bounds a root pack by a caller-supplied `ctx.capability`. The actual tool boundary returns a customer-visible capability refusal without executing the tool. `test_domain_root_capability.py` covers low-risk ceilings, read-only roles, HIPAA outbound denial, explicit run grants, child inheritance and the refused write; all 10 local tests pass. The evidence below describes the older path.

- **User impact:** An admin restricts a user or channel (for example read-only, or max risk 'low', or a regulatory profile that forbids outbound actions). The same user starts a task through a specialist pack and the pack's tool list and risk ceiling apply instead, so actions the admin blocked for that person become available. Nothing on screen shows that the user's restrictions were dropped.

  - packages/maverick-core/maverick/agent.py:1812-1815 — _resolve_capability returns the explicit (pack) grant before ever looking at ctx.capability (the user's RBAC / regulatory attenuation)
  - Confirmed independently by the audit coordinator (MAP.md V3)
  - [C5b-066] packages/maverick-core/maverick/orchestrator.py:1950 — root = agent_from_profile(_profile, ctx, brief, depth=0) (parent=None)
  - [C5b-066] packages/maverick-core/maverick/domain.py:920-924 — parent_cap = getattr(None,'capability',None) → pack envelope minted alone (domain.py:637-645)
  - [C5b-066] packages/maverick-core/maverick/agent.py:1811-1812 — an explicit grant is returned before ctx.capability (the run's RBAC/regulatory grant) is consulted
  - [C5b-066] packages/maverick-core/maverick/regulatory_compiler.py:101,137,161 — HIPAA/SOC2 ATTENUATE deny_tools=_OUTBOUND (email, gmail, ses, sns, twilio, slack_bot, discord_bot)

  - [U3-038] packages/maverick-core/maverick/domain.py:919-924 — with no parent, parent_cap = None and domain_capability() mints the pack envelope alone
  - [U3-038] packages/maverick-core/maverick/agent.py:1809-1815 — an explicit capability wins; ctx.capability (the run's RBAC/regulatory grant) is only used when none is passed
  - [U3-038] packages/maverick-core/maverick/regulatory_compiler.py:101,137,161 — HIPAA and SOC 2 profiles ATTENUATE deny_tools=_OUTBOUND (email, gmail, ses, sns, twilio, slack_bot, discord_bot); domain.py:596-611 adds email/notify/calendar to pack envelopes when [workforce] levels is on

#### UX-013 · P1 · Trust · Coding-mode SEARCH/REPLACE apply runs `git worktree add` on the HOST against the agent's workdir without the git filter guard — a repo-local smudge filter executes on the host, escaping a container sandbox

- **Who / where:** IT/security, developer, workspace admin · `agent.py _extract_and_apply_patch (coding-mode FINAL with SEARCH/REPLACE blocks)`
- **User impact:** With a container sandbox the administrator believes model-written code cannot touch the host. In coding mode, anything that can write the workspace's .git/config inside the container (e.g. notebook_exec, which needs no approval) plants a smudge filter; when the agent's answer is applied, Lightwork itself runs that filter on the host as the service user, with the host environment. A prompt-injected coding task can therefore run commands outside the sandbox.
- **Evidence (code-verified):**
  - packages/maverick-core/maverick/agent.py:2279-2286 — host subprocess `git -c core.hooksPath=<tmp> -C <workdir> worktree add --detach ... HEAD` (only hooksPath overridden; no git_metadata_may_execute_filters check, no git_env_without_user_config)
  - packages/maverick-core/maverick/agent.py:2341-2346 — host `git worktree remove --force`; 2371-2384 host `reset --hard`/`clean -fd`; 2422-2431 host `git apply -` fallbacks likewise unguarded
  - packages/maverick-core/maverick/agent.py:4660-4661 — invoked for every coding-mode FINAL needing an apply check; has_exec is true for docker/local/ssh backends
  - coding_mode.py:2040-2052 and orchestrator.py:2850-2855 — the same checkout IS guarded there (fix for prior W2-4) but this sibling site was missed
  - cmd: scratchpad/audit/C5a/k4 — repo with `.gitattributes: * filter=pwn` and `.git/config filter.pwn.smudge="sh -c 'id > PWNED; cat'"`, then the exact argv `git -c core.hooksPath=<dir> -C repo worktree add --detach --quiet cand HEAD` → rc=0 and PWNED contains 'uid=0(root)': the filter ran on the host
- **Recommendation (effort M):** Route this site through the same hardening already used in coding_mode.evaluate_candidate: refuse when git_safety.git_metadata_may_execute_filters(workdir) is true, run with git_env_without_user_config() + scrub_env(), and add `-c core.fsmonitor=false -c filter.*` neutralisation; better, perform the worktree/apply inside the sandbox via sandbox.exec. Add a regression test with a planted smudge filter.
- Source: C5a-004 · prior audit: W2-4 (sibling site, the W2-1/W2-4 fix did not cover agent.py)

#### UX-017 · P1 · Trust · `maverick record verify` accepts a forged Operating Record capsule signed with any key (origin check is self-certifying)

- **Current-source reconciliation:** `verify_capsule` now checks an explicit trusted public key/keyring, defaulting to this installation's audit keyring, and CLI `record verify` accepts `--pubkey`/`--trusted-keys`. A forged capsule signed with an arbitrary key fails as untrusted; focused origin tests pass. The historical reproduction below predates this change. A verifier on another installation must receive the producer's trusted public key through an authenticated channel; a capsule alone cannot establish its own origin.

- **User impact:** An auditor or acquiring company handed a capsule ('the firm's decisions as a system of record') gets 'ok' for a capsule anyone fabricated or altered and re-signed. The tool gives a false assurance of provenance on exactly the artifact meant to prove what the company decided.

  - packages/maverick-core/maverick/operating_record.py:13-16 — docstring promises 'integrity and origin are verifiable offline'

- **Recommendation (effort S):** Require a trust anchor: `maverick record verify --pubkey <hex>|--trusted-keys <file>` (and default to the local audit keyring), fail with 'signed by an untrusted key' when the embedded key is not trusted, and print the key fingerprint prominently. #### UX-019 · P1 · Trust · A server-wide MAVERICK_KMS_KEY_ID silently overrides each workspace's own KMS key (BYOK)

- **Current-source reconciliation:** `tenant.kms.get_kms` reads the named workspace's own overlay key and passes it explicitly to the cloud KMS builder, ahead of the server-wide variable. `test_tenant_kms_fleet.py` covers tenant BYOK precedence, a workspace without its own key, and ambient-context isolation. The generic cloud builder still gives a server environment key precedence over the operator's global config key, which is intentional and separate from workspace BYOK. Showing the effective key identity on the Security page remains a product visibility gap; live cloud revocation has not been exercised here.
- **Who / where:** IT/security, compliance · `per-tenant [kms] key_id with cloud KMS (aws/gcp/vault)`
- **User impact:** An enterprise customer who configured their own KMS key (so they can revoke Lightwork's access) has their data keys wrapped with the operator's key instead whenever the operator also set the global variable. The customer's revocation right is silently void and nothing in the product shows which key is in use.
- **Evidence (reproduced):**
  - packages/maverick-core/maverick/kms_backends.py:71-72, 109-110, 147-148 — key_id = key_id or os.environ['MAVERICK_KMS_KEY_ID'] or cfg['key_id']
  - packages/maverick-core/maverick/tenant/kms.py:196-216 — get_kms passes the tenant's cfg 'so the backend uses THIS tenant's key_id'
  - cmd: MAVERICK_KMS_KEY_ID=...key/OPERATOR-GLOBAL; build_cloud_kms('aws', {'key_id': '...key/TENANT-BYOK', ...}).key_id → 'arn:aws:kms:us-east-1:111:key/OPERATOR-GLOBAL'
- **Recommendation (effort S):** Give per-tenant cfg['key_id'] precedence over the environment (env as fallback only when the tenant has none), and show the effective key id per workspace on the Security/Encryption page.
- Source: C5a-070

#### UX-020 · P1 · Trust · DSAR export files are kept forever in plaintext after the request is closed

- **Current branch:** New closes commit `closed` with a pending cleanup marker before touching the export, then remove only the current tenant/request's regular, single-link artifact whose embedded intent and digest match the request. The response and stored request expose `export_cleanup.status` (`removed` or `failed`) and a safe message; calling close again retries a failed or interrupted cleanup without repeating fulfillment. An orphan written just before an interrupted fulfillment is also removed when the request closes. Focused DSAR tests pass, including tampered-path/content refusal. Already-closed legacy requests still need a repeat close or a separate migration/sweep; there is no time-based retention purge yet.
- **Who / where:** compliance, IT/security · `DSAR fulfil / close in the Privacy workspace`
- **User impact:** Every access request leaves a complete copy of the person's data on disk indefinitely, outside at-rest encryption and outside retention — the opposite of data minimisation, and FEATURES.md's 'no second copy' claim does not cover this path.
- **Evidence (code-verified):**
  - packages/maverick-core/maverick/privacy_ops.py:2946-2976 — fulfill_dsar writes the subject's full export to data_dir('dsar_requests')/exports/<id>-export.json via atomic_write_text (plaintext)
  - packages/maverick-core/maverick/privacy_ops.py:3002-3021 — close_dsar does not delete it; no other core/dashboard code references that path (grep)
- **Recommendation (effort S):** Delete (or seal with at-rest encryption and a retention date) the export on close/after a configurable window ([privacy_ops] dsar_export_retention_days, Settings > Privacy), and include it in the retention purge.
- Source: C5c-032

#### UX-021 · P1 · Trust · REST goals have no spend or time cap by default, while docs/api.md promises '$2, 30min' defaults and a [0,100] clamp

- **Current branch:** REST goal admission now always supplies finite caps, including when a legacy installation has no general task limit: omitted requests use the configured limit or $2/30 minutes; explicit requests are narrowed by operator ceilings and an API maximum of $100/24 hours. The accepted goal body exposes exact `limits`, and keyed receipt recovery exposes the durable dispatch limits. Reviewed Copilot task-start previews use the same calculation. CLI/internal operator no-limit policy remains unchanged. Focused local REST and Copilot tests pass; installed deployment acceptance is still open.
- **Who / where:** developer, workspace admin, IT/security · `POST /api/v1/goals; docs/api.md`
- **User impact:** An integrator who trusts the API docs and omits max_dollars (or passes a typo like 1000) launches an uncapped, unbounded-duration run that can spend real provider money; nothing in the 201 response reveals the effective cap.
- **Evidence (reproduced):**
  - cmd: curl -X POST :8823/api/v1/goals -H 'Origin: http://127.0.0.1:8823' -d '{"title":"cap test","max_dollars":1000}' → HTTP 201 goal #4 (accepted, no clamp)
  - cmd (lab env): python3 -c 'from maverick.runner import configured_max_dollars,configured_max_wall_seconds; ...' → configured None None; budget_from_config() → max_dollars None, max_wall_seconds None
  - packages/maverick-core/maverick/runner.py:186-187 — DEFAULT_MAX_DOLLARS/DEFAULT_MAX_WALL_SECONDS = _optional_limit(env) → None unless MAVERICK_DEFAULT_MAX_* set
  - packages/maverick-dashboard/maverick_dashboard/api.py:1383-1385 — max_dollars = clamp_task_limit(payload.max_dollars, configured_max_dollars()) → unlimited when nothing configured
  - docs/api.md:43-45 — 'max_dollars clamped to [0, 100], max_wall_seconds to [1, 86400]'; docs/api.md:180-182 — 'defaults are conservative ($2, 30min)'
  - packages/maverick-dashboard/maverick_dashboard/api_schemas.py:164 — Field(ge=0.0) only; no upper bound
  - [C7-010] docs/api.md:180-182 — 'Always set explicit max_dollars and max_wall_seconds from external callers -- defaults are conservative ($2, 30min)'
  - [C7-010] docs/task-limits.md:3-5 — omitted limits remain unset across the CLI, dashboard, MCP ...
  - [C7-010] packages/maverick-core/maverick/budget.py:609-614 — all caps default None
  - [C7-010] prior audit W5-109 flagged '$2, 30min' vs code '$5, 3600s'; the SSE half was fixed but the defaults sentence was not, and is now wrong in a new way
- **Recommendation (effort S):** Either ship real defaults (e.g. [budget] max_dollars / max_wall_seconds written by the wizard and shown in Settings > Spending limits) or reject API goals without a cap when no deployment ceiling exists; return the effective caps in GoalOut (e.g. limits:{max_dollars,max_wall_seconds,max_depth}); correct docs/api.md.
- Source: C3-001, C7-010 · prior audit: W5-109 (partially fixed, W5-109 (still present, defaults now absent entirely, defaults sentence still wrong), not $5/1h as W5-109 recorded)

#### UX-022 · P1 · Trust · Flow tool calls formerly used a weaker text scan that let 'rm -rf /' through (source fix verified locally)

- **October 4 source reconciliation:** The flow action runner now calls `tool_authz.authorize(tool, params)` before effect. That shared gate invokes `shield_policy.scan_tool_call_block`, which passes the actual tool name and argument dictionary to `Shield.from_config().scan_tool_call`; the older text scan remains an additional floor. The real Shield still returns no block for `scan_block("shell {'cmd': 'rm -rf /'}")`, but returns `rm_rf_root` for `scan_tool_call_block("shell", {'cmd': 'rm -rf /'})`; an ordinary `read_file` call is allowed. Existing real-Shield regression tests cover destructive and nested arguments through `tool_authz`, and the dispatch-contract test catches a new ungated registry call. `Workflow.run` remains an in-process library API with no production caller; the dispatch contract guards that assumption. The cited A2A, federation and agent-bus calls are input screening of goal/message prose, not direct tool dispatch. Their default execution paths enter the orchestrator, whose `Agent._run_tool` calls `scan_tool_call` on the eventual tool and its arguments. The dashboard security API call cited below screens telemetry and rules, not a tool invocation. Those text surfaces should not classify every mention of a dangerous command as an attempted tool call.
- **Verification limit:** `test_shield_policy.py` and `test_tool_authz.py` passed locally (52 tests). Installed A2A/federation/agent-bus journeys and the external agent-shield SDK were not exercised; the local Shield used its built-in rules. The optional shield can still be disabled by operator configuration on non-required installations.
- **Who / where:** IT/security, workspace admin, developer · `flow/workflow tool steps (tool_authz), A2A tasks, federation inbound, agent bus, dashboard security API`
- **Original user impact:** A destructive command in a flow action could pass a repr-based text scan even though the agent tool-call scan would block it. This direct-dispatch gap is closed in the current source; A2A, federation and agent-bus messages still require separate installed-path verification.
- **Historical evidence (the direct-dispatch call site has since changed):**
  - packages/maverick-core/maverick/tool_authz.py:103-105 — payload = f"{tool} {params}" (Python repr) → shield_policy.scan_block
  - packages/maverick-core/maverick/shield_policy.py:80 — Shield().scan_input(text), i.e. prompt-injection input rules, not tool-call rules
  - packages/maverick-shield/maverick_shield/guard.py:405-417 — documents this repr-quoting bypass for scan_input
  - cmd: shield_policy.scan_block("shell {'cmd': 'rm -rf /'}") → None (allowed); Shield().scan_tool_call('shell', {'cmd': 'rm -rf /'}) → BLOCKED (rule rm_rf_root). Also confirmed by the audit coordinator (MAP.md V2)
- **Recommendation status:** Superseded for direct flow tool calls by the shared gate and real-Shield tests above. Keep ingress text screening on message surfaces and verify their downstream agent tool gate in an installed integration environment.
- Source: C5a-038

#### UX-024 · P1 · Trust · Browser sessions previously crossed users, goals and workspaces (source fix verified locally)

- **October 4 source fix:** Browser contexts are keyed by workspace, principal and goal; the optional `browser` and `aria_navigate` tools use one dedicated worker thread per scope, preserving Playwright's thread affinity across actions. The ARIA node ledger is scoped too. The goal-finally path closes every scoped context on its worker, including failed or cancelled goals. Goal-scoped use cannot load or save the server-wide `MAVERICK_BROWSER_STATE` file, and its agent file-access gate no longer treats that file as an active sink. Standalone local use keeps the explicit opt-in persistence behavior.

The production optional-tool registration selects the managed worker path. The focused browser suite passed locally (51 tests). Playwright itself is not installed here, so a real Chromium cookie/login acceptance run remains open.
- **Who / where:** IT/security, end user, workspace admin · `[capabilities] browser = true (opt-in) in the multi-user dashboard / serve process`
- **Historical user impact:** A logged-in page could remain open for the next user's task and expose its cookies or content. The former module-global session is removed in the current source.

  - packages/maverick-core/maverick/tools/browser.py:14-16 — docstring 'Closed at the end of the goal via close_browser()'

  - packages/maverick-core/maverick/agent.py:1989 — enabled via [capabilities] browser
- **Recommendation status:** Implemented in source; run an installed Chromium test with two authenticated goals before calling the browser journey customer-ready.

#### UX-025 · P1 · Trust · Shell commands require a person's approval, but notebook_exec (on by default) runs arbitrary model-written Python in the same workspace with no approval at all

- **Who / where:** IT/security, workspace admin, compliance · `tools notebook_exec (default), code_exec, wasm_run, git_advanced, sql_query read_only=false, lsp_bridge`
- **User impact:** Security admins see that 'Run a command' needs human approval and assume model-authored code cannot run unreviewed. In practice the assistant can write a notebook file and execute it — with full Python, subprocess and network access available to the sandbox — without anyone being asked. The approval on shell gives a false sense of control; with the default local backend this is code on the host.
- **Evidence (reproduced):**
  - packages/maverick-core/maverick/tools/shell.py:309-340 — shell asks a person for every command
  - packages/maverick-core/maverick/tools/notebook_exec.py:64-86 — concatenates code cells and runs `python -` via sandbox_run with no consent call; registered by default at tools/__init__.py:1436-1439
  - tools/code_exec.py:122-126, wasm_run.py:104, git_advanced.py:52-64,140-160, sql_query.py:200-201, lsp_bridge.py:81-88 — same pattern (no consent gate)
  - cmd: MAVERICK_REHEARSAL=0, scripted task: write_file report.ipynb (cell imports os/subprocess, writes NB_RAN.txt) then notebook_exec → 'exit_code: 0 stdout: notebook code ran as uid 0' and NB_RAN.txt created in the workspace; the shell call in the same run was refused for lack of approval (out_d4.txt)
- **Recommendation (effort M):** Apply one policy to all code-execution tools: route notebook_exec, code_exec, wasm_run, git_advanced mutating ops, sql_query read_only=false and lsp_bridge through the same require_operation_consent (or the same admin-configurable execution policy as shell). Show in Settings > Safety a single 'Running code' control that lists every tool it covers.
- **Implementation update (2026-10-04):** The notebook path had already gained one-use exact-operation consent. `code_exec`, WebAssembly runs, Git mutations, write-enabled SQLite statements and host language-server launches now use a shared fresh-consent adapter. It binds the reviewed inputs, execution target, timeout and relevant file versions, denies silent/standing approval, and rechecks the permit at execution. `code_exec` asks before its declared tool calls; those calls still use their own safety path. Settings now explains the coverage and links to Approvals. Read-only database queries, Git inspection and the WebAssembly version probe remain ungated. Focused local tests cover each denied boundary, the shared policy in automatic modes, existing execution behavior, and lint. A live installed dashboard approval walkthrough remains unverified; this is source-level closure, not a production acceptance claim.
- Source: C5a-014

#### UX-033 · P1 · Bug · Importing an n8n workflow that fans out to several actions keeps only the first branch; the others become unreachable, yet the import report marks every step 'preserved' (D10)

  - [C5c-015] packages/maverick-core/maverick/consent_preferences.py:2568-2577 — record_preferences raises 'preference receipts cannot manufacture non-consent authority' for any purpose whose basis is not 'consent'
  - [C5c-015] packages/maverick-dashboard/maverick_dashboard/consent_public_api.py:3207-3218 — published purposes must carry the policy's lawful bases, so contract/legitimate_interests purposes are always present in the list when configured

#### UX-043 · P1 · Bug · Tasks given to a department-deployed specialist on Fleets run as a generic orchestrator: the specialist's persona, playbook and deliverable contract are never applied

- **October 4 resolution:** Current `run_fleet_agent` rejects a disabled or missing specialist pack and stamps the goal with `agent.domain`; the orchestrator builds the root through `agent_from_profile`, which supplies the specialist's persona, playbook, refusals and output contract under its attenuated capability. A local request-to-run check deployed the Sales & GTM department, assigned a ready Deal Inspection specialist, and confirmed its persona reached the model stand-in, its goal retained the pack domain, and its run principal and shell denial survived dispatch. The earlier generic-orchestrator reproduction is historical.
- **Related readiness correction:** The department API previously allowed deployment if *any* specialist passed setup checks, but saved the entire roster, including specialists whose required actions were unavailable. It now saves only `action_ready` specialists and returns deployed/skipped counts with a user-facing setup reason and recovery link for each skipped specialist. The Workforce page shows the count held back. Departments with no verified-ready specialists receive a 409 before a fleet is saved. Runtime still checks the pack and capabilities again when work starts, because setup can change after deployment.
- **Verification:** `test_fleet_dispatch.py` deployed a real department and reached a fake local model with the named specialist's persona and restricted tools (2 focused deploy checks passed); `test_workforce.py` verified mixed-readiness persistence, truthful skipped reasons, all-ready behavior and no-ready refusal (9 focused checks passed). Ruff passed. No external provider output was assessed. In the local default setup, Commerce has no verified-ready specialist and correctly needs setup before deployment.
- **Who / where:** end user, workspace admin · `/workforce 'Deploy team' -> /fleets 'Give it to … / Start task' -> POST /api/v1/fleets/{fleet}/run`
- **Historical user impact:** An administrator deployed 'Commerce' and handed work to 'Merchant Analytics'; an earlier revision ran an unbriefed generic agent wearing that name.
- **Historical evidence (reproduced before domain binding):**
  - cmd: POST /api/v1/departments/commerce/deploy -> fleet dept-commerce (11 agents, domain=pack); POST /api/v1/fleets/dept-commerce/run {agent: com_merch_analytics, prompt: 'Summarise last week sales trends…'} -> goal 7 done
  - logs/llm.jsonl for goal 7: system prompt starts 'You are the orchestrator of a Lightwork swarm'; neither 'Merchant Analytics' nor 'merchandis' appears anywhere in it (the pack persona begins 'You are the Merchant Analytics specialist…', domains/com_merch_analytics.toml:5)
  - packages/maverick-dashboard/maverick_dashboard/api.py:13635-13656 — run_fleet_agent only narrows the capability with domain_capability(); w.create_goal(...) is called without set_goal_domain, so orchestrator.py never builds the root via agent_from_profile
  - contrast: POST /api/v1/goals with domain=cx_triage (api.py:1367-1375, 1415) does inject the persona (llm.jsonl contained the cx_triage persona)
- **Remaining scope:** Real provider responses and live external sources remain unverified; setup changes after deploy can make a specialist unavailable, in which case runtime refuses the run rather than using a generic agent.

#### UX-048 · P1 · Bug · After the first task in a new workspace, the default-on 'rehearsal' gate refuses every high-risk tool (write_file, shell, http_fetch, browser, spawn_subagent, connectors) with jargon and no approval path — and then learns from its own refusals to block them

- **Who / where:** end user, evaluator, workspace admin · `every agent tool call (agent.py _rehearsal_denial); [rehearsal] enable (default = governed_learning_default() = True)`
- **User impact:** A new customer's first task works; from the next task onward the assistant can no longer save a file, run a command, fetch a web page, use the browser, delegate to a specialist or call a connector. The task still finishes as 'done' and the only explanation is 'Held by pre-execution rehearsal ... world-model has no support for this action in this state ... seek approval' — but no approval request exists and nothing tells the admin that a learning feature is doing this. Because refused attempts are recorded as failed experience, the gate can go on to block the same tools 'confidently'.
- **Evidence (reproduced):**
  - packages/maverick-core/maverick/config.py:2892-2917 — [rehearsal] enable defaults to governed_learning_default() (True at HEAD, printed by `python3 -c 'from maverick.config import governed_learning_default; print(governed_learning_default())'` → True); min_support=5
  - packages/maverick-core/maverick/agent.py:3892-3935 — any tool whose tool_risk is 'high' is refused unless the fitted world-model vouches: '⚠ Held by pre-execution rehearsal ({decision}): {reason}. The tool was not executed; choose another approach or seek approval.' — no approval is actually requested
  - tool_risk at HEAD: write_file, shell, notebook_exec, apply_patch, http_fetch, browser, spawn_subagent, database, salesforce = 'high'
  - packages/maverick-core/maverick/rehearsal_runtime.py:55-85 — the model is fitted from the trajectory store, which records held (never-executed) attempts as steps of that tool
  - cmd: scratchpad/audit/C5a/tools/run_script.py (scripted fake model calling write_file/notebook_exec/shell) in a fresh MAVERICK_HOME: task 1 → write_file ran; tasks 2-9 → every call returned '⚠ Held by pre-execution rehearsal (escalate): world-model has no support for this action in this state' (out_rehearsal.txt); a new process then returned 'Held ... (block): rehearsal predicts a poor outcome (0.056 < floor 0.500)' with trajectory Counter shell=9 (all refused attempts). The 0.056 outcome partly reflects the lab verifier scoring low; the 'escalate' holds do not depend on it
- **Recommendation (effort M):** Ship rehearsal in observe-only mode until a workspace has real support (log the verdict, never hold), or map ESCALATE to a real approval request via require_consent with a readable reason. Never record a held tool call as an executed step in the trajectory store. Surface the switch on Settings > Safety with plain copy ('Hold unfamiliar high-impact actions for review'), and show held actions on the task page with a one-click 'approve and run'.
- **Implementation update (2026-10-03):** Rehearsal now defaults to watch-only predictions. Settings > Safety exposes its switch and mode; Shield, capability, and consent checks still decide their own refusals. Calls stopped before dispatch are excluded from executed action history and trajectory scoring, and ambiguous older failed rows are excluded from rehearsal fitting. Explicit Hold mode now requests a fresh person in Approvals for one exact task/tool/argument set, then checks the live permit before allowing the normal safety gates to continue. Rejection, timeout, unavailable authority, unavailable prediction and stale approval stop the action; an unanswered request is withdrawn. The native page has a synthetic authenticated browser journey, but the actual installed task-to-approval-to-execution journey and inline task review control remain open.
- Source: C5a-010

#### UX-049 · P1 · Bug · Historical: distilled skills were stored as proposals but never entered later-run recall

- **October 4 reconciliation:** Current source deliberately keeps raw `learned-skills/` proposals out of agent recall. `skills.admit_learned_skill` requires administrator review of exact bytes, current shared-source lineage, validation and the learning stop before admission into the installed-skill recall path. Learned page and Copilot expose that review path. The old suggestion to recall raw proposals automatically would bypass this governance. A real after-admission use/outcome journey remains unqualified.
- **October 4 verification:** The current guarded path is wired through `available_skills()` → `apply_skill_overlays()` → `Agent._build_system()`, which records both name and exact-version use counters. Existing focused tests exercise proposal creation, explicit admission, next-prompt recall, use count, withdrawal, and refusal of private-source proposals. No runtime bypass was added. The stale distiller, CLI and Learned-page descriptions now distinguish a suggestion from a skill available for recall. This verifies source behavior and a synthetic next-agent prompt, not a live installed task-to-review-to-outcome result or causal improvement.
- **Who / where:** end user, workspace admin, evaluator, compliance · `Every goal run (agent skill recall); dreaming; orchestrator per-run distillation`
- **User impact (original finding):** Learning produced suggestions but no route for those suggestions to reach later-run recall, so calling a suggestion an active improvement was misleading. Current source adds explicit review and admission; use counts measure recall, not improvement caused by the skill.

  - cmd: python3 repro_learned_skill.py → 'distilled skill written to: learned-skills/quarterly-vendor-report.md'; 'runtime recall sees it: False (514 skills available)'; 'user skills dir used by recall: skills'
  - README.md:20 — 'A workforce that provably improves ... skill distillation'; docs/FEATURES.md:217-224 and skill/distillation_local.py:7 — '... so it's picked up on later runs'

  - [C5a-087] packages/maverick-core/maverick/skill/distillation_local.py:23, 167-168 — store = data_dir('learned-skills')
  - [C5a-087] packages/maverick-core/maverick/skills.py:40-48, 308-337 — available_skills() reads built-in skills + skills_dir() = data_dir('skills') only
  - [C5a-087] Confirmed independently by the audit coordinator (MAP.md V1)

  - [C7-013] docs/getting-started.md:139 — 'maverick skills # what the swarm distilled from this run'
  - [C7-013] packages/maverick-core/maverick/orchestrator.py:2529-2556 — default-on local distillation writes 'a reusable SKILL.md under ~/.maverick/learned-skills'

  - [C7-013] packages/maverick-core/maverick/cli/__init__.py:5035-5050 — `skills` command lists available_skills(), i.e. the 514 builtin + ~/.maverick/skills; empty-state text 'no skills yet (in <builtin> or ~/.maverick/skills)'

#### UX-052 · P1 · Resolved for in-product alerts · Task owners need reliable notice when work finishes, fails, or needs an answer

- **Current branch (2026-10-04):** Goal creation enrolls a current named owner.
  The owner-scoped inbox projects completed, failed, blocked and open-question
  states; the shared navigation bell polls a count while the page is visible.
  The dashboard's bounded observer refreshes enrolled owners while pages are
  closed when background alerts are enabled. Copilot can read the same inbox.
  Personal preferences, current membership, quiet hours, digest timing and
  per-event choices govern what appears. The API, new-owner enrollment and
  background observer now all stop when personal preferences are disabled,
  matching the unavailable page and hidden bell.
- **Verified locally:** A signed-in owner completes one task and gets a question
  on another before opening the inbox; background observation records both,
  and the owner sees separate notices with authenticated task links. A second
  owner's work is excluded. Focused dashboard and delivery checks passed.
- **Private delivery limit:** Slack/Telegram delivery additionally requires
  background observation, an HTTPS dashboard origin, a verified My Data identity,
  bot/channel allowlists and the owner's explicit destination choice. The inbox
  now explains when My Data identity linking is disabled. Provider acceptance
  is recorded separately from whether the person read the message. Existing
  installs must enable personal alerts; external delivery remains opt-in.
- **Historical reproduction:** In the earlier lab run, a working organization
  ntfy self-test received zero notices for finished/failed/question-waiting
  tasks. That shared ntfy channel remains for organization operations and is
  deliberately not a destination for private task content. The prior settings
  label implied otherwise; the present installer separates shared alerts from
  personal task alerts.
- **Installer prerequisite (2026-10-04):** If private Slack/Telegram delivery is
  selected while My Data is off, setup now asks explicitly whether to turn on
  identity linking. Declining keeps private delivery off and leaves in-product
  alerts available; accepting writes the needed My Data feature switch. Both
  choices passed focused installer checks. Live provider delivery remains open.
- Source: U8-026; `test_personal_notification_badge_journey.py`,
  `test_personal_notification_scheduler.py`, `test_personal_notification_delivery.py`

#### UX-053 · P1 · Bug · Breach-notification plan reads '1.2k customers' as 12 people and tells the officer the incident is below California's and Japan's reporting thresholds

- **Current branch (2026-10-03):** The incident form and API accept a numeric
  affected-person count. Legacy free text is parsed only when unambiguous;
  otherwise the count remains unknown and the notification plan does not assert
  a threshold outcome. Focused privacy, notification, and UI checks passed.

- **Who / where:** compliance · `GET /api/v1/privacy/incidents/{id}/notification-plan (Privacy workspace incident page)`
- **User impact:** A privacy officer relying on the plan during the 72-hour clock can be told a 1,200-person breach is below the regulator's threshold (under-notification risk) or that a 300-person breach is over it. Ranges like '1,000-5,000' become 10,005,000. The input box gives no hint that only a plain integer is understood.
- **Evidence (reproduced):**
  - packages/maverick-dashboard/maverick_dashboard/api.py:2986-2990 — subjects_affected = int(''.join(every digit in the free-text affected_estimate))
  - packages/maverick-core/maverick/privacy_ops.py:3048 — affected_estimate is free text (100 chars) typed by the reporter
  - packages/maverick-core/maverick/breach_notification.py:535-565 — the parsed count drives authority_below_threshold and the threshold_note
  - cmd: audit/C5c_repro/r04_breach_count.py → incident affected_estimate '1.2k customers' → plan us_ca below=True note='Reported subject count (12) is below this regulator's 501-subject trigger'; '~300 (0.5% of base)' parses as 30005 → no threshold notes (output: audit/C5c_repro/r04.out)
- **Recommendation (effort S):** Add a numeric 'people affected (best estimate)' field to the incident form (with optional low/high), keep the free-text note separate, and have the plan use the number or say 'count not provided' instead of guessing. Never concatenate digits; if parsing text, accept only a single integer with separators and otherwise refuse.

#### UX-057 · P1 · Bug · Database connectors refuse every query — even SELECT 1 — and many ordinary connector actions (HubSpot contact_create, Trello card_create, Salesforce update, Jira transition …) are refused outright

- **Current branch (2026-10-03):** A constant `SELECT 1` still runs directly.
  Customer SQL, GraphQL mutations, and connector changes without an atomic
  revision contract now reach the existing fresh human approval and durable
  prepare/commit path. The review warns when no ETag was supplied, without
  assuming the service lacks one, and generic REST updates without `if_match` are
  accepted only inside that exact approved request; direct calls still refuse.
  A real SQLite customer-table read through the governed registry passed with
  human approval. This does not make all SQL safely read-only or qualify every
  provider and connector operation; live customer endpoints, scopes, result
  readback, and the full UI approval journey remain to be validated.

- **Who / where:** end user, workspace admin, evaluator, developer · `tools database, snowflake, bigquery, oracle, databricks and ~40 bespoke connector write ops; all GraphQL mutations; REST PUT/PATCH/DELETE without if_match`
- **User impact:** A customer connects their Postgres or Snowflake warehouse and asks a simple question; the assistant cannot run any query and reports an ETag/revision error that means nothing to them. Adding a HubSpot contact, creating a Trello card or GitLab issue, resolving a PagerDuty incident and dozens of other advertised actions are likewise impossible, while the product markets 2,877 write-capable connectors.
- **Evidence (reproduced):**
  - packages/maverick-core/maverick/governed_tools.py:374-385 — any SQL connector, GraphQL tool, or op not in _REVISION_EXEMPT_OPS (governed_tools.py:44-53) raises 'this connector does not declare an atomic revision/ETag contract'
  - packages/maverick-core/maverick/governed_tools.py:828-831 — governance_enabled() always True
  - packages/maverick-core/maverick/tools/database_tool.py:1-6 — tool description still says 'Simple read statements run directly'
  - cmd: scratchpad/audit/C5a/tools (out_d2.txt) — base_registry(...) with dummy creds: database {op:query, sql:'SELECT 1'} → 'REFUSED (governed): a fresh read and atomic remote revision precondition are required for target \'query\' (this connector does not declare an atomic revision/ETag contract); no external write was attempted.' Same for snowflake query, hubspot contact_create, trello card_create
  - naming asymmetry: create/task_create/page_create/comment are exempt but contact_create/card_create/issue_create/issue_comment are refused (map/03t D2)
  - [C3-038] packages/maverick-core/maverick/tools/enterprise_connectors.py:1-7 — 'writes are confirm-gated'; tools/_rest_connector.py:271-272 — 'DRY RUN: would {op} … Re-run with confirm=true.'
  - [C3-038] packages/maverick-core/maverick/governed_tools.py:579-600 — governed writes bypass the tool's own confirm/DRY RUN; without a revision contract returns 'REFUSED (governed): a fresh read and atomic remote revision precondition are required … no external write was attempted.'
  - [C3-038] governed_tools.py:44-53 — _REVISION_EXEMPT_OPS allows create/task_create/page_create/comment but not contact_create/card_create/issue_create/issue_comment (map/03t D2 naming asymmetry)
  - [C3-038] map/03t D2 (static simulation): database/snowflake/bigquery query, salesforce record_update/delete, hubspot contact_create/update, servicenow update/delete, jira transition, linear update_status, gitlab issue_create/comment, every GraphQL mutation … always refused
- **Recommendation (effort L):** Classify SQL by statement (read-only SELECT via sql_safety → run without the write contract; writes → human approval) and treat create/append/one-shot ops by semantics, not name (contact_create, card_create, issue_create, *_comment). Where compare-and-set is impossible, allow a human-approved write with an explicit 'no concurrency protection' note instead of refusing. Replace the refusal text with plain language. Add a matrix test over every connector op.
- Source: C5a-053, C3-038

#### UX-060 · P1 · Reliability · After a crash and quick restart, a running chat stays 'Working…' forever: orphan recovery only runs at startup and skips goals updated in the last 60 s

- **Current branch (code review, 2026-10-03):** The dashboard now starts a

#### UX-062 · P1 · Reliability · After 2,048 knowledge rights requests, every knowledge read and search in that workspace is permanently denied

- **Current branch (2026-10-04):** Normal submission stops at the 2,048 active-record limit; reads stay available at that limit. For a legacy or externally overfilled local ledger, the administrator's Ready to archive view now scans bounded pages of request IDs beyond the old first-2,048 window and shows only requests that pass the existing finished-request checks. Each archive still requires a separate revision-bound, audited action; source restrictions and evidence remain retained. A focused overfill test confirmed reads fail closed before recovery and resume after archiving one later finished request. Focused core/API tests and 28 knowledge-page JS tests passed. Shared storage still refuses the two-store archive protocol, and installed acceptance remains open.

- **Who / where:** end user, compliance, workspace admin · `Knowledge search, read, export, jobs (knowledge_search tool and dashboard library)`
- **User impact:** Once a workspace accumulates 2,048 correction/deletion requests over its lifetime, the AI can no longer read any knowledge source and users get an unintelligible 'request boundary' error; there is no admin action to recover.
- **Evidence (code-verified):**
  - packages/maverick-core/maverick/knowledge_access.py:56 — _MAX_REQUESTS = 2_048
  - packages/maverick-core/maverick/knowledge_access.py:440-446 — if the request store holds >= 2,048 rows, raise KnowledgeAccessDenied('knowledge retirement authority cannot be resolved within its request boundary')
  - packages/maverick-core/maverick/knowledge_access.py:457-467 — _admission (every read) calls this check

  - [C5c-030] packages/maverick-core/maverick/privacy_rights_orchestration.py:103 — verify_delete is a required erasure phase

#### UX-066 · P1 · Ux · AI provider failure is shown as 'Lightwork stopped — internal error' with status 'Paused': no cause, no remedy

  - [U8-019] templates/chat_goal.html:478-481 halt card shows goal.result verbatim in #halt-reason
  - [U8-019] docs/customer-experience-contract.md:37-42 (no stack traces/serialized objects; translate status codes into meaningful states)

  - [C5a-027] cmd: fake model server stopped, task via run_goal_in_thread → log 'LLM call failed (attempt 1/3): APIConnectionError ... openai.APIConnectionError: Connection error.' then RESULT returned='error' status='blocked' result='internal error'

Try again in a few minutes' / 'The AI connection needs attention — ask an admin to check Settings › AI connection' with a link for admins). Use a 'failed' status (Stopped) rather than 'blocked' for crashes, and post an error step in the work log.

#### UX-067 · P1 · Ux · Default (no-token) install rejects every scripted API write with a misleading 'Reload the dashboard' 403; docs/api.md says 'no auth' and its template example fails

- **Current branch (2026-10-03):** A local API write without browser headers
  now explains the exact same-origin header or in-product API-key path. The
  REST guide and local request example use a matching Origin. The CSRF gate
  still refuses a forged browser Origin. Focused security checks passed.

- **Who / where:** developer, evaluator · `POST /api/v1/goals (any mutating /api/v1 route) in loopback no-token mode`
- **User impact:** An evaluator following the REST docs on a fresh install gets a 403 telling them to reload a browser page they are not using; the real remedy (set a server access token and send a Bearer header, or add an Origin header) is documented nowhere.
- **Evidence (reproduced):**
  - cmd: curl -X POST http://127.0.0.1:8823/api/v1/goals -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"title":"Quarterly report [ask]"}' → HTTP 403 {"detail":"cross-site request blocked — for your security, changes must be made from the Lightwork page itself. Reload the dashboard and try again."}
  - same request + -H 'Origin: http://127.0.0.1:8823' → HTTP 201 (so the only workaround is spoofing a browser Origin header)
  - packages/maverick-dashboard/maverick_dashboard/app.py:2196-2217 — loopback no-token branch requires _is_same_origin for unsafe methods
  - docs/api.md:8 — 'By default, no auth -- the server binds to 127.0.0.1 only.'; docs/api.md:139-146 — template example has no Authorization/Origin header and would 403
- **Recommendation (effort S):** Make the 403 detail API-aware (when the request has no Origin/Referer, say: 'API clients need a server access token: Settings > All settings > Server access token, then send Authorization: Bearer …'); document the CSRF rule and token setup in docs/api.md 'Auth'; add a 'Create API token' action to Settings > Access.

#### UX-074 · P1 · Customization · Azure OpenAI and AWS Bedrock cannot be set up in the product: Settings > Provider keys offers only 9 providers, while the kernel supports 14
