#### UX-191 · P2 · Bug · 'Run another flow' whose target contains an approval passes validation, then the parent run is 'Rejected' instantly and the child's approval is never requested (D2)

- **Who / where:** workspace admin · `Run another flow step; POST /api/v1/flows/{id}/run`
- **User impact:** Reusing an approval sub-process — a core pattern in Power Automate child flows — silently fails as 'Rejected' on every run.
- **Evidence (reproduced):**
  - d1.py: child d2-child-b (approval → setvar) published; parent d2-parent-b (subflow → d2-child-b) save 201, publish 200, run db53adf5… → 'rejected', cursor 'a', error ''
  - screenshot: shots/U4/rej_d2.png — 'Run another flow · Not reached', no reason shown
  - packages/maverick-core/maverick/flow/runner.py:1042-1082 child runs ctx.nested() (cannot pause); ir.py:597-598 never inspects the referenced child
  - [C5b-029] packages/maverick-core/maverick/flow/runner.py:1042-1082 — subflow runs with ctx.nested() (cannot pause)
  - [C5b-029] packages/maverick-core/maverick/flow/ir.py:597-598 — Flow.validate never inspects the referenced child
  - [C5b-029] packages/maverick-core/maverick/flow/runner.py:1484-1487 — nested delay is a no-op
  - [C5b-029] cmd: python3 repro_flow.py → parent(subflow→child with approval): validate() = []; run status=rejected error=''
- **Recommendation (effort M):** Either support pausing inside subflows (propagate the pause to the parent run) or refuse at save/publish: 'The flow “D2 child” asks for approval, which can't happen inside Run another flow yet'. Explain rejections caused by engine limits distinctly from human rejections.
- Source: U4-025, C5b-029

#### UX-192 · P2 · Bug · No check anywhere for steps that can never run (unreachable from the first step): client and server validation accept orphaned steps

- **Current branch (2026-10-04):** The flow editor identifies and explains unreachable steps; publication checks the saved graph server-side before activation. Drafts may retain disconnected work for editing. The canvas dims those steps and names the issue for assistive technology. Existing published releases are not retroactively changed.

- **Who / where:** workspace admin, developer · `/flows/designer Save/Publish; POST /api/v1/flows; flow/ir.py Flow.validate`
- **User impact:** Steps that are disconnected by editing (delete a connector, add after a decision, import) stay in the flow looking live but never execute; nothing tells the builder.
- **Evidence (code-verified):**
  - packages/maverick-dashboard/maverick_dashboard/templates/flow_designer_core.js:152-189 — validateFlow checks start, dangling refs, required fields; no reachability check
  - grep -n -i 'unreachable\|reachab\|orphan' packages/maverick-core/maverick/flow/ir.py packages/maverick-core/maverick/flow/runner.py → 0 hits
  - Reproduced consequence: invoice-approval flow with 2 orphaned steps saved and published with no warning (build1.out)
- **Recommendation (effort S):** Add a reachability pass to Flow.validate (warning on save, error on publish) and to FDCore.plainProblems ('The step “Approval” can never run — connect it from an earlier step'), and dim unreachable nodes on the canvas.
- Source: U4-002

#### UX-193 · P2 · Bug · 'Wait for another app' inside a Repeat-for-each passes Save and Publish, then every run ends 'Rejected' with no reason (D1)

- **Current branch (2026-10-04):** Client and server authoring checks now refuse a nested event wait with a plain instruction to move it into the main flow. If an existing release still reaches this runtime path, it fails with that reason instead of reporting a human rejection. A live installed migration journey has not been run.

- **Who / where:** workspace admin · `POST /api/v1/flows, /publish, /run; run page`
- **User impact:** The flow looks valid, then every run appears to have been 'Rejected' (as if a person said no); the admin has no clue the loop is the cause.
- **Evidence (reproduced):**
  - d1.py: flow d1-loop-wait-b (foreach body = wait_event) → save 201, publish 200, run 00bfde60… → status 'rejected', error ''
  - screenshot: shots/U4/rej_d1.png — header 'Rejected', steps 'Update data Done · Repeat for each item Not reached', no explanation
  - packages/maverick-core/maverick/flow/ir.py:825-845 _pause_node_errors flags nested approval/delay only; runner.py:1282-1293 rejects a nested wait_event at run time
  - Contrast: nested delay IS refused at save: 'delay node 'd' can't wait inside a loop/branch' (d1.py first run)
  - [C5b-028] packages/maverick-core/maverick/flow/ir.py:825-845 — _pause_node_errors flags nested approval/delay but not NODE_WAIT
  - [C5b-028] packages/maverick-core/maverick/flow/runner.py:1282-1293 — nested wait_event raises _Reject
  - [C5b-028] cmd: python3 repro_flow.py → nested wait_event: validate() errors = []; run status=rejected error='' (nested approval/delay both produce validation errors)
- **Recommendation (effort S):** Add wait_event to _pause_node_errors (same plain message as delay) and, at run time, record a human-readable reason instead of an empty rejection.
- Source: U4-024, C5b-028

#### UX-241 · P2 · Reliability · An approval set to 'Never — wait until someone decides' still gets a 7-day 'Decide by' deadline, after which it can no longer be approved and is never expired by the sweep (D7)

- **Who / where:** end user, workspace admin · `Approval step 'Stop waiting after' = Never; run page 'Decide by'`
- **User impact:** A 'wait forever' approval silently becomes undecidable after a week and the run is stranded paused with no on-expire path.
- **Evidence (reproduced):**
  - Approval step left at default 'Never — wait until someone decides' (kinds.out); run page shows 'Decide by: 10/7/2026, 5:19:28 PM' (7 days) — shots/U4/f1_paused_runpage.png
  - packages/maverick-core/maverick/flow/execution.py:696-700 — expiry = resume_at or time.time()+7*24*3600 for the card
  - runner.py:1476-1478 — resume_at None when expires_after is 0, so the expiry sweep never resolves it; map/06 D7 (approval_cards.py:394 refuses an expired card)
  - Not reproduced end-to-end (would need a 7-day wait)
  - [C5b-034] packages/maverick-core/maverick/flow/execution.py:696-700 — card expiry = resume_at or now + 7 days
  - [C5b-034] packages/maverick-core/maverick/flow/ir.py:275-276 — no expiry means 'waits forever'
  - [C5b-034] packages/maverick-core/maverick/approval_cards.py:394-395 — require_current_approval_card: 'the approval expired; request a fresh review'
  - [C5b-034] packages/maverick-dashboard/maverick_dashboard/automation_queue.py:1158-1162 — expiry path raises 'flow approval has no valid expiry reservation' when resume_at is None
  - [C5b-034] grep allow_expired/remint/reissue in dashboard → no card re-mint path found
  - [C1-011] packages/maverick-core/maverick/flow/approvals.py:25 — _DEFAULT_TTL = 7 * 24 * 3600 # a week to act on an approval
  - [C1-011] packages/maverick-core/maverick/flow/execution.py:699 — expiry falls back to time.time() + 7 * 24 * 3600 when the node has no resume_at
  - [C1-011] packages/maverick-core/maverick/approval_cards.py:324 — ttl = max(60.0, min(float(ttl_seconds), 7 * 24 * 3600.0))
  - [C1-011] packages/maverick-core/maverick/codebase/features.py:231 — APPROVAL_TTL = 7 days
- **Recommendation (effort S):** Either honour 'Never' (no card expiry, or re-mint the card on open) or make the UI say 'up to 7 days' and route to the expiry path at day 7.
- Source: U4-012, C5b-034, C1-011

#### UX-242 · P2 · Reliability · Drafter fallback silently drops the requested schedule and approval gate: 'every weekday at 9am … ask the finance lead to approve before posting to Slack' becomes one unscheduled AI task with no approval step

- **Current branch (2026-10-04):** The fallback now warns plainly when a requested schedule or approval step is missing, and the editor displays that warning. It still produces an editable one-step draft that a person can publish after reviewing; there is no persistent requirement check or installed browser acceptance yet.

- **Who / where:** workspace admin, compliance · `/flows/designer → ✨ Draft`
- **User impact:** A user who publishes the fallback thinks approval is enforced because the words 'ask … to approve' are in the step; in fact nothing pauses for a human and nothing is scheduled.
- **Evidence (reproduced):**
  - nl.out: DRAFT FLOW schedule '' timezone '' nodes [('agent', "Every weekday at 9am pull yesterday's Stripe payments…")] — no approval node
  - packages/maverick-core/maverick/flow/draft.py:551-555 — any failure falls back to single_agent_flow(description)
  - The fallback message does not say the approval or schedule were lost
- **Recommendation (effort S):** On fallback, detect approval/schedule intent in the description and either insert an approval node + schedule or state plainly 'Not included: approval step, weekday 9am schedule — add them below'. Never present an agent brief as a substitute for an approval gate.
- Source: U4-020

#### UX-298 · P2 · Ux · When the plain-English drafter fails, the user sees a Python exception name ('couldn't build a full graph (ValueError)') and gets one AI step whose name is the description cut mid-word

- **Current branch (2026-10-04):** Fallback notes no longer expose Python exception names, the draft title stops at a word boundary, and the designer offers **Try draft again** after a warning or failure while retaining the description. A better short summary and installed browser acceptance remain open.

- **Who / where:** workspace admin, evaluator · `/flows/designer → ✨ Draft`
- **User impact:** On any model hiccup the evaluator sees developer jargon and a meaningless one-box flow with a truncated title, with no suggestion to retry or rephrase.
- **Evidence (reproduced):**
  - nl.out: message 'couldn't build a full graph (ValueError); starting from a single agent step you can expand'
  - nl.out: flow name set to "Every weekday at 9am pull yesterday's Stripe payments, summa" (60-char cut)
  - screenshot: shots/U4/nl_draft_result.png
  - Lab note: fake model returns non-JSON, so this is the failure path; success path not exercised
- **Recommendation (effort S):** Say 'I couldn't turn that into steps — try again or add steps yourself', keep the original description visible, offer Retry, and title the draft from a short summary, never a truncated sentence.
- Source: U4-019

  - packages/maverick-core/maverick/cli/_ekko_groups.py:282 'Strict guided JSONL event stream.' and :318 observer 'guided_jsonl' vs 'windows_foreground' — no other platform observer
  - grep -n 'guided\|download' static/lightwork-ekko-recording.js templates/ekko.html → only explanatory text (ekko.html:135,193); no download of a recorder or guided-recording tool in the page
- **Recommendation (effort L):** Ship a macOS foreground-app observer or a browser-extension recorder, and hide/explain the file option with a download link to the recorder.
- Source: U4-035

### Administration and settings (33)

#### UX-144 · P2 · Trust · Turning on 'Run code' or 'Control a desktop' for every agent is one unconfirmed checkbox save

- **Who / where:** workspace admin, IT/security · `/settings (Features tab) → POST /settings/capabilities`
- **User impact:** An admin tidying the Features tab can grant every agent in every workspace shell/desktop control with one click and no 'are you sure', no second approver even when [safety] quorum_required is set, and no record.
- **Evidence (reproduced):**
  - cmd: curl -H 'Origin: http://127.0.0.1:8815' -X POST /settings/capabilities -d 'code_exec=on&computer_use=on' → 303 /settings?saved=capabilities (no confirm step, no quorum, no audit)
  - packages/maverick-dashboard/maverick_dashboard/admin_pages.py:531-547 settings_set_capabilities: no confirm/quorum, unlike /settings/budget (quorum 247-257) and All settings 'Affects safety' confirm
  - UI copy: 'Control a desktop … The highest-impact capability; enable only for workflows that need to use another app.' — yet saved with a plain 'Save abilities' button
- **Recommendation (effort S):** Treat capability enablement as a weakening change: show a consequence dialog listing what agents gain, honour settings_quorum like the budget form, and audit it. Consider per-workspace scoping of capabilities.
- Source: U5-002

#### UX-156 · P2 · Trust · Pausing, resuming and removing a workspace are not written to the audit log (creation, plan and limit changes are)

- **Who / where:** IT/security, compliance · `POST /api/v1/admin/tenants/{id}/suspend|resume, DELETE /api/v1/admin/tenants/{id}`
- **User impact:** Nobody can prove who took a client's workspace offline or removed it, or when.
- **Evidence (reproduced):**
  - UI: Pause 'Beta Ops' (POST …/beta-ops/suspend 200) and Remove duplicate 'Acme Finance' (DELETE …/acme-finance-2 204); GET /api/v1/audit/tail?n=50 → kinds: setting_changed, tenant_created ×3, learning_update — no suspend/delete rows
  - packages/maverick-dashboard/maverick_dashboard/api.py:1075-1091,1171-1181 call registry.suspend_tenant/resume_tenant/delete_tenant with no audit; registry.py:555-600 audits only plan/quota
  - [C5a-073] packages/maverick-core/maverick/tenant/registry.py:475-480 — suspend/resume = _mutate(status=...) with no audit_event
  - [C5a-073] packages/maverick-core/maverick/tenant/registry.py:620-638 — delete_tenant(purge=True) rmtree without audit; only plan/quota changes are audited (560-564)
- **Recommendation (effort S):** Emit TENANT_SUSPENDED / TENANT_RESUMED / TENANT_DELETED global audit rows with actor and reason, rolled back on AuditRefused like plan/quota changes; ask for an optional reason in the confirm dialog.
- Source: U5-017, C5a-073 · prior audit: W2-72 (related: delete leaves RBAC behind)

#### UX-164 · P2 · Bug · Activity log page shows 'Could not load the protection status. This was changed since you opened it. Refresh the page' when the real cause is 'no workspace selected' — refreshing never fixes it

- **Who / where:** compliance, IT/security, workspace admin · `/audit`
- **User impact:** An auditor sees the protection panel (checkpoints, write-once, SIEM) as broken with a false explanation, refreshes repeatedly, and cannot tell whether the log is protected.
- **Evidence (reproduced):**
  - page load → GET /api/v1/audit/unified/status → 409 {"detail":"select an active tenant before using unified audit"}
  - page text: 'Protection — Daily checkpoints — Write-once copies — Security monitoring — Could not load the protection status. This was changed since you opened it. Refresh the page and try again.'
  - packages/maverick-dashboard/maverick_dashboard/unified_audit_api.py:99 raises the 409; templates/audit.html:327 fetches it; static/lightwork-ui.js:300 maps every 409 to 'This was changed since you opened it'
  - screenshot: shots/U5/audit.png
- **Recommendation (effort S):** Show the protection status for the installation when no workspace is selected, or say 'Choose a workspace to see its protection status' with a workspace picker; pass the server's detail through instead of the generic 409 text.
- Source: U5-010

#### UX-216 · P2 · Bug · Settings says '0 of 9 AI providers connected' and 'vLLM / OpenAI-compatible: No key' while an OpenAI-compatible provider from the environment is running every task

- **Who / where:** workspace admin, evaluator · `/settings`
- **User impact:** The first screen an administrator sees contradicts itself: it asks them to add a key although work is already running, and gives no way to see or rotate the credential actually in use.
- **Evidence (reproduced):**
  - lab env: OPENAI_COMPATIBLE_BASE_URL + OPENAI_COMPATIBLE_API_KEY + MAVERICK_MODEL_OVERRIDE=openai_compatible:fake-model (tasks run fine)
  - screenshot: shots/U5/settings.png — 'CURRENT STATE 0 of 9 AI providers connected · Add a provider key'
  - screenshot: shots/U5/settings_tab_models.png — '0 providers with a key', every provider 'No key', while 'Will use' column shows 'Fake Model · Openai Compatible' for all roles
  - packages/maverick-dashboard/maverick_dashboard/settings_store.py:97-108 PROVIDERS lists 'vllm' labelled 'vLLM / OpenAI-compatible' with env hint OPENAI_COMPATIBLE_BASE_URL, but config.provider_configuration_state('vllm') only checks VLLM_* (packages/maverick-core/maverick/config.py:685-731); provider 'openai_compatible' is not in the Settings list at all
- **Recommendation (effort S):** Build the Settings provider list from the kernel's provider registry (KNOWN_PROVIDERS) and provider_configuration_state for each, including openai_compatible/azure/bedrock/tgi; label env-sourced providers 'Set by your server (environment)' with the effective address.
- Source: U5-003

#### UX-217 · P2 · Bug · All settings shows 'Compatible AI service address/key: Not set · Default' while OPENAI_COMPATIBLE_BASE_URL/API_KEY are set and in use (catalog rows declare no environment source)

- **Who / where:** workspace admin, IT/security · `/settings/all → Integrations → AI service addresses`
- **User impact:** The admin believes no AI service address is configured, and saving one silently re-routes all task text to a new address (config beats env) without the page ever having shown the old one.
- **Evidence (reproduced):**
  - GET /api/v1/settings/catalog: providers.openai_compatible.base_url 'Not set | Default'; providers.openai_compatible.api_key 'Not set | Default' — with OPENAI_COMPATIBLE_BASE_URL and OPENAI_COMPATIBLE_API_KEY exported and every task using them
  - packages/maverick-dashboard/maverick_dashboard/settings_catalog_runtime.py:251-300 — openai_compatible/azure/bedrock rows have no env=(...) although config.PROVIDER_KEY_ENV_MAP/PROVIDER_BASE_URL_ENV_MAP (maverick-core/maverick/config.py:685-731) define them
- **Recommendation (effort S):** Declare the provider env variables on these rows (or resolve via config.provider_configuration_state) so the page shows 'Set by server start-up setting: http://…' and the confirm dialog shows old → new.
- Source: U5-033

#### UX-226 · P2 · Bug · Workspace-level administrators see 'Workspace members' controls on Users but the members API requires installation-wide admin, so they cannot list or change their own workspace's members

- **Who / where:** workspace admin · `/users → Workspace members; /api/v1/admin/tenants/{id}/roles`
- **User impact:** Delegated workspace owners (the whole point of per-workspace roles) get a permission error when adding a colleague, so every membership change escalates to the installation admin.
- **Evidence (code-verified):**
  - packages/maverick-dashboard/maverick_dashboard/api.py:1214-1252 list/put/delete tenant roles call require_global_permission(request, 'admin')
  - map/12 D5: /users requires tenant-aware admin (admin_pages.py:762) and _workspace_options offers the tenant admin's own workspaces; static/lightwork-workspace-members.js:12 calls the global-admin API
  - not reproduced live (lab runs in no-sign-in mode where everyone is installation admin)
  - [C5c-069] packages/maverick-dashboard/maverick_dashboard/admin_pages.py:612-640 — _workspace_options offers non-global admins the workspaces they belong to
  - [C5c-069] packages/maverick-dashboard/maverick_dashboard/static/lightwork-workspace-members.js:12 — calls /api/v1/admin/tenants/{id}/roles
  - [C5c-069] packages/maverick-dashboard/maverick_dashboard/api.py:1210-1256 — GET/PUT/DELETE roles require require_global_permission('admin')
- **Recommendation (effort S):** Authorize tenant-role list/assign/remove with tenant-aware admin on that tenant (require_permission with the path tenant), while preventing a workspace admin from granting installation-wide roles.
- Source: U5-040, C5c-069 · prior audit: map/12 D5

#### UX-228 · P2 · Bug · Workspaces: two workspaces can have the same name ('Acme Finance' twice); the page's 'name already exists' message is dead code

- **Who / where:** workspace admin · `/tenants → Create workspace (POST /api/v1/admin/tenants)`
- **User impact:** The workspace switcher, spending-limit list and members picker show two identical 'Acme Finance' entries; admins can put a client's work, budget and people in the wrong one.
- **Evidence (reproduced):**
  - UI: created 'Acme Finance' then 'Acme Finance' again → both POST 201; GET /api/v1/admin/tenants → ids acme-finance and acme-finance-2, both display_name 'Acme Finance'
  - packages/maverick-dashboard/maverick_dashboard/api.py:1016-1033 unique_slug() suffixes the id, so the 409 branch is never hit for a duplicate name
  - packages/maverick-dashboard/maverick_dashboard/static/lightwork-tenants.js:58-60 expects 409 → 'A workspace with that name already exists'
- **Recommendation (effort S):** Reject (or require confirmation for) a display name already used by an active workspace, case-insensitively; show the id/creation date to disambiguate existing duplicates.
- Source: U5-012

#### UX-230 · P2 · Reliability · Backups ship switched off: 'Workspace backups' (snapshot, check, restore) default to Off, so a new installation has no protected copy until an admin finds the toggle

- **Who / where:** workspace admin, IT/security, evaluator · `/settings Features → 'Workspace backups'; /workspace/recovery`
- **User impact:** Customers discover there is no backup only when they need a restore; the Settings > Features description 'Let administrators make, check and restore backups' reads like an optional extra rather than basic data protection.
- **Evidence (code-verified):**
  - packages/maverick-dashboard/maverick_dashboard/settings_store.py:126 FEATURE_DEFAULTS 'workspace_recovery': False
  - live: /workspace/recovery → 'Workspace recovery is turned off.'
  - packages/maverick-dashboard/maverick_dashboard/recovery_api.py _admit requires [features] workspace_recovery (map/12 §2)
- **Recommendation (effort S):** Default workspace backups on (snapshot creation needs no special authority), or make 'Set up backups' a required step in first-run setup and show a persistent 'No backup yet' warning on Settings/Overview.
- Source: U5-022

#### UX-265 · P2 · Ux · Workspace recovery page says 'Your recovery access is unavailable. Sign in with an authorized account' when the real reason is that backups are switched off

- **Who / where:** workspace admin, IT/security · `/workspace/recovery`
- **User impact:** A local administrator is sent to sign in (impossible in local mode) and sees every snapshot/restore control even though none can work.
- **Evidence (reproduced):**
  - page shows both 'Workspace recovery is turned off … turn on Workspace recovery under Features in Settings' AND 'Your recovery access is unavailable. Sign in with an authorized account and reload this page before continuing.'
  - GET /api/v1/recovery/status → 403 'Workspace recovery is disabled. A global administrator can enable it in Settings before entering recovery mode.'
  - screenshot: shots/U5/workspace_recovery.png
- **Recommendation (effort S):** When the feature is off, show only the 'turn it on' state with a direct toggle (for global admins) and hide or disable the controls; reserve the sign-in message for real 401s.
- Source: U5-021

#### UX-291 · P2 · Ux · During an emergency stop the chat home shows no stopped banner; a user's new request immediately fails as 'Lightwork stopped — halted' with a 'Try again' button that cannot work

- **Who / where:** end user, workspace admin · `/ (chat home) while /api/v1/halt active`
- **User impact:** Business users keep submitting work into a stopped system, see the internal word 'halted', and retry pointlessly; nothing tells them an administrator paused all work or when it will resume.
- **Evidence (reproduced):**
  - UI: Settings → 'Emergency stop' → 'Stop work' → header pill 'STOPPED — click to resume'; then / (chat home): no 'stopped'/'emergency' text anywhere (Playwright body scan)
  - sent 'Write a short note about Q3 planning' → card 'Lightwork stopped · halted · [Try again] · Set a spending limit for this attempt'
  - screenshots: shots/U5/halt_chat_home.png, shots/U5/halt_chat_after_send.png
- **Recommendation (effort S):** Show a persistent banner in the chat shell while a stop is active ('An administrator paused all work at 18:28 — new requests will wait'), disable or relabel the composer, queue requests as 'Waiting for resume', and replace 'halted/Try again' with plain copy plus who to contact.
- Source: U5-036

#### UX-316 · P2 · Ux · License page lists 'Multiple workspaces: Off' (and other paid features Off) while those features work because license enforcement is off; the page never says enforcement is off

- **Who / where:** workspace admin, IT/security, evaluator · `/settings/license`
- **User impact:** Admins cannot tell what they are actually licensed for vs. what currently works; a later enforcement switch would silently break workspaces the page claimed were off all along (or buyers under-buy/over-buy).
- **Evidence (reproduced):**
  - /settings/license: 'No license · Basic plan … Multiple workspaces Off … This server has no trusted license keys yet, so it cannot confirm that a license is genuine and paid features stay off.'
  - same instance: /tenants created 'Acme Finance', 'Beta Ops', 'Gamma Client' successfully
  - packages/maverick-core/maverick/entitlements.py:330-335 require() returns True when not enforcing; tenant/registry.py:421-431 gate is fail-open
- **Recommendation (effort S):** Show 'License checking: off — all features available' vs 'on', and per feature 'Available now (not licensed)' so the effective state and the licensed state are both visible.
- Source: U5-030

#### UX-332 · P2 · Ux · Saving a model for a role is accepted with 'Saved' but silently ignored when the server's model override is set; the page gives no reason

- **Who / where:** workspace admin, IT/security · `/settings → Save role models`
- **User impact:** The admin believes planning now uses a stronger model; nothing changed and nothing says why. This is exactly the 'successful save while another source silently overrides it' the customer-experience contract forbids.
- **Evidence (reproduced):**
  - cmd: POST /settings/models/roles orchestrator=anthropic:claude-opus-4-8 → banner 'Saved. Role models updated.'; 'Will use' for Orchestrator still 'Fake Model · Openai Compatible'
  - screenshot: shots/U5/settings_roles_env_override.png

- **Recommendation (effort S):** Detect MAVERICK_MODEL_OVERRIDE / _<ROLE> in the Models section, disable the pickers it controls, and show 'Set by your server's deployment settings: <model>' with the owner; refuse the save with that explanation.
- Source: U5-006 · prior audit: post-install-operation-coverage.md 'Settings controlled by deployment'

#### UX-333 · P2 · Ux · All settings shows deployment-controlled settings as 'Now: Controlled by the server' without the effective value, the owning variable or any path to take control in-product

- **Who / where:** workspace admin, IT/security · `/settings/all (e.g. 'Require known prices')`
- **User impact:** The admin cannot see whether billing-grade pricing is on or off right now (default says On, actual is Off), nor who controls it, nor how to move control into the product — the contract's 'explain the current owner and provide an authorized transfer' is unmet.
- **Evidence (reproduced):**
  - lab: MAVERICK_BILLING_STRICT=0 in env and [budget] strict_pricing=false in config.toml → GET /api/v1/settings/catalog row budget.strict_pricing: value null, value_text 'Controlled by the server', source_text 'Set by your server's deployment settings', default_text 'On'
  - cmd: POST /api/v1/settings/catalog budget.strict_pricing=true → 409 'Require known prices is set by your server's deployment settings, so it can't be changed here.'
  - packages/maverick-dashboard/maverick_dashboard/settings_all_page.py:127-130 _resolve returns value None/known False for env-locked rows
- **Recommendation (effort M):** Resolve and display the effective value from the env/operator source, name the source in plain words ('server start-up setting'), and offer an admin 'Request transfer to Lightwork settings' guide that produces the exact removal step for IT plus readback once it takes effect.
- Source: U5-032 · prior audit: post-install-operation-coverage.md 'Settings controlled by deployment'

#### UX-334 · P2 · Ux · Settings 'Find a setting' says 'No settings match' for budget, Slack, SSO, single sign-on, api key, retention and timeout — including 'budget', which its own placeholder suggests

- **Who / where:** workspace admin, evaluator · `/settings #settings-search`
- **User impact:** The first search box an admin tries fails for the most common admin tasks (spending, SSO, Slack), so they conclude the product can't do it; the 1,519-row All settings page is the only place those settings exist.

  - same terms on /settings/all return 13/10/6/3/7/11/1 rows — the main search never looks there
- **Recommendation (effort M):** Make the Settings search federated: include All settings rows, Channels, Users, Workspaces, Spending limits and Connections results with links; add synonyms (budget→spending, SSO→single sign-on/company sign-in, key→secret).

#### UX-336 · P2 · Ux · Every 409 anywhere in the dashboard is shown as 'This was changed since you opened it', hiding the real reason (already exists, not configured, no workspace selected, controlled by deployment)

#### UX-339 · P2 · Ux · Workspace spending limit can be set in two places with two different meanings — Workspaces 'Daily limit' vs Spending limits 'Whole workspace' — and each shows 'No limit' while the other is set

#### UX-343 · P2 · Ux · Users page says 'Sign-in is off. Roles only take effect once company sign-in is turned on' with no link or path to turning sign-in on; the invitation toggle refuses with 'Set up this computer's owner account first' — also no link

#### UX-579 · P3 · Ux · Emergency stop and resume capture no reason from the administrator (audit shows 'manual via dashboard' / 'operator requested halt clear')

### Governance workbenches (18)

#### UX-207 · P2 · Bug · 'Turn on' reports success but the page stays off: Consent register (needs a secret set elsewhere) and AI evidence analysis (needs the evidence gateway)

- **Who / where:** compliance, workspace admin · `/consent, /ai-evidence-analysis, POST /api/v1/features/modules`
- **User impact:** The officer clicks Turn on, sees no error, and the feature is still off with no explanation of the missing prerequisite. Repeated clicks do nothing.
- **Evidence (reproduced):**
  - POST /api/v1/features/modules {section:'consent_registry',enabled:true} -> 200 enabled:true; /consent still renders 'Consent register is turned off.' with the same Turn on button (crawl u6_crawl_on.json)
  - Turn on ai evidence analysis clicked on /ai-evidence-analysis -> POST 200; page then says 'Evidence analysis is turned off for this workspace.' with no button (crawl u6_crawl_on.json)
  - packages/maverick-core/maverick/consent_registry.py:94-97 also requires consent_registry.subject_salt (16-256 chars); the /privacy banner says 'It also needs a protection secret, set on the Settings page'
  - packages/maverick-dashboard/maverick_dashboard/ai_evidence_analysis_composition.py:557-560 requires evidence_gateway.enable, but api.py _MODULE_SWITCHES['ai_evidence_analysis']['requires'] is ()
- **Recommendation (effort S):** Make each switch's requires chain match the kernel gate (add evidence_gateway), and have the gate banner list unmet prerequisites (e.g. 'needs a protection secret - Set it now') with an inline control that generates the salt.
- Source: U6-008

#### UX-221 · P2 · Bug · AI Vendor Onboarding with no workspace shows a false 'The workspace or record changed' dead end instead of the workspace picker

- **Who / where:** compliance, evaluator · `GET /third-party/vendor-onboarding`
- **User impact:** A compliance officer opening the vendor onboarding page first sees an error claiming something changed, with Reload as the only action, which loops forever. Nothing tells them to create or choose a workspace.
- **Evidence (reproduced):**
  - Fresh lab, no workspace: GET /third-party/vendor-onboarding -> 409 page titled 'Refresh before continuing' with copy 'The workspace or record changed after this page loaded. Reload it...' (screenshot: shots/U6/off_third-party_vendor-onboarding.png); reloading repeats it. Every other tenant-bound page (e.g. /third-party/contracts, /consent/bulk-jobs) shows 'Choose a workspace' with a Set up my workspace button.
  - packages/maverick-dashboard/maverick_dashboard/vendor_onboarding_page.py:24 raises HTTPException(409, 'Select an active tenant') (capital S)
  - packages/maverick-dashboard/maverick_dashboard/app.py:2315-2325 routes to the picker only when detail.startswith('select an active tenant') (case-sensitive), so this page falls through to the generic 409 copy at app.py:2368-2371
- **Recommendation (effort S):** Use the shared lowercase detail (or a typed exception) in vendor_onboarding_page.py, and make the handler match case-insensitively / on an error code rather than message prefix.
- Source: U6-002 · prior audit: QA-029 (browser-friendly tenant gate, marked fixed) - this page missed

#### UX-263 · P2 · Ux · Model Risk & AI Assurance is one 18,000-pixel page with 478 visible form controls in 93 forms

- **Who / where:** compliance, evaluator · `/security/assurance`
- **User impact:** A risk officer who wants to register one AI system and assess it must scroll through supplier reviews, drift, agent reach, red teaming, EU incidents, literacy, cost, policy packs and more on one page. There is no task list or 'what to do next'. OneTrust AI Governance and ServiceNow AI Control Tower split this into an inventory list, per-system record pages and a task inbox.

  - Playwright on /security/assurance with modules on: 478 visible inputs/selects/textareas, 93 <form> elements, document height 17,980 px (u6_probe2.py)

  - Before a workspace existed the same page fired 10 failing API calls (409) on load (u6_crawl_off.json)
- **Recommendation (effort L):** Split into an AI-system inventory list plus a per-system record page (tabs: risk, evidence, incidents, tasks), and keep module-specific tools on their own pages. Put a guided 'Register an AI system -> classify -> assess' path at the top.
- Source: U6-012

#### UX-305 · P2 · Ux · Several workbenches say 'Ready', then fail with 'temporarily unavailable, try again in a few minutes' for persistent setup problems

- **Who / where:** compliance, workspace admin · `/third-party/contracts, /ai-entity-tasks, /privacy/drop, /consent/trust-center-authority, /consent/scan-notice-proposals, /assess/evidence-autopopulation, /compliance/continuous-evidence`
- **User impact:** After turning a module on, the officer is told it is ready and then told to wait; waiting never helps and neither they nor IT get a reason or a next step. Root cause not determined in this audit (the exceptions are swallowed).
- **Evidence (reproduced):**
  - /third-party/contracts shows 'AVAILABILITY Ready' then 'Could not load the contracts. This is temporarily unavailable. Please try again in a few minutes.'; API GET /api/v1/third-party/contracts -> 503 'Contract lifecycle store is unavailable'
  - /ai-entity-tasks shows 'Ready ... Task controls are ready' then 'Could not finish this. This is temporarily unavailable'; GET /api/v1/ai-entity-tasks -> 503 'AI-entity task store is unavailable'
  - /privacy/drop 'temporarily unavailable' <- 503 'DROP authority composition is unavailable'; /consent/trust-center-authority 503 'Trust Center authority is unavailable'; scan-notice-proposals 503 'runtime is unavailable'; autopopulation 503 'assessment evidence authority is unavailable'; continuous-evidence setup 503 'collector allowlist is unavailable'
  - Retried after >10 minutes and a restart: unchanged. homes/u6/logs/dashboard.out contains only the access line for each 503 (no cause logged)
  - packages/maverick-dashboard/maverick_dashboard/third_party_contracts_api.py:373-383 and ai_entity_tasks_api.py:234-244 convert any exception into a generic 503 without logging
- **Recommendation (effort M):** Distinguish 'not configured' from 'temporarily unavailable'; log the swallowed exception with a correlation id; have availability probes exercise the same store factory so 'Ready' is truthful; name the missing setup and link to where it is done.
- Source: U6-009

#### UX-324 · P2 · Ux · Access request is marked 'Answered' after collection although nothing was delivered, and the collected copy cannot be downloaded from the request

- **Current-source scope correction:** UX-020 now removes an authentic saved export on close and exposes cleanup failure/retry in the product. The misleading "Answered" state before delivery and missing officer review/download of the collected package remain open here. The old indefinite-retention evidence below is historical after that close-path fix; existing closed records require a retry or migration sweep.
- **Who / where:** compliance · `/privacy/dsar/{id} > 'Collect their data and mark answered'`
- **User impact:** The request list shows the person as answered before they have received anything, so SLA reporting overstates compliance; the officer cannot review or hand over the collected copy, and a second copy of personal data lingers on the server indefinitely.
- **Evidence (reproduced):**
  - Live: opened access request DSAR-639cc5bd10 from Privacy > Data requests, clicked 'Collect their data and mark answered' > Continue; status became 'Answered' while 'Send them a secure link' still reads 'No secure link sent yet' (shots/U6/dsar_access_collect.png)
  - Rendered request page contains no download/export link (curl grep for export|download -> none)
  - Export written to tenants/local/dsar_requests/exports/DSAR-639cc5bd10-export.json (plaintext JSON on the server); per packages/maverick-core/maverick/privacy_ops.py:2946-2976 and :3002-3021 it is never deleted on close (map/10b D3)
- **Recommendation (effort M):** Separate 'data collected' from 'response delivered'; show the collected package with a reviewed download/redaction step; delete (or retention-limit) the server-side export when the request closes.
- Source: U6-014 · prior audit: W4-49 (plaintext export, no retention - still present)

- **Recommendation (effort M):** Show the questionnaire row with Copy link / Resend / Revoke, a due date and automatic reminders, and a 'View answers + score' drawer; refresh the panel in place after creation; record the signed-in person, not 'dashboard'.

#### UX-636 · P3 · Ux · Before a workspace exists, governance pages fail in three different ways (picker, silent failed calls, or 'not ready')

### Whole-app UI sweep (32)

#### UX-278 · P2 · Ux · Connections page contradicts itself: 'Connections is turned off' next to 'Your sign-in or administrator access changed. Sign in again'

- **Who / where:** workspace admin, evaluator · `/connections, /workspace/recovery`
- **User impact:** An administrator is told to sign in again (on an install with no sign-in) when the only thing needed is the Turn on button; they may chase a non-existent auth problem.
- **Evidence (reproduced):**
  - /connections (local admin, feature off): API 403 on /api/v1/connections and /api/v1/connection-setup; page text shows 'Connections is turned off.' AND 'Your sign-in or administrator access changed. Sign in again and reload Connections.' (u7/crawl_results.jsonl)
  - static/lightwork-connection-setup.js:78 maps any 403 (kind session/scope) to the sign-in message; the API detail actually says 'Connections aren't enabled on this server yet…'
  - /workspace/recovery shows 'Workspace recovery is turned off.' plus 'Your recovery access is unavailable. Sign in with an authorized account…' (static/lightwork-workspace-recovery.js:14) while /api/v1/recovery/status says 'Workspace recovery is disabled.'
- **Recommendation (effort S):** Branch on the server's feature-off detail (or a machine-readable code) before falling back to the session/scope message; suppress the secondary panel error when the page already shows the module-off banner.
- Source: U7-013 · prior audit: related U5-011 (409 variant)

#### UX-314 · P2 · Ux · Sidebar 'Knowledge' is a dead end in a local install: 'Sign in with your own account' although this install has no sign-in

- **Who / where:** evaluator, end user, workspace admin · `/knowledge-access (sidebar Insights > Knowledge; linked from every page)`
- **User impact:** An evaluator clicking Knowledge in the main navigation is told to sign in to an account that cannot exist on their install; neither 'Choose a workspace' nor reload fixes it. There is no in-product path to use Knowledge locally.
- **Evidence (reproduced):**
  - GET /knowledge-access → 403 page 'Sign in with your own account — This page works only when you sign in with your own account and choose a workspace.' with buttons 'Reload this page', 'Choose a workspace', 'Back to home' (lab: auth off, local operator)
  - knowledge_access_api.py:291-296 `if not actor or not actor.startswith('user:') or not tenant: raise HTTPException(403, 'Sign in with a named account…')` — a loopback single-user install never has a `user:` principal
  - ui_visibility.py PAGES: /knowledge-access label 'Knowledge', group Observe, in_nav true, ready true
  - linkcheck: /knowledge-access linked from all 150+ crawled pages (u7/linkcheck.json)
  - screenshot: shots/U7/desktop_knowledge_access.jpg
- **Recommendation (effort M):** Either support the local operator as a named actor for Knowledge, or hide/mark the nav item as 'Needs company sign-in' with a link to set up sign-in (Settings > Access) instead of a dead-end 403.
- Source: U7-010

#### UX-315 · P2 · Ux · Skills page tool picker shows ~2,000 developer docstrings: env-var names, 'op=validate with roots ({principal: [caps]})', '[governed: writes simulated…]'

- **Who / where:** end user, workspace admin · `/skills (create-a-skill tool list)`
- **User impact:** A business user building a skill has to pick tools from a wall of API documentation they cannot interpret; it contradicts the contract's rule that endpoint names and config keys stay out of the ordinary experience.
- **Evidence (reproduced):**
  - Rendered text: 'Aircall — Aircall REST. ops get/post/put/delete (writes need confirm). Auth: AIRCALL_BASE_URL + AIRCALL_TOKEN (api_id:api_token, basic). [governed: writes simulated, human-gated, and transaction-receipted]'; 'Capability delegation — … op=validate with 'roots' ({principal: [caps]}) and 'grants' ([{from, to, cap}])'; 'Bias eval — … op=evaluate with 'groups' ({name: {selected, total, [tp], [positives]}})' (u7/copy_scan.json)
  - copy scan on /skills: 105 snake_case identifiers, 15 '/api/v1/…' endpoint examples, env vars incl. ANTHROPIC_API_TOKEN, JSON-shaped schemas
  - templates/skills.html:287 `text.textContent = human(t.name) + ' — ' + t.description` renders the raw tool docstring from /api/v1/tools
- **Recommendation (effort M):** Add a plain-language `summary` field to tool metadata (fallback: first sentence, stripped of 'Auth:'/'op='/'[governed…]' segments) and show technical details only in an expandable 'For developers' row.
- Source: U7-016

#### UX-321 · P2 · Ux · Overview 'Current state' badge says 'idle' while a task is blocked waiting for the user's answer

- **Who / where:** end user, evaluator · `/overview`
- **User impact:** The at-a-glance status tells a manager nothing needs them while work is actually stalled on their reply; the only signal is small text in the card copy.
- **Evidence (reproduced):**
  - With seeded task #2 blocked on 'Which region should the report cover?': /overview hero shows '3 goals on record' + badge 'idle' + '2 delivered · 1 blocked' (screenshots shots/U7/desktop_overview.jpg, shots/U7/themes/light_overview.jpg)
  - templates/index.html:13-14 `badge=(counts.active ~ ' active') if counts.active else 'idle', badge_class='ok' if counts.active else 'idle'` — blocked/waiting work never changes the badge
- **Recommendation (effort S):** Make the badge reflect the most urgent state: 'N waiting on you' (warn) when counts.blocked > 0, then 'N active', then 'All caught up'; link it to the filtered task list.
- Source: U7-032

#### UX-412 · P2 · Perf · Results page ships 1.16 MB of HTML (356,000 px tall on a phone) with a 1,446-option role picker and no pagination; 7.2 s to load on phone

- **Who / where:** end user, evaluator · `/deliverables`
- **User impact:** The page is slow and practically unscrollable on a phone; the role picker is unusable at 1,446 options.
- **Evidence (reproduced):**
  - curl /deliverables → 1,161,885 bytes, 0.52 s server time (idle lab)
  - crawl: phone load 7.21 s (TTFB 1,257 ms), desktop 3.98 s; document scrollHeight 356,154 px at 390 px width — u7/pages.csv, u7/digest.json 'slow'
  - Visible text begins with a <select> 'Pick one of 1446 roles…' listing every role (incl. near-duplicates 'Academic advisor' / 'Academic advisors')
  - app.py:3322-3327 one list_goals query per pack spec (2,031)
  - [C4-011] cmd: pages.py -> 1,134.7 KB at both 5k and 20k tasks; first load 1.44 s (5k) / 0.81 s (20k), warm 0.22-0.67 s
  - [C4-011] packages/maverick-dashboard/maverick_dashboard/app.py:3322-3329 — one list_goals query per deliverable spec (idx_goals_domain_completed now makes each cheap, so the old W3-21 3 s cliff did not reproduce)
- **Recommendation (effort M):** Paginate/virtualise the inbox (e.g. 25 per page), replace the role <select> with a type-ahead, batch the per-pack query into one grouped query.
- Source: U7-009, C4-011 · prior audit: W3-21 (query-per-pack, W3-21 (still present at HEAD), latency cliff not reproduced at HEAD, payload remains)

#### UX-415 · P2 · A11Y · Selected Settings tab is unreadable in the High-contrast theme (white on cyan, 1.25:1) and fails contrast in every theme

- **Who / where:** workspace admin, IT/security, end user · `/settings (tab bar), themes dark/light/solarized/hicontrast`
- **User impact:** A low-vision administrator who switches to the High-contrast theme precisely to read the UI cannot read which Settings section they are in; the active tab is the least legible element on the page. It also fails WCAG 1.4.3 in the default dark theme.
- **Evidence (reproduced):**
  - axe color-contrast on /settings button[data-settings-tab=general][aria-selected=true]: hicontrast #ffffff on #00ffff = 1.25:1; solarized #ffffff on #4fa3d8 = 2.77:1; dark #ffffff on #3d8bff = 3.31:1 (need 4.5:1) — u7/theme_results.jsonl, u7/axe_summary.json
  - screenshot: shots/U7/hicontrast_settings_tabs.png (the 'General' label is nearly invisible)
  - packages/maverick-dashboard/maverick_dashboard/templates/settings.html:703 — `.settings-tabs [aria-selected="true"] { background: var(--brand); color: var(--on-brand, white); }`
  - grep: `--on-brand` is never defined anywhere in static/ or templates/ (only used), so the fallback `white` always wins; the design system's real token is `--brand-fg` (static/lightwork.css:57-92, #000000 in hicontrast/solarized)
- **Recommendation (effort S):** Replace `var(--on-brand, white)` with `var(--brand-fg)` in settings.html:703 (and grep for any other `--on-brand` use); add a rendered-theme contrast check for the selected-tab state to the a11y gate.
- Source: U7-001

#### UX-485 · P3 · Bug · 'Download AI inventory list' (Compliance) and 'Download the public key' (Consent publishing) open raw JSON error pages

- **Who / where:** compliance · `/compliance → /api/v1/compliance/downloads/ai-bom; /consent/publishing → /api/v1/consent/publishing/signing-key/public-key`
- **User impact:** Clicking a download button replaces the page with a line of JSON; the user loses their place and gets no path to fix it.

  - /api/v1/consent/publishing/signing-key/public-key → 409 application/json {"detail":"Select a workspace before using the signing key."}

- **Recommendation (effort S):** Render these as buttons that check availability first (disabled with a reason, per QA-063) or fetch and show a toast on failure; never navigate the browser to a JSON error.
- Source: U7-015 · prior audit: QA-063 (same class: unavailable downloads should be disabled with an explanation)

#### UX-539 · P3 · Reliability · Task 'Plan tree' pulls its graph library from cdn.jsdelivr.net at runtime; offline/air-gapped installs only get the list fallback

  - Every other dashboard script is self-hosted under /static
- **Recommendation (effort S):** Vendor cytoscape.min.js under /static (it already has an SRI pin) and drop the CDN from the page CSP.
- Source: U7-021

#### UX-549 · P3 · Ux · Activity log rows dump internal fields: 24-hex 'Call ID', 64-hex 'Call commitment', 'sha256:lightwork.tool-call-id:v2' and raw JSON input

- **Who / where:** compliance, workspace admin · `/audit`
- **User impact:** An auditor reading the activity log must skip past hashes and serialized JSON on every tool event; the useful part (who asked what) is buried.
- **Evidence (reproduced):**
  - /audit rendered text for the seeded [ask] task: 'Name Ask user · Call ID 4fc05d8f644a6d4e63eb7a9c · Call commitment a05c42ea8be53d9f3300966741b268a8b7445d1b989a27a4c41ad42a57792ad7 · Call commitment algorithm sha256:lightwork.tool-call-id:v2 · Input {"question": "Which region should the report cover?"}' (u7/copy_scan.json sha/hash, raw_json)
  - audit_actions_api.py:109-112 event_details() shows every event key not in _HIDDEN, so each new kernel field (agent.py:3252-3253 call_commitment/_algorithm) leaks into the table automatically; the chain hashes themselves are correctly tucked into a <details>
- **Recommendation (effort S):** Switch event_details to an allow-list of human fields per event kind; move call ids/commitments into the existing 'How this entry is protected' disclosure; render input as readable text.
- Source: U7-017

#### UX-595 · P3 · Ux · Agent names are shown as slugs with random hex suffixes ('Orchestrator 0 8992d2', 'Orchestrator 0 24303e') on history, receipts and activity pages

- **Who / where:** end user, compliance · `/goals/{id}/trajectory ('Who' filter and each step), /audit/receipts (Agent column), /audit`

- **User impact:** ~75 KB of redundant font transfer on first load (more on slow/mobile links) and four font swaps instead of one.

  - md5sum static/fonts/manrope-200/300/400/500/600/700.woff2 → all 938c6e8019b69313372c47dbb7a7c930 (24,836 bytes each)
  - static/lightwork.css:1393-1398 six @font-face rules, one per weight, each pointing at a different copy
  - Phone load of /start requested manrope-200, -400, -600 and -700 (4 × 24.8 KB for one file) — u7/misc.py output
- **Recommendation (effort S):** Ship one variable font file with a single `@font-face { font-weight: 200 800; src: url(manrope-var.woff2) }` and delete the copies.
- Source: U7-020 · prior audit: W3-77 (asset weight, still present)

#### UX-697 · P3 · A11Y · Governance Agents page skips a heading level (h3 'Breach response' with no h2 above it)

- **Who / where:** compliance · `/governance-agents`
- **User impact:** Screen-reader heading navigation presents the agent sections as sub-points of the page title's intro rather than as sections, making the page structure confusing.

#### UX-699 · P3 · A11Y · Links inside body text are distinguishable only by hue (no underline, 1.13-1.47:1 against surrounding text) on 12+ pages in every theme

- **Who / where:** end user, workspace admin, compliance · `/overview, /spend, /savings, /automations, /deliverables, /workflows, /finance, /fleets, /learned, /shoring, /tenants, /tenants/overview (+ /settings, /agents, /privacy, /flows/designer, /workflow-builder, /permissions, /learning in hicontrast)`
- **User impact:** Colour-blind and low-vision users cannot tell that words like 'chat', 'Workforce', 'run history' or 'Templates' in page intros are links, so they miss the intended next step (WCAG 1.4.1 Use of Color).
- **Evidence (reproduced):**
  - axe link-in-text-block (serious) on 12 pages at both 1400x900 and 390x844 (u7/axe_summary.json); example /deliverables `.hero-lede > a[href=/goals]` 'run history': link #3d8bff vs text #8e97ac = 1.13:1, no underline
  - theme sweep: light 1.47:1, solarized 1.43:1, hicontrast 1.28:1 (12 pages) — u7/theme_results.jsonl
  - The hero lede links (e.g. Overview 'chat', 'Workforce') are the main cross-page navigation in the page intro
- **Recommendation (effort S):** Underline links in running text (`.hero-lede a, .muted a, p a { text-decoration: underline; text-underline-offset: 2px }`) in lightwork.css, keeping the colour; exempt nav/buttons.
- Source: U7-002

#### UX-700 · P3 · A11Y · Small tap targets on phones: 13x13 px checkboxes (12 pages) and 20 px-tall row links on Tasks

- **Who / where:** end user, compliance · `/consent, /cortex, /external-agents, /channels and 8 more (checkboxes); /goals ('Plan', 'Step by step' 26x20 px)`
- **User impact:** Hard to hit accurately with a finger; below WCAG 2.2 target-size (24x24) guidance.
- **Evidence (reproduced):** phone pass: 94 checkbox inputs at 13x13 px on 12 pages; /goals row actions 'Plan' 26x20, 'Step by step' 77x20; several <summary> toggles 20-22 px tall — u7/phone2_results.jsonl
- **Recommendation (effort S):** Give checkbox/radio a 24px min hit area (label padding or `min-width/min-height: 24px`), and min-height 32px for row action links and summaries on touch devices.
- Source: U7-026

#### UX-701 · P3 · A11Y · Text contrast on the 'Liquid Glass' surfaces cannot be verified by tooling: axe marks ~8,800-11,700 text nodes per theme as 'needs review' on 30 sample pages

- **Who / where:** compliance, IT/security · `30 sample pages × 4 themes (dark, light, solarized, hicontrast)`
- **User impact:** Nobody — neither CI nor an automated audit — can currently vouch that ordinary text meets WCAG contrast on glass cards; accessibility claims to enterprise buyers are unsupported.
- **Evidence (reproduced):**
  - axe color-contrast 'incomplete' counts: dark 11,683, light 11,683, solarized 11,683, hicontrast 8,828 nodes (backgrounds are translucent/blurred gradients axe cannot resolve) — u7/theme_results.jsonl
  - Only 1 hard color-contrast violation per theme was provable (U7-001); the rest is unmeasured
  - docs/customer-experience-contract.md:21-26 requires verifying readability on the actual backgrounds; the CI a11y gate is static-only (W3-76)
- **Recommendation (effort M):** Add a rendered contrast check that screenshots text boxes and computes contrast against the sampled pixels (or temporarily disables backdrop-filter to measure against the solid fallback) for the top pages in all themes; wire it into CI next to a11y_audit.
- Source: U7-031 · prior audit: W3-76

#### UX-702 · P3 · A11Y · Very small text across the shell: sidebar group labels 10.5 px, hero state labels and table headers 11 px on phones

- **Who / where:** end user, workspace admin · `152 of 160 pages at 390 px (sidebar .navgrp__label on every base page)`
- **User impact:** Navigation group names and table column headers are hard to read without zooming, especially in all-caps monospace.
- **Evidence (reproduced):** phone pass: text with computed size <12px on 152 pages: span.navgrp__label 10.5px (every page), div.hero-statebox__label 11px (56 pages), th 11px (29 pages), board SVG text 10px (/overview, /oversight, /graph-editor) — u7/phone2_results.jsonl

#### UX-703 · P3 · A11Y · Ekko page has two unlabeled sidebar landmarks (the product nav and Ekko's own <aside id=sidebar>)

- **Who / where:** end user · `/ekko`
- **User impact:** Screen-reader users listing landmarks see two identical 'complementary' regions and cannot tell the navigation from Ekko's panel.

#### UX-705 · P3 · A11Y · Goal Map: task nodes are focusable but sit inside an SVG exposed as role=img, so screen readers hide them

- **Who / where:** end user · `/graph-editor`
- **User impact:** Keyboard users tab into map nodes that assistive technology announces as nothing (children of an image), a confusing silent focus trap-like experience.
- **Evidence (reproduced):** axe nested-interactive (serious): `<svg id="ge-svg" role="img" aria-label="Map of 3 tasks. Use the editor beside the map…">` has focusable descendants (both viewports) — u7/axe_summary.json
- **Recommendation (effort S):** Either remove tabindex from the SVG nodes (the side editor is the keyboard path, as the label says) or change the SVG to role=group with labelled node buttons.

#### UX-706 · P3 · A11Y · Horizontally scrollable tables cannot be scrolled with the keyboard (scroll wrappers are not focusable) on 11 pages

- **Who / where:** compliance, IT/security, workspace admin · `/code, /agent-control-plane, /audit/binder, /compliance/obligations, /embed-demo, /immune, /partner, /security, /security/assurance, /security/report, /skills (mostly at phone width)`
- **User impact:** A keyboard-only or switch user on a narrow window cannot reach the right-hand columns of these tables (status, actions, dates) at all; mouse/touch users can.
- **Evidence (reproduced):**
  - axe scrollable-region-focusable (serious), 32 nodes on 11 pages — u7/axe_summary.json; e.g. /code phone `section[aria-labelledby=ic-repo-title] > .ic-table-wrap`, /agent-control-plane phone `.acp-table-wrap`
  - The wrappers are `overflow-x:auto` divs with no tabindex and no focusable content in the clipped columns
- **Recommendation (effort S):** Give each table scroll wrapper `tabindex="0"`, `role="region"` and an `aria-label` naming the table (one shared `.table-wrap` component), or reflow tables into cards below 560px.
- Source: U7-003

#### UX-707 · P3 · A11Y · Task 'Plan tree' and 'Step-by-step history' pages have no <h1> (the task title is an <h2>)

- **Who / where:** end user, compliance · `/goals/{id}/plan, /goals/{id}/trajectory`

#### UX-709 · P3 · Docs · Built-in API docs (/docs, /redoc) depend on public CDNs, and ReDoc's Google Fonts stylesheet is blocked by the app's own CSP on every load

- **Who / where:** developer, IT/security · `/docs, /redoc`
- **User impact:** Developers on restricted networks get blank API docs; everyone gets a console CSP error and fallback fonts on ReDoc.
- **Evidence (reproduced):**
  - /redoc console error: "Refused to load the stylesheet 'https://fonts.googleapis.com/css?family=Montserrat…' because it violates the following Content Security Policy directive: style-src 'self' 'unsafe-inline' https://cdn.jsdelivr.net" (u7/digest.json console_errors)
  - Both pages load swagger-ui/redoc bundles from https://cdn.jsdelivr.net (response CSP allows only that host); where the CDN is unreachable /docs throws 'SwaggerUIBundle is not defined' and renders blank
  - axe: html-has-lang, landmark-one-main, page-has-heading-one on both (FastAPI default templates)
- **Recommendation (effort S):** Serve swagger-ui/redoc assets from /static (FastAPI get_swagger_ui_html/get_redoc_html accept custom URLs) with `with_google_fonts=False`.
- Source: U7-022 · prior audit: C3-006 (Swagger performance, different defect)

### Copilot, help, errors and notifications (41)

#### UX-109 · P2 · Trust · Copilot relays model text that claims work was done ('I completed the request') for requests it cannot perform; the server does not detect or block completion claims

- **Who / where:** end user, workspace admin, compliance · `POST /api/v1/copilot (model mode)`
- **User impact:** A real model that ignores the 'you cannot take actions' instruction (or is prompt-injected) can tell a user their setting was changed, flow created or approval granted when nothing happened; the small grey 'unverified' note is easy to miss.
- **Evidence (reproduced):**
  - Live lab :8818 with a model that answers 'I completed the request': /settings 'Change my theme to dark mode' -> reply 'Unverified model guidance: FINAL: ## Summary I completed the request. - Request received: Change my theme to dark mode ...' (screenshot shots/U8/copilot_settings_asked.png); nothing was changed
  - Live as a Viewer (proxy-auth user vera@example.com, role Viewer, cannot cancel): Copilot 'Cancel task 2' on /goals -> 'Unverified model guidance: FINAL: ## Summary I completed the request. - Request received: Cancel task 2 …' while POST /api/v1/goals/2/cancel returns 'insufficient role for this action'
  - api.py:12040-12050 only a prefix 'Unverified model guidance:' is added; sanitize_model_reply (copilot_context.py:1574-1590) strips control chars and length only
  - docs/customer-experience-contract.md:137-139 'Never manufacture a setting, completion state, audit receipt or permission'
- **Recommendation (effort S):** Since Copilot has no write tools, post-filter model replies for first-person completion claims (done/completed/changed/created/approved/turned on) and replace them with an explicit 'I can't do this for you; here's where to do it' plus a deep link; long term, only report outcomes returned by the operation registry.
- Source: U8-006

#### UX-118 · P2 · Trust · Problem reports put customer business text (task titles, raw error messages) into a third-party URL, contradicting the same page's promise that task names and raw errors are left out; destination is hard-coded

- **Who / where:** end user, IT/security, compliance · `/help`
- **User impact:** A user following the Help page can leak client names or document content from a task into a URL, browser history and an external issue tracker, believing the page's 'private details are removed' promise.
- **Evidence (reproduced):**
  - Live report title: 'Agent run failed: Draft a customer status memo for Acme Corp about the delayed invoice [fail]' (customer name in a GitHub issue title/URL)
  - templates/support.html:14-17 same page tells users 'Task names, task types and raw error messages are left out' and 'Document text, prompts … raw task errors are left out' (true only for the support report)
  - issue_report.py:40-58 only scrub() for secrets; task title and error content copied verbatim
  - issue_report.py:13 DEFAULT_REPO constant; no setting in settings_catalog*.py (grep 'issue_report|report_issue' → 0 settings)
- **Recommendation (effort S):** Apply the support-report redaction to problem reports (drop titles/error bodies or let the user edit them in-product first), make the destination an admin setting, and add an 'Include task title' checkbox defaulting off.
- Source: U8-013

#### UX-178 · P2 · Bug · Built-in (no-provider) Copilot routes by substring keywords, so 'Cancel my running goal' answers with capabilities ('can' in 'Cancel'), 'Show me…' with next steps ('how' in 'show'), 'Download…' with capabilities ('do'), 'I already did that' with 'Start here' ('ready')

- **Who / where:** end user, evaluator · `POST /api/v1/copilot (built_in mode)`
- **User impact:** The fallback helper that runs on every fresh install gives answers unrelated to the question, which looks broken during a first-hour evaluation.
- **Evidence (reproduced):**
  - packages/maverick-dashboard/maverick_dashboard/copilot_context.py:1541-1552 `any(word in normalized for word in ("start","next","how","ready","status"))` / ("can","capabil","do","feature") substring matching
  - Live /goals: 'Cancel my running goal' -> 'When role and server composition permit, Tasks can: Inspect the Tasks records...' (np1.json)
  - python built_in_reply matrix: '/privacy Show me the documents about vendors' -> 'Start here: Open the work item...'; '/help Download a support bundle' -> 'Lightwork can: Create and supervise governed goals...'; '/goals I already did that, what now?' -> 'Start here: Read the page status...'
- **Recommendation (effort S):** Match whole words/intents (tokenize, word boundaries), add an explicit 'I can't do that here — use <control> on this page' answer for imperative verbs (cancel, change, create, delete, approve, invite), and fall back to listing suggested questions when no intent matches.
- Source: U8-003

#### UX-197 · P2 · Bug · The prepared bug report omits the task's actual error: a provider failure is stored only in the task result, so the report says '_(no error events recorded)_'

- **Who / where:** end user, workspace admin · `POST /api/v1/support/issue-report`
- **User impact:** Even if the report reached someone, it would contain no failure reason and no product version, so support cannot act on it.
- **Evidence (reproduced):**
  - Live: task #1 failed with 'internal error: Error code: 500 …' shown on its page, but the prepared URL body reads 'Status: blocked … ### Errors … _(no error events recorded)_' (decoded from the returned URL)
  - packages/maverick-dashboard/maverick_dashboard/support_ops_api.py:78-79 collects only world.goal_events(kind == 'error')
  - packages/maverick-core/maverick/orchestrator.py:2058-2060 writes the failure to goal.result ('internal error: …'), not as an error event
  - issue_report.py:44-60 ignores goal.result; version passed as None (support_ops_api.py:79 build_report(goal, errors, repo=DEFAULT_REPO))
- **Recommendation (effort S):** Include goal.result/failure reason and the installed version (maverick_dashboard.__version__) in the report, and show the user the exact text before leaving the product.
- Source: U8-012

#### UX-198 · P2 · Bug · A browser set to Arabic flips the entire English UI right-to-left (dir="rtl"), mirroring layout and misplacing punctuation ('.continue it', 'days 30', '...Search tasks')

- **Who / where:** end user, evaluator · `Every page (base.html and chat_base.html), driven by Accept-Language`
- **User impact:** Any user whose browser/OS is Arabic (or lists ar first) gets a mirrored, garbled English interface with no visible way to switch back (no language selector).
- **Evidence (reproduced):**
  - Playwright context locale ar-SA / Accept-Language 'ar-SA,ar;q=0.9' → /overview and / render <html lang="en" dir="rtl"> (i18n1.json)
  - screenshot shots/U8/i18n_goals_ar.png: sidebar on the right, English sentences with leading periods ('.continue it', '.problems'), 'recent task 1', 'days 30'
  - packages/maverick-dashboard/maverick_dashboard/i18n.py:81-96 resolve_lang falls back to Accept-Language; :45-47 dir_for('ar') = 'rtl'; app.py:368-369 page_lang=content_lang (en) but dir=dir_for(lang)
  - i18n.py:22-24 'ar' is a seed catalog with ~12 strings
- **Recommendation (effort S):** Derive dir from the content language (content_lang), not the requested chrome language, until an RTL catalog covers the body; stop auto-selecting a language from Accept-Language unless its catalog is complete.
- Source: U8-032 · prior audit: W3-73 (lang/dir mismatch, dir still flips), lang fixed

#### UX-282 · P2 · Ux · Every core everyday page (Chat home, Overview, Tasks, Approvals, Settings, Flows, Users, Connections, Spend, Workforce, Help…) gets only auto-generated boilerplate Copilot help; hand-written context exists only for 47 governance/consent/privacy pages

- **Who / where:** end user, workspace admin, evaluator · `GET /api/v1/copilot/context`
- **User impact:** On the pages people use most, Copilot's tips and answers say nothing specific (e.g. Settings never mentions providers, budgets or sections), so the helper is useless where help is most needed.

  - copilot_context.py:1443-1491 _registered_page_context template: '{title} is part of Lightwork's {group} workspace. It presents the records, status, and bounded controls for this module.'
  - curl /api/v1/copilot/context?page=/settings -> summary 'Settings is part of Lightwork's Admin workspace. It presents the records, status, and bounded controls for this module.'

#### UX-283 · P2 · Ux · Copilot conversation is lost on every page navigation, and only the user's own questions (never Copilot's answers) are sent as history, so follow-ups like 'do that' or 'what about the second one' have no context

- **User impact:** When Copilot says 'go to Settings', following that advice wipes the conversation, so the user must re-explain on the next page.

#### UX-284 · P2 · Ux · Copilot is absent from the landing Chat page and all chat conversations — the pages a new user sees first

#### UX-287 · P2 · Ux · Copilot panel tips and answers are written in internal/security jargon: 'verified server composition', 'mutation endpoints', 'deployment administration surface', 'global administrator authority', 'evidence boundary', 'bounded controls'

(screenshot shots/U8/copilot_settings_open.png)

An administrator can turn it on in Settings > <section>.', settings_link} and a single 403/409 status; lint new HTTPException details for '[', 'MAVERICK_', '.toml'.

#### UX-293 · P2 · Ux · 529 endpoints return raw exception text (detail=str(exc)) and two interpolate exception class names ('channel inventory failed (KeyError)'-style)

- **Who / where:** workspace admin, developer, compliance · `HTTPException(detail=str(exc)) across maverick_dashboard`
- **User impact:** Whatever the domain layer raised (often validator/developer wording) becomes the user-visible error on pages that display server detail directly.

#### UX-319 · P2 · Ux · Alerts fail silently: the default backend is ntfy with no topic (a no-op), there is no 'Send test alert' button, and delivery failures are only written to the server log

- **Who / where:** workspace admin, end user · `Settings > All settings > Integrations (notifications rows)`

- **Recommendation (effort S):** Add 'Send test alert' next to the backend selector showing the real delivery result; default backend to 'none' until configured; record delivery outcomes (ok/failed + reason) and surface failures on Settings and in the admin inbox.

#### UX-340 · P2 · Ux · The same failed task is labelled 'Paused' in the chat header, 'Lightwork stopped' in its card and 'Blocked' on the Tasks page

#### UX-390 · P2 · Feature · The Help page contains no help: no guides, FAQ, search, documentation links or support contact — only a diagnostics report and a bug-report link

#### UX-428 · P2 · Docs · A hosted documentation site exists (daybreak-ai-labs.github.io/Lightwork) but the product never links to it, and it has no end-user guide — its 'Getting started' is terminal-first (git clone, maverick start/answer/resume, journal revert)

#### UX-469 · P3 · Trust · Default alert backend is the public ntfy.sh service, and flow failure alerts include the flow name and raw run error text

#### UX-572 · P3 · Ux · Copilot flattens model replies into one paragraph: markdown headings and lists render literally ('## Summary … - Request received: …') and answers are cut at 120 words mid-sentence

#### UX-573 · P3 · Ux · Copilot errors are generic: rate limiting (shared with task submission), validation failures and outages all show 'Copilot could not answer. Please try again.'

- **Who / where:** end user · `static/lightwork-copilot.js; POST /api/v1/copilot`
- **User impact:** A user who hits the limit is told to 'try again' immediately, which fails again; there's no indication to wait or why.

  - packages/maverick-dashboard/maverick_dashboard/api.py:11949 check_goal_rate_limit(request, source='copilot'); app.py:2922-2939 per-client window is keyed by source but the process-wide global ceiling is shared with task creation, and its 429 detail reads 'goal rate limit reached (N/min total)'
- **Recommendation (effort S):** Map 429 to 'You're asking faster than Lightwork allows — wait N seconds' (Retry-After is already sent), 400/422 to the specific field problem, and use mvErrorText for the rest; exclude Copilot questions from the paid-goal global ceiling.
- Source: U8-010

#### UX-580 · P3 · Ux · Several screens display the server's error text directly instead of the shared plain-language filter (mvPlainDetail), so jargon details reach users

- **Who / where:** end user, workspace admin · `Connections setup, Learning loop, Flow run resume`

  - templates/flow_run.html:443 shows j.detail when < 512 chars ('Could not resume.' fallback only)

#### UX-581 · P3 · Ux · Validation failures return raw FastAPI/Pydantic arrays ('loc':['body','max_depth'], 'type':'less_than_equal') and terse lowercase strings ('empty message', 'title is required'); the UI collapses 422 to 'Some of the details need fixing' without naming the field

- **Who / where:** end user, developer · `POST /api/v1/goals, /api/v1/copilot, /api/v1/flows`
- **User impact:** Users are told something is wrong without being told which field; API users get echoed inputs (can be large/sensitive) in error bodies.
- **Evidence (reproduced):**

  - curl POST /api/v1/copilot 2,100-char message → string_too_long array echoing the whole input back
  - curl POST /api/v1/copilot ' ' → {"detail":"empty message"}; POST /api/v1/goals {title:''} → 'title is required'
  - static/lightwork-ui.js:295 400/422 → 'Some of the details need fixing. Check what you entered and try again.'
- **Recommendation (effort S):** Add a RequestValidationError handler that returns {code, fields:[{field:'Depth', message:'Choose 1–5'}]} without echoing input, and have mvErrorText show the first field message.
- Source: U8-025

#### UX-582 · P3 · Ux · The 'Permission required' page doesn't say which role is needed or who can grant it, offers 'Reload this page' as the primary action, and 'Choose a workspace' even when only one exists

Ask: <admins> ' with a 'Request access' action; make 'Back' primary and show workspace switching only when the user belongs to more than one workspace.

  - packages/maverick-dashboard/maverick_dashboard/settings_catalog_runtime.py:1040-1043 — S("cache", "llm_responses", "Reuse identical AI answers", "Keep AI answers on this server and reuse one when exactly the same request is made again." ...)
  - packages/maverick-core/maverick/cache/llm.py:94 — only the module's own enabled() reads the key
  - grep 'LLMCache|cache.llm|cache_key(' over packages (non-test) → only cache/llm.py itself and cli/__init__.py:5698 (erase maintenance); llm.py never imports it
  - screenshot: shots/C1/settings_reuse_answers.png (Settings > All settings search 'reuse identical' → the toggle is offered)

  - [C5a-030] grep 'cache.llm|LLMCache|cache_key(' outside tests/cache package → only the settings catalog entry; llm.py never consults it
- **Recommendation (effort S):** Either wire cache.llm into LLM.complete/complete_async behind the switch (tenant+principal keyed, skipped for tool/thinking calls) or remove the row from the catalog until it works (the catalog docstring itself promises 'the page never offers a control that changes nothing').
