#### UX-359 · P2 · Customization · Notifications are a single deployment-wide destination; people cannot choose how or about what they are notified

- **Who / where:** end user, workspace admin · `[notifications] (Settings > Integrations > 'Send finished-task alerts with')`
- **User impact:** Every finished task in the workspace goes to one ntfy topic or Slack channel; an individual cannot ask to be emailed when *their* task needs an answer, or mute routine completions.
- **Evidence (reproduced):**
  - packages/maverick-core/maverick/notifications.py:13 — backend = "ntfy" # ntfy | pushover | discord | slack | none (one config section)
  - notifications.py:179-207 — notify() picks backends from config (or an explicit override); no principal/user parameter
  - Settings catalog notification rows (backend, ntfy_topic, ntfy_server, slack_webhook, discord_webhook, batch_window_seconds, batch_max, user_key) are all deployment-wide; grep 'notification_pref|per_user' → 0
  - [U8-029] Live /account shows only role/permissions/tool limits — no preferences of any kind (pages1.json; shots/U8/page_account.png)
  - [U8-029] settings_catalog.py:866-888 single global [notifications] backend/topic/webhook, admin-only (settings_all_page requires global admin)
  - [U8-029] packages/maverick-core/maverick/notifications.py:201-208 one backend list from config for every event
- **Recommendation (effort L):** A per-user Notifications page (/account/notifications): channels (email, Slack DM, Teams, push), events (my task finished / needs my answer / approval assigned to me / failures) and quiet hours; keep the current section as the workspace broadcast default.
- Source: C1-030, U8-029

#### UX-360 · P2 · Customization · Invite links always expire after 7 days; no admin choice and the UI copy hard-codes '7 days'

- **Who / where:** workspace admin, IT/security · `/users invite form`
- **User impact:** Security teams that require 24-72 h invite links cannot shorten them; admins inviting people who are away cannot lengthen them and must re-invite.
- **Evidence (code-verified):**
  - packages/maverick-dashboard/maverick_dashboard/invites.py:39 — INVITE_TTL_HOURS = 7 * 24
  - packages/maverick-dashboard/maverick_dashboard/invites.py:234 — create(..., ttl_hours: float = INVITE_TTL_HOURS); grep 'ttl_hours' in dashboard/CLI → no caller passes it
  - packages/maverick-dashboard/maverick_dashboard/templates/users.html:117,120,124 — 'It works once and expires in 7 days.'
  - Contrast: session length after acceptance IS configurable ([dashboard] invite_session_days, catalog row 'Stay signed in after an invitation')
- **Recommendation (effort S):** Add [dashboard] invite_link_hours (1-720, default 168) next to invite_session_days on Settings > People & access, offer a per-invite 'Expires in' select on /users, and render the actual expiry in the copy.
- Source: C1-005

#### UX-361 · P2 · Customization · 'What agents call you' is one deployment-wide name: every person in a team is addressed by the installer's name

- **Who / where:** end user, workspace admin · `[persona] user_name (Settings > AI models > 'What agents call you'; consumer wizard Q1)`
- **User impact:** Once a second person is invited, agents greet and address them by the administrator's name (e.g. every colleague is told 'Sure, Chris'); users have no personal place to set their own name or tone.
- **Evidence (code-verified):**
  - packages/maverick-core/maverick/persona.py:41-51 — load_persona() reads load_config()['persona'] (deployment/tenant config, no principal)
  - packages/maverick-core/maverick/persona.py:76-77 — adds 'The person you work for likes to be called {user_name}.' to every agent's system prompt (agent.py:130-131)
  - apps/installer-cli/maverick_installer/wizard.py:9443 — consumer setup writes persona={..., "user_name": user_name} from the installer's first answer
  - Settings catalog row: persona user_name 'What agents call you' (group AI models) — a global value
- **Recommendation (effort M):** Move 'What agents call you' (and optional personal style/addendum) to a per-user Profile page (/account) keyed by principal, falling back to the identity provider's display name; keep [persona] name/style/addendum as workspace defaults.
- Source: C1-024

#### UX-363 · P2 · Customization · All Settings changes are deployment-wide: there is no in-product way to customize one workspace (tenant overlay is file-only)

- **Who / where:** workspace admin, IT/security, compliance · `/settings/all, /settings (models, budget, permissions)`
- **User impact:** In a deployment serving several departments or client workspaces, an admin cannot give one workspace a different safety level, persona, retention period, model or budget from the product; the only route is hand-editing a TOML file on the server, which the customer experience contract rules out.
- **Evidence (code-verified):**
  - packages/maverick-core/maverick/config.py:368-370 — dashboard_overrides_path() = config_path().parent / dashboard-config.toml (one global file)
  - packages/maverick-dashboard/maverick_dashboard/settings_store.py:698-712 — _write() always writes config.dashboard_overrides_path()
  - packages/maverick-core/maverick/config.py:470-480 — the per-workspace layer tenants/<t>/config.toml exists in the merge order but settings_store/api only READ it (settings_store.py:749, 1907; api.py:8392) — no dashboard writer
  - packages/maverick-core/maverick/runtime_overrides.py:33 — OVERRIDES_PATH = data_dir("runtime-overrides.toml") resolved once at import, so dashboard model pins, allowed-model list, per-task budget cap and denied tools are process-global too (also map/02 §6.5)
  - [U5-039] ui_visibility: /settings scope 'global'; All settings _sources uses base config, dashboard overlay and operator overlay only (packages/maverick-dashboard/maverick_dashboard/settings_all_page.py:64-86)
  - [U5-039] maverick-core/maverick/config.py:550-561 load_config merges tenants/<t>/config.toml last (highest precedence) — map/12 D7
  - [U5-039] per-workspace UI limited to /tenants/{id}/features (plan feature overrides) and the daily limit
  - [U5-038] catalog row providers.per_tenant_keys 'Let each workspace use its own AI service key' (settings_catalog_runtime.py:~296) — help: 'A workspace that has its own key for an AI service uses it instead of the shared one.'
  - [U5-038] grep tenant_config_path packages/maverick-dashboard/maverick_dashboard → only readers (settings_store.py:749,1907; webhook_settings.py:75; api.py:8392); no writer of tenants/<id>/config.toml
  - [U5-038] /tenants row actions are only Plan, Daily limit, Features, Pause, Remove
- **Recommendation (effort L):** Add a workspace scope selector to Settings > All settings ("All workspaces / This workspace") that writes the tenant overlay through the same validated serializer, shows inherited vs overridden values, and resolve runtime-overrides per tenant at call time.
- Source: C1-018, U5-039, U5-038 · prior audit: map/12 D7

#### UX-364 · P2 · Customization · Browser session lifetime is hard-coded (OIDC 12 h, SAML 8 h) and there is no idle timeout at all

- **Who / where:** IT/security, compliance · `/auth/callback (OIDC), SAML ACS, all signed-in pages`
- **User impact:** Enterprises with a policy such as '15-minute idle lock, 8-hour absolute session' cannot meet it; SAML and OIDC users of the same workspace get different session lengths without explanation.
- **Evidence (code-verified):**
  - packages/maverick-dashboard/maverick_dashboard/oidc_login.py:71 — _SESSION_TTL = 12 * 3600 (used :518, :537)
  - packages/maverick-dashboard/maverick_dashboard/saml.py:43 — _SESSION_TTL = 8 * 60 * 60 # 8h, matching the OIDC browser session (it does not match: OIDC is 12 h)
  - grep -ri 'idle' in maverick_dashboard/*.py → only repl_ops_api (REPL sessions) and world_model idle_tx_timeout; no dashboard idle sign-out
  - Settings catalog has no session_hours/idle row (lk.py 'session' → only invite_session_days)
- **Recommendation (effort M):** Add [dashboard] session_hours (absolute) and idle_minutes knobs shared by OIDC, SAML and invite sessions, with a client-side idle warning; expose on Settings > People & access > 'Sign-in sessions' and in the wizard's OIDC/SAML step.
- Source: C1-006 · prior audit: W2-22 (still present at HEAD)

#### UX-366 · P2 · Customization · Outbound webhooks are one flat URL list with one secret: no per-endpoint event selection, headers or payload format

- **Who / where:** developer, workspace admin · `[webhooks] outbound / Settings > Integrations`
- **User impact:** An integrator who wants only 'goal finished' events in Slack and only approval events in ServiceNow must filter on the receiver; tools that expect a specific JSON shape (Teams cards, PagerDuty) need a relay service.
- **Evidence (code-verified):**
  - packages/maverick-core/maverick/webhooks.py:102-112 — _load_config_outbound() returns list(section.get("outbound")) and one secret
  - packages/maverick-core/maverick/webhooks.py:248-253 — every event is sent to every URL as the fixed envelope {"v":1, "event", "ts", "payload"}
  - grep 'payload_template|body_template' in maverick/webhooks.py → 0
- **Recommendation (effort M):** Model outbound webhooks as named endpoints ([[webhooks.endpoints]] url, events[], secret, headers, optional Jinja-sandboxed body template) managed on a Settings > Integrations > Webhooks page with a 'send test event' button.
- Source: C1-022

#### UX-493 · P3 · Bug · 'Levels of helpers under a task' setting (1-10) is ignored for REST API tasks: the API defaults to 3 and never exceeds 5

#### UX-663 · P3 · Customization · Theme choice lives only in a browser cookie and custom themes are an admin TOML table of 8 hex colours

### Market feature gaps (19)

#### UX-367 · P2 · Feature · Partial: role-based access -- custom roles can only combine four permission atoms (admin, operate, audit, view)

- **Who / where:** IT/security, workspace admin, compliance · `/users, rbac.py`
- **User impact:** Security teams cannot create an approver who cannot start work, a flow author who cannot touch connections, or a manager who can see analytics but not transcripts; they must over-grant 'operate' or 'admin'.
- **Evidence (code-verified):**
  - packages/maverick-dashboard/maverick_dashboard/rbac.py:28-35 -- 'every permission a custom role can hold is one of the same four atoms'; PERMISSION_ATOMS = admin, audit, operate, view
  - packages/maverick-dashboard/maverick_dashboard/rbac.py:81-84 -- operator = run/cancel goals, approve, tools (one bundle)
  - cmd: count of require_permission(request, X) -> operate 665, view 403, admin 146, audit 74
  - packages/maverick-dashboard/maverick_dashboard/auth.py:636-657 -- department (suite) scoping exists as a separate filter
  - competitor: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-copilot-studio/analytics-overview (fetched) -- Analytics Viewer and Bot Transcript Viewer roles
  - competitor (search snippet): support.claude.com roles -- 'Admins define groups, roles, and capabilities to govern exactly which people can use which products and connectors'
- **Recommendation (effort L):** Split atoms into business permissions (approve, author_agents, author_flows, manage_connections, manage_channels, view_spend, view_transcripts, export_audit) and add a role builder in Users with an effective-permission preview.
- Source: C2-025

#### UX-368 · P2 · Feature · Missing: a test chat for a specialist inside the Agent Factory editor (try it before saving)

  - competitor: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-copilot-studio/publication-fundamentals-publish-channels (fetched) -- 'Use the test chat (the Test agent panel) while you're building your agent'

#### UX-371 · P2 · Feature · Partial: approvals are not routed to the assigned approver outside the dashboard (email/Teams/Slack/mobile)

  - cmd: grep 'ops_alert' callers -> external_agents.py:1373, killswitch.py:223, provider_cost_cap.py:1797 only
  - competitor: https://www.salesforce.com/agentforce/observability/ (fetched) -- 'near real-time alerts on key metrics that agent admins can use to execute immediate, targeted interventions'
- **Recommendation (effort M):** Alert rules on failure rate, thumbs-down rate, approval backlog age, daily spend per specialist; deliver to email/Slack/Teams with a link to the filtered runs.
- Source: C2-011

#### UX-678 · P3 · Feature · Missing: webhook events for approval requested/decided and agent questions

### Integrations, API and developer experience (41)

#### UX-100 · P2 · Trust · Email channel accepts any message whose From header is on the list unless SPF/DKIM explicitly failed (no DMARC/alignment), so a spoofed From can drive the agent

- **Who / where:** IT/security, workspace admin · `packages/maverick-channels/maverick_channels/email.py`
- **User impact:** Anyone who can deliver mail to the agent's inbox with a forged From of an allowed colleague (e.g. via a relay that adds no Authentication-Results) can start work under that colleague's identity.
- **Evidence (code-verified):**
  - packages/maverick-channels/maverick_channels/email.py:168-220 — _authentication_verdict rejects only an explicit spf/dkim 'fail'; missing, neutral or unrelated-domain pass is accepted
  - email.py:364-367 — From allowlist check; topmost Authentication-Results trusted unless EMAIL_TRUSTED_AUTHSERV_ID is set (map/14a D9)
  - /channels Email card has no field for the trusted authserv-id (settings_store.py:356-364)
  - [C5c-107] packages/maverick-channels/maverick_channels/email.py:364-367 — rejects only an explicit 'fail' verdict before the From-header allowlist
  - [C5c-107] map 14a D9: topmost Authentication-Results trusted unless EMAIL_TRUSTED_AUTHSERV_ID is set (168-210)
- **Recommendation (effort M):** Require dmarc=pass with From alignment (or dkim=pass aligned) by default, expose 'trusted mail server' (authserv-id) on the Email card, and log refused senders on the page.
- Source: C3-035, C5c-107

#### UX-101 · P2 · Trust · Voice channel lets any caller with the webhook bearer drive the agent: the caller allowlist is optional, contradicting the 'per-sender allowlist, default-deny' promise

- **Who / where:** IT/security, workspace admin · `packages/maverick-channels/maverick_channels/voice.py`
- **User impact:** Anyone who can phone the Vapi/Retell/Bland number reaches the agent with the operator's tools and budget; admins reading the docs believe callers are restricted.
- **Evidence (code-verified):**
  - packages/maverick-channels/maverick_channels/voice.py:116-122 — 'Empty = allow any authenticated caller (bearer still required)'
  - packages/maverick-channels/maverick_channels/__init__.py:9-11 — package doc claims each adapter requires a per-sender allowlist, default-deny (map/14a D10)
  - packages/maverick-channels/tests/test_channel_authz.py:484-501 asserts the allow-any behaviour
  - [C5c-108] packages/maverick-channels/maverick_channels/voice.py:116-122 — 'Empty = allow any authenticated caller'
  - [C5c-108] map 14a D10: packages/maverick-channels/maverick_channels/__init__.py:9-11 says per-sender allowlist, default-deny
- **Recommendation (effort S):** Make VOICE_ALLOWED_CALLERS required like every other adapter (fail to start without it), or require an explicit allow_any_caller=true opt-in shown as a warning on /channels.
- Source: C3-047, C5c-108

#### UX-127 · P2 · Trust · Goals started over MCP (and A2A/REST) are uncapped by default, and maverick_resume advertises only goal_id although it honours max_dollars/max_wall_seconds/max_depth

- **Who / where:** developer, workspace admin · `lightwork mcp tools maverick_start / maverick_resume`
- **User impact:** An IDE assistant calling maverick_start without max_dollars can run an unbounded paid swarm; MCP clients cannot discover that resume accepts limits, so resumed runs also go uncapped.
- **Evidence (reproduced):**
  - packages/maverick-mcp/maverick_mcp/server.py:153-175 — _task_budget: caller value, else [mcp] max_dollars / MAVERICK_MCP_MAX_DOLLARS, else resolve_budget_caps() → None when nothing configured
  - cmd (lab env): configured_max_dollars() → None; budget_from_config() → max_dollars None (see C3-001)
  - cmd: stdio tools/list → maverick_resume inputSchema properties ['goal_id'] only; map/14a D14: _tool_resume reads max_dollars, max_wall_seconds, max_depth (server.py:1653-1658)
  - packages/maverick-dashboard/maverick_dashboard/settings_catalog_runtime.py:1610-1709 — [mcp] max_dollars exists only as an advanced setting, default empty
- **Recommendation (effort S):** Ship a non-empty default per-goal cap for machine callers ([mcp]/[a2a]/[api] max_dollars, shown in Settings > Spending limits), declare the resume limit arguments in its inputSchema, and echo the effective limits in structuredContent.
- Source: C3-046 · prior audit: W5-109 (related default-cap drift)

#### UX-169 · P2 · Bug · Turning on sign-in (OIDC) silently breaks every chat channel: each message is refused with 'Authentication failed: OIDC token is missing or invalid'

- **Who / where:** IT/security, end user, workspace admin · `Channel handler with [auth.oidc] enabled`
- **User impact:** An IT admin who enables corporate SSO for the dashboard unknowingly cuts off every Slack/Teams-style user; nothing on the Channels page warns about the conflict.
- **Evidence (code-verified):**
  - packages/maverick-core/maverick/server.py:213-221 — when oidc_enabled(), principal must come from verify_oidc_token(_extract_oidc_token(msg)); otherwise returns '⚠ Authentication failed: OIDC token is missing or invalid.'
  - packages/maverick-core/maverick/server.py:991-1026 — _extract_oidc_token reads msg.id_token / msg.raw headers
  - packages/maverick-channels/maverick_channels/delivery.py:138-150,433-434 — the handler receives an IncomingMessage rebuilt from the journal with raw=None; no adapter sets id_token (map/14a D8)
  - [C5c-106] packages/maverick-core/maverick/server.py:991-1000 — OIDC token read from msg.id_token/oidc_token or raw headers
  - [C5c-106] grep id_token in packages/maverick-channels → 0 adapters set it
  - [C5c-106] packages/maverick-channels/maverick_channels/delivery.py:140-150 — handler receives an IncomingMessage rebuilt from the journal payload
  - [C5c-106] map 14a D8: server.py:213-221 replies '⚠ Authentication failed…'
- **Recommendation (effort L):** Map channel identities to directory principals (e.g. Slack user → verified email → OIDC subject via SCIM) instead of requiring a per-message ID token; until then show a blocking warning on /channels and in readiness when OIDC is on.
- Source: C3-030, C5c-106

#### UX-258 · P2 · Reliability · Remote MCP tool servers using OAuth start failing mid-task when the access token expires: the bearer is fetched once at connect and never refreshed

- **Who / where:** developer, workspace admin, end user · `/mcp 'Another online tool server' with OAuth; [mcp_servers.<name>] oauth`
- **User impact:** Long goals that use an OAuth-protected tool server (e.g. a hosted CRM MCP) start getting 401 errors once the token's TTL (often 1 h) passes; the agent reports tool failures the admin cannot explain.
- **Evidence (code-verified):**
  - packages/maverick-core/maverick/mcp_client.py:1049-1056 — _bearer() docstring promises 'fetched + cached + refreshed'
  - mcp_client.py:1067-1074 — bearer read once in start() and baked into httpx.AsyncClient default headers
  - mcp_client.py:1088-1099 — per-request _headers() adds session id/protocol version but never re-reads the token (map/14b D7)
  - [C5c-117] packages/maverick-core/maverick/mcp_client.py:1072 — Authorization header set once in start()
  - [C5c-117] packages/maverick-core/maverick/mcp_client.py:1088-1099 — _headers() never refreshes it (docstring 159-162 promises refresh)
- **Recommendation (effort S):** Resolve the bearer per request in _headers() via provider.token() (which already caches/refreshes), and retry once on 401 after forcing a refresh.
- Source: C3-053, C5c-117

#### UX-259 · P2 · Reliability · Outbound webhook delivery is fire-once: no retry/backoff, no delivery log, no 'send test' button, and unsigned by default

- **Who / where:** developer, workspace admin · `Settings > All settings > 'Send task events to these addresses'`
- **User impact:** A receiver outage of a few seconds silently loses 'goal finished' events forever; admins have no screen showing what was sent, what failed, or a way to redeliver.
- **Evidence (code-verified):**
  - packages/maverick-core/maverick/webhooks.py:194-227 — _post makes one client.post; non-2xx or exception is only log.warning'd
  - webhooks.py:285-294 — in-flight cap reached → 'dropping dispatch' (event lost)
  - packages/maverick-dashboard/maverick_dashboard/settings_catalog.py:889-893 — setting copy 'receive a signed message' although signing needs a separately set secret (webhooks.py:274-282 signs only 'if secret')
  - cmd: GET /settings/webhooks → {configured:false, outbound_configured:false, ownership:'No signing secret is active.'} on a fresh install
- **Recommendation (effort M):** Persist outbound deliveries in a small journal with exponential retry, show a delivery log with Redeliver/Send test on the webhooks settings card, require (or auto-generate) a signing secret when a URL is added.
- Source: C3-040

#### UX-267 · P2 · Ux · WhatsApp/SMS setup never tells the admin which callback URL to register with Meta/Twilio, and the webhook listeners bind to loopback by default

- **Who / where:** workspace admin · `/channels WhatsApp (Cloud API) and SMS (Twilio) cards`
- **User impact:** The admin cannot complete Meta's or Twilio's webhook form from the product; even with the right URL, the provider cannot reach a loopback listener without an undocumented reverse proxy.

  - grep 'whatsapp-cloud|/webhook/sms|public_base_url' templates/channels.html plain_labels.py → 0 hits
  - map/14a adapters table: whatsapp_cloud serves /webhook/whatsapp-cloud; whatsapp/sms FastAPI+Twilio 'loopback bind by default'; Twilio signature uses [channels] public_base_url (ch/base.py:75-100)
- **Recommendation (effort M):** Show the exact callback URL (from [channels] public_base_url, editable on the card) with a copy button and a reachability self-test; explain the tunnel/proxy requirement in-product.
- Source: C3-051

#### UX-275 · P2 · Ux · CLI top-level help is one flat alphabetical list of 166 commands with no grouping, and its 'New here?' footer tells `lightwork` users to run `maverick …`

- **Who / where:** developer, evaluator, workspace admin · `lightwork --help`
- **User impact:** A new CLI user cannot find the dozen everyday commands among 166 governance/ML/finance entries, and is told to type a different program name than the one they installed and ran.
- **Evidence (reproduced):**
  - cmd: lightwork --help → 184 lines, 'Commands:' lists a2a … workforce-graduation alphabetically (Click introspection: 166 top-level, 445 leaf commands)
  - same output footer: 'New here? Start with these four: maverick init / maverick start "..." / maverick chat / maverick doctor'
  - cmd: lightwork answer 999 x → 'No such question #999. See open questions with `maverick status`.'; lightwork resume --goal-id 999 → 'See `maverick status`.'; lightwork start → 'Answer with: maverick answer <id> …'
  - root help text: 'Lightwork: multi-agent swarm for long-horizon work.' (not the governed-workforce positioning)
- **Recommendation (effort M):** Use a click Group subclass with sections (Everyday, Setup & health, Governance, Compliance, Finance, Advanced/Operator) and hide rarely used groups behind `lightwork help --all`; render the invoked program name (ctx.find_root().info_name) in footers and error hints.
- Source: C3-018

#### UX-276 · P2 · Ux · CLI output/flag conventions are inconsistent: only 58 of 445 commands support --json, and list limits are spelled --limit, -n/--limit, -n/--num, --top, --count, --max

- **Who / where:** developer · `lightwork status|history|doctor|version|cost|logs|ps|spend`
- **User impact:** Scripts and CI jobs cannot reliably parse status/history/doctor output and must learn per-command flag spellings and exit codes.
- **Evidence (reproduced):**
  - Click introspection: --json on 58 of 445 leaf commands; --format on 16
  - limit flags: --limit 33, --top 5, -n 4, --num 2, --count 1, --max 1
  - cmd: lightwork status --help → only --cost (no --json); history → --limit only; doctor/version → no --json; ps → -n,--limit --json; logs → -n,--num; cost → --csv
  - exit codes differ for the same 'not found' situation: lightwork answer 999 x → rc 1; lightwork resume --goal-id 999 → rc 2
- **Recommendation (effort M):** Add a global --output {text,json} (or --json) on the root group honoured by every read command, standardise on --limit/-n, and document exit codes (0 ok, 1 failure, 2 usage/not-found, 3 policy refusal) in `lightwork help exit-codes`.
- Source: C3-020

#### UX-318 · P2 · Ux · MCP maverick_start returns 'DONE.' plus operator debug text ('[skill distill disabled: set MAVERICK_AUTO_DISTILL=1 to enable]', '[tokens in=… hit_rate=… $=…]') inside the answer the client shows the user

#### UX-325 · P2 · Ux · API versioning is inconsistent: 62 JSON write endpoints live outside /api/v1 (RPC-style /users/set, /channels/save, /mcp/add, /settings/providers…) plus unversioned /api/goal/{id} duplicates

#### UX-326 · P2 · Ux · Seven different pagination schemes and 83% of GET endpoints have no paging at all

#### UX-327 · P2 · Ux · Goal event stream exposes the internal orchestrator prompt and nonce-wrapped tool frames, and never contains the question text the agent asked

- **Who / where:** developer, end user · `GET /api/v1/goals/{id}/events, /events/stream`

  - same response: kind 'observation' content "tool=ask_user -> <tool_output tool='ask_user' id=6a21bf82b204e47b>\nQUEUED question #1. The user will answer asynchronously…</tool_output 6a21bf82b204e47b>" — the question text itself is only available from GET …/open_questions

- **Recommendation (effort M):** Emit typed, user-facing events (step_started, tool_called{name,summary}, question_asked{question_id,text}, approval_needed, completed{deliverable}) with ISO timestamps; keep raw frames behind a ?detail=debug flag for operators.

#### UX-351 · P2 · Customization · Only 7 of the 17 supported chat channels can be set up in the product; Matrix, Signal, Bluesky, Mastodon, Threads, RCS, iMessage, Voice, IRC and WhatsApp (Twilio) need config.toml/env vars

- **Who / where:** workspace admin · `/channels`
- **User impact:** An admin who reads that Lightwork supports Signal or Matrix finds no way to turn it on without a terminal.

  - packages/maverick-dashboard/maverick_dashboard/settings_store.py:337-373 — CHANNELS: telegram, discord, slack, whatsapp_cloud, sms, email, mattermost
  - packages/maverick-core/maverick/server.py:773-791 — _WIRES has 17 entries (adds signal, matrix, bluesky, mastodon, whatsapp, threads, rcs, imessage, voice, irc)
  - channels page (c3work/ui1.json) shows only the 7 managed cards plus a read-only inventory
- **Recommendation (effort M):** Generate channel cards from one channel registry (fields, help, secret flags, allowlist) shared by server._WIRES, the wizard and settings_store, so every wired channel is configurable in /channels.
- Source: C3-033

#### UX-373 · P2 · Feature · Channel replies are text-only: files the agent produces are never delivered to chat users, because the platform's own handler still returns a bare string (deprecated v1 contract)

- **Who / where:** end user · `Channel reply path`
- **User impact:** A user who asks in Slack for 'the Q3 report as a spreadsheet' gets a text summary and must open the dashboard to fetch the file; threaded replies cannot be used.
- **Evidence (code-verified):**
  - packages/maverick-core/maverick/server.py:198 — async def _handle_message(self, msg) -> str
  - packages/maverick-channels/maverick_channels/base.py:274-287 — as_reply wraps a str into a text-only Reply and calls warn_once('channels.str_handler') (the v1 shim); map/14a D3: remove_in='0.3.0' (core/deprecations.py:56-62)
  - map/14a D13: Reply.attachments / thread_ref are never shipped by any adapter; every saved send uses reply.text only
  - inbound attachments ARE supported (telegram.py:153-233, delivery.py:117-122), so the asymmetry is visible to users
- **Recommendation (effort L):** Return Reply(text, attachments=[deliverables], thread_ref=…) from Server._handle_message and implement file upload per adapter (Slack files.upload v2, Telegram sendDocument, email MIME attachment) under the delivery journal's per-chunk receipts.
- Source: C3-031

#### UX-395 · P2 · Feature · MCP surface cannot cancel a goal, stream its progress, list approvals or pick a specialist; maverick_start blocks until the whole run finishes

- **Who / where:** developer · `lightwork mcp tools/list`
- **User impact:** From Claude Desktop or an IDE a user cannot say 'stop that run', see what the agent is doing, or route work to one of the 2,031 specialist packs — the REST API can do all of these.
- **Evidence (reproduced):**
  - cmd: tools/list → 10 tools; none for cancel, goal events/progress, approvals, specialists/domains, deliverables or spend
  - maverick_start description: 'Returns the final answer after the swarm completes. Long-running.'; input schema has no domain/specialist field (args: title, description, max_dollars, max_wall_seconds, max_depth)
  - packages/maverick-mcp/maverick_mcp/server.py:202-415 — TOOLS catalog; progress only via SSE heartbeats with no content, cancellation only via notifications/cancelled on the in-flight request
  - serverInfo name is 'maverick' and tool prefix 'maverick_' (brand leak into every client's tool picker)
- **Recommendation (effort M):** Add lightwork_cancel, lightwork_goal_events (since cursor), lightwork_approvals_list/decide (governed), and a domain argument on start; rename the server/tool prefix to lightwork_ with maverick_* aliases for one release.
- Source: C3-025

#### UX-411 · P2 · Perf · Every agent build spawns a fresh long-lived Node child for each configured TypeScript plugin and never reaps it until process exit

- **Who / where:** developer, workspace admin, IT/security · `[plugins] ts; dashboard / serve processes`
- **User impact:** On a long-running dashboard with a TS plugin configured, each task (and each sub-agent) that calls the plugin leaves another Node process running, steadily consuming memory until restart.
- **Evidence (code-verified):**
  - packages/maverick-core/maverick/ts_plugin_host.py:329-366 — load_ts_plugin runs --describe and creates a new _PluginChild, appended to module-global _CHILDREN
  - ts_plugin_host.py:290-302 — children closed only by an atexit hook
  - map/03t §2.1/§2.3 + map/14b D4 — base_registry (which loads TS plugins, tools/__init__.py:1710-1726) is rebuilt for every Agent including every spawned child (agent.py:1757,1968)
  - [C5c-116] packages/maverick-core/maverick/ts_plugin_host.py:290-302 — children removed only at atexit
  - [C5c-116] packages/maverick-core/maverick/grpc_plugin_host.py:185-195 — describe() spawns subprocess.Popen
  - [C5c-116] map 14b D4/D5: base_registry() (every agent build) re-describes and appends a new child
- **Recommendation (effort M):** Cache one _PluginChild per pinned command digest (process-wide) and reuse it across registries, with an idle timeout and a health check; expose running plugin processes on /plugins.
- Source: C3-054, C5c-116

#### UX-416 · P2 · Docs · No admin-facing setup guide for any chat channel (Slack scopes/Socket Mode/events, finding user IDs for the allowlist, Telegram group rules); docs/channel-*.md cover delivery internals only

  - packages/maverick-dashboard/maverick_dashboard/plain_labels.py:205-212 — per-channel 'Where do I find these details?' links go to vendor consoles (e.g. https://api.slack.com/apps), not to Lightwork instructions
  - docs/handbook.md:143 — only 'maverick serve # channel server: Telegram/Discord/Slack/...'

#### UX-435 · P2 · Docs · TypeScript plugin SDK is not installable: '@maverick/plugin-sdk' is not on npm (404), its README imports it by that name with no build/link steps, and no CI runs its tests

- **Who / where:** developer · `sdks/plugin-ts`

  - sdks/plugin-ts/package.json — name '@maverick/plugin-sdk' 0.1.0, main dist/index.js (dist not committed)

- **Recommendation (effort S):** Publish the SDK (as @lightwork/plugin-sdk) or document 'npm install <path-to>/sdks/plugin-ts' + build; add a CI job running `npm test`; add a runnable example plugin and a `lightwork plugin new --kind ts-tool` scaffold.

#### UX-443 · P2 · Docs · Idempotency-Key works on POST /api/v1/goals but is documented nowhere (not in OpenAPI for that op, not in docs/api.md)

- **Who / where:** developer · `POST /api/v1/goals`
- **User impact:** Integrators retrying on network timeouts (Zapier, cron, mobile) will double-launch paid goals because they do not know the safe-retry mechanism exists.
- **Evidence (reproduced):**
  - cmd: POST /api/v1/goals with 'Idempotency-Key: abc-1' twice → both 201 Location /api/v1/goals/2, second has 'idempotency-replayed: true'; different body same key → 409 'Submission key already belongs to different content'
  - packages/maverick-dashboard/maverick_dashboard/api.py:1380-1405 — reads Idempotency-Key; GET /api/v1/goal-submissions/receipt reconciles by key (api.py:1487-1509)
  - cmd: header-param census → Idempotency-Key declared on exactly 1 op (/api/v1/security/assurance/gateway/assurance-packet), not on /api/v1/goals
  - grep -n Idempotency docs/api.md → 0 hits
- **Recommendation (effort S):** Declare the Idempotency-Key header parameter and 409 response on POST /api/v1/goals (and every create route that honours it), document retry semantics and the receipt-reconcile endpoint in docs/api.md.
- Source: C3-010

#### UX-444 · P2 · Docs · OpenAPI spec declares no securitySchemes/security, so Swagger UI has no Authorize button and generated clients have no auth

- **Who / where:** developer · `/openapi.json, /docs`
- **User impact:** On any token-protected deployment 'Try it out' in /docs cannot send the bearer, and openapi-generator/kiota clients (recommended in docs/api.md:25-26) come out with no auth configuration.
- **Evidence (reproduced):**
  - cmd: python: json.load(openapi.json) → components keys ['schemas'] only; securitySchemes None; top-level security None
  - Playwright on /docs (rendered in 31.9 s): locator('button.authorize').count() → 0
  - screenshot: shots/C3/docs_top.png
- **Recommendation (effort S):** Declare an HTTP bearer securityScheme (plus OIDC if configured) in app.openapi() and apply it globally, exempting the auth-free probe routes; this also gives Swagger its Authorize dialog.
- Source: C3-004 · prior audit: W2-19 (related: public OpenAPI, recommends Authorize dialog)

#### UX-445 · P2 · Docs · 97% of /api/v1 operations have untyped responses (dict[str,Any] or {}), so the spec cannot drive typed clients

- **Who / where:** developer · `/openapi.json`
- **User impact:** Developers generating SDKs (the docs' recommended path) get Map<String,Object>/any for nearly every call, must reverse-engineer payloads by trial, and get no compile-time safety or IDE help.
- **Evidence (reproduced):**
  - cmd: classify 2xx schema of 2,277 /api/v1 ops → dict[str,Any] 1,553; any ({}) 657; typed $ref 28; typed array 5; no content 27
  - e.g. GET /api/v1/goals/{goal_id}/open_questions → {type:object, additionalProperties:true}; POST /api/v1/goals/{goal_id}/answer and /cancel declare no response body schema
  - 1,769 of 2,277 /api/v1 ops have no description; 0 of 1,100 component schemas carry an example
- **Recommendation (effort L):** Add response_model= to routers (start with goals, questions, approvals, spend, connectors, channels), add examples via json_schema_extra, and add a CI ratchet counting untyped /api/v1 responses so the number only goes down.
- Source: C3-005 · prior audit: W3-4 (related: add response_model/responses declarations)

#### UX-446 · P2 · Docs · API spec is 2.4 MB / 2,587 ops mixing 131 HTML pages and 85 /static assets; 1,587 ops lumped under one 'v1' tag, 497 untagged; Swagger takes ~32 s and has no filter

- **Who / where:** developer, evaluator · `/openapi.json, /docs`
- **User impact:** A developer opening /docs waits half a minute, then scrolls one undifferentiated list that starts with tenant administration and interleaves UI pages and JS files; finding 'create a goal' or 'answer a question' is guesswork.
- **Evidence (reproduced):**
  - cmd: curl -w '%{size_download} %{time_total}' /openapi.json → 2,452,643 bytes, 8.49 s first fetch (0.10 s cached)
  - cmd: python analysis → 2,386 paths / 2,587 ops; 131 ops respond text/html (e.g. GET /goals, /settings, /privacy/board); 85 GET /static/*.js|css ops
  - tags: 'v1' on 1,587 ops, 131 distinct tags, 497 ops untagged
  - Playwright /docs: rendered after 31.9 s; first section 'v1' starting with /api/v1/admin/tenants; no operation filter input (count 0); screenshots shots/C3/docs_top.png, shots/C3/docs_bottom.png
- **Recommendation (effort M):** Set include_in_schema=False on HTML pages and static routes; replace the blanket 'v1' tag with product-area tags (Goals, Questions, Approvals, Spend, Connectors, Channels, Governance…); enable swaggerUiParameters filter=true and docExpansion='none'; publish a curated 'core' spec alongside the full one.
- Source: C3-006 · prior audit: W2-19 (related: spec size/public)

#### UX-447 · P2 · Docs · docs/api.md polling example only exits on 'done' or 'blocked', so it loops forever on cancelled/failed goals, and ignores the terminal flag the API returns

- Source: C3-012 · prior audit: W5-109 (same doc, different defect)

- **Recommendation (effort S):** Point the 401 at 'Settings > Integrations > Webhook signing secret'; add X-Lightwork-* headers (keep X-Maverick-* as aliases) and document verification code samples.

### Performance and scale (10)

#### UX-237 · P2 · Reliability · 'maverick dashboard' stop/restart waits for every running task to finish; the 20 s shutdown deadline is ignored

- **Who / where:** workspace admin, IT/security · `maverick dashboard (SIGTERM, Settings > Maintenance restart, systemd/docker stop)`
- **User impact:** An admin who restarts Lightwork to apply a setting waits until all running tasks finish, which for long tasks can be hours. Process managers usually SIGKILL after 10-90 s. The admin then hits the stuck-'active' state described in C4-001.
- **Evidence (reproduced):**
  - cmd: start '[slow]' task (2 x 20 s model calls), SIGTERM at +4 s -> process exited after 40.3 s; log 'Waiting for background tasks to complete. (CTRL+C to force quit)'
  - packages/maverick-core/maverick/cli/__init__.py:2917-2929 — CLI builds a plain uvicorn.Server(config) with no timeout_graceful_shutdown
  - packages/maverick-dashboard/maverick_dashboard/_server.py:74-91 — the bounded shutdown (DashboardServer) is only used by `python -m maverick_dashboard.app` (app.py:12033-12046)
  - packages/maverick-dashboard/maverick_dashboard/_lifecycle.py:19-31 — shutdown_timeout_seconds default 20
- **Recommendation (effort S):** Launch the CLI dashboard through maverick_dashboard._server.run_dashboard_server (or set config.timeout_graceful_shutdown from shutdown_seconds()), then checkpoint and mark in-flight goals 'interrupted, resumable' at the deadline. Show a 'N tasks running, stop anyway?' prompt on the in-app restart.
- Source: C4-003

#### UX-330 · P2 · Ux · Task search looks at only the 1,000 most recently updated tasks and silently returns nothing for older work

- **Who / where:** end user, compliance · `GET /api/v1/goals/search (sidebar 'Search chats')`
- **User impact:** A user searching for last quarter's report gets 'no results' as if it never existed, and each empty search takes ~1.5 s.
- **Evidence (reproduced):**
  - cmd: with 5,000 and again 20,000 seeded tasks, /api/v1/goals/search?q=Seeded%20task%203%3A -> [] (task 3 exists; it is older than the 1,000-row window); q=renewal returns recent matches
  - cmd: the no-match search costs 1.62 s (5k) / 1.54 s (20k) median of 3; the match search costs 0.56-0.58 s
  - packages/maverick-core/maverick/world_model.py:2271-2311 — search_goals(scan=1000): 'ORDER BY updated_at DESC LIMIT ?' then decrypt + substring filter in Python; no 'searched only recent N' signal returned
- **Recommendation (effort M):** Add a searchable index (a keyed-HMAC token index or FTS over a separately protected plaintext table where policy allows). At minimum return 'searched your latest 1,000 tasks — search older' with pagination over the scan window, plus date filters.
- Source: C4-008

#### UX-405 · P2 · Perf · A trivial chat turn ships 128 tool schemas (110 KB, ~27k tokens) to the model

- **Who / where:** end user, workspace admin · `POST /api/v1/goals, /chat/send -> orchestrator model call`
- **User impact:** Each simple question pays for ~27k input tokens of tool definitions before any work. That adds time-to-first-token and dollars to every turn (roughly $0.08 per turn at $3/M input, before caching), and the cost repeats on every step of multi-step tasks.
- **Evidence (reproduced):**
  - lab llm.jsonl (instrumented fake): orchestrator call for 'Say hello' req_bytes=113,534, n_tools=128, tools_bytes=109,831; same on all 76 logged calls (max req 113,718)
  - cmd: base_registry() -> 3,306 tools registered, 128 exposed after deferral
- **Recommendation (effort M):** Expose a minimal core toolset for chat (ask_user, search/fetch, file basics, tool_search) and defer the rest behind tool search. Mark offline calculators deferrable. Put the tool block behind a prompt-cache breakpoint. Add a CI budget on exposed-schema bytes.
- Source: C4-005 · prior audit: W1-122 (225 tools / ~47k tokens) — reduced but still present at HEAD

#### UX-407 · P2 · Perf · Dashboard cold start takes 14-36 s to answer /livez; ~40-50% of the import is spent re-materialising every route to rename them

- **Who / where:** evaluator, workspace admin, IT/security · `maverick dashboard startup; /livez`
- **User impact:** Every restart, including the ones needed to apply settings, leaves the product unreachable for 15-35 s. First-run evaluators see a dead browser tab, and health-check-driven deploys (ECS/K8s) risk killing a pod that is still starting.
- **Evidence (reproduced):**
  - cmd: c4work/dash_start.sh x3 -> livez after 29.3 / 20.4 / 16.5 s (median 20.4 s, load ~8 on 4 shared cores); earlier under load ~12: 26.6 / 36.0 / 36.3 s; later single runs 14.5, 13.6, 14.1 s at load ~1.4
  - cmd: import maverick_dashboard.app x3 -> wall 22.9/15.0/18.8 s, CPU 14.1/13.2/13.8 s (so ~13-14 s even on an idle core)
  - cmd: timing wrapper on route_identity.stabilize_effective_route_names -> 11.2/5.7/9.3 s = 49%/38%/50% of import
  - cProfile: stabilize_effective_route_names 25.8 s of 52.1 s profiled import; FastAPI _populate_api_route_state x8,781, get_dependant x23,276 (import.prof)
  - packages/maverick-dashboard/maverick_dashboard/route_identity.py:107-130,177-223 — _effective_routes() walks all lazy route contexts twice and marks routers changed (forcing a rebuild); app.py:12051
  - cmd: openapi paths = 2,386; app routes 380 top-level
- **Recommendation (effort M):** Compute unique route names statically, e.g. with a CI check that fails on colliding names or by using explicit name= on colliding handlers, instead of materialising all FastAPI effective contexts at import. Lazily import rarely used governance routers. Keep a startup budget test (e.g. import < 5 s CPU).
- Source: C4-004

#### UX-621 · P3 · Ux · After a crash the task shows the raw marker ' [process restarted mid-run]' as its result, and the marker stays while the task runs again

- **Who / where:** end user · `GET /api/v1/goals/{id}; chat thread`
- **User impact:** The user sees internal bracketed text instead of 'Interrupted when Lightwork restarted — Continue?', and the stale text stays visible while the task is running again.
- **Evidence (reproduced):**
  - cmd: after the restart > 60 s: goal 20462 {status:'blocked', result:' [process restarted mid-run]'}
  - cmd: after Resume: status 'active' with result still ' [process restarted mid-run]' for >30 s
  - packages/maverick-core/maverick/world_model.py:1420-1429 — marker appended into the result column
- **Recommendation (effort S):** Store interruption as a status reason/event, not in the result. Render a plain-language banner with Continue/Discard actions, and clear it on resume.
- Source: C4-018

#### UX-685 · P3 · Perf · Workforce, Learning, Trust and Tools pages take 0.4-0.8 s server time on an empty workspace

- **Who / where:** workspace admin, evaluator · `/workforce, /learning, /trust, /tools`
- **User impact:** These pages feel sluggish compared with the rest of the app even on a fresh install, and they get slower under concurrent users because rendering is synchronous.
- **Evidence (reproduced):**
  - cmd: pages.py (median of 3, loopback, no network) at 5k goals: /workforce 0.88 s, /learning 0.86 s, /trust 0.82 s, /tools 0.76 s; at 20k goals: 0.81/0.71/0.77/0.40 s — the cost doesn't depend on task count
  - same run: /, /chat, /overview, /approvals, /settings 0.03-0.12 s
- **Recommendation (effort S):** Profile and cache the pack/skill/tool catalog aggregates (they change only on install/config change); render the hero first and lazy-load the heavy panels.
- Source: C4-010 · prior audit: W3-24 (sync work on the event loop) related

#### UX-687 · P3 · Perf · About 1 s of platform overhead before the model is even called on a trivial task; the full 3,306-tool registry is rebuilt for every agent and child

- **Who / where:** end user, developer · `POST /api/v1/goals (instant fake model)`
- **User impact:** Short Q&A feels slower than the model's own latency, and swarm fan-out pays the registry build once per child.
- **Evidence (reproduced):**
  - cmd: latency2.py (warm) first model call at +0.90/+1.61/+0.85 s after submit; submit->done 0.96-1.75 s; 52-task run median 1.35 s (min 0.91, max 3.1) with a model that answers instantly (load ~7)
  - cmd: regbuild.py base_registry x6 -> 3,306 tools; cold 0.37 s CPU; warm median 0.19 s CPU / 0.60 s wall under load
  - packages/maverick-core/maverick/agent.py:1757,1968-1993 — every Agent (incl. spawn_subagent/swarm children) calls base_registry
  - llm.jsonl: 2 model calls per trivial task (orchestrator + reasoning-reward verifier)
  - [C5a-066] packages/maverick-core/maverick/agent.py:1757, 1968 — per-agent base_registry build and connector re-wrap (map/03t D22 measured ~0.3 s warm per build)
- **Recommendation (effort M):** Cache the immutable part of the registry per process (descriptor objects, schema JSON) and clone or bind per agent. Build the long-tail connector descriptors lazily. Trace pre-model phases in the run timeline so the overhead is visible.
- Source: C4-007, C5a-066 · prior audit: map/03t D22

#### UX-688 · P3 · Perf · First task after every dashboard start is ~3 s slower: the Anthropic SDK is imported lazily inside cost estimation even for other providers

- **Who / where:** end user, evaluator · `first chat/task after start`
- **User impact:** The first message after install or restart, which is also the evaluator's first impression, stalls for several extra seconds with no explanation.
- **Evidence (reproduced):**
  - cmd: latency2.py right after restart -> first task done +4.07 s (first model call at +3.82 s) vs next three 1.04/1.75/0.96 s
  - cProfile of `maverick start`: llm._estimate_call_cost 3.64 s, all in importing providers.anthropic_provider (llm.py:1490-1496) although provider is openai_compatible; providers.get_provider_client 2.0 s
  - cmd: import maverick.providers.anthropic_provider 2.02/2.39/1.59 s, openai 1.03/1.33/0.74 s
  - packages/maverick-dashboard/maverick_dashboard/app.py:629-646 — _warm_goal_runtime warms hooks only
- **Recommendation (effort S):** Import anthropic_provider.effective_max_tokens only when the model is an Anthropic model (or move the helper to a light module). Add provider SDK and client construction to _warm_goal_runtime.
- Source: C4-006

#### UX-691 · P3 · Perf · Dashboard uses ~300 MB RSS idle and ~440 MB after 50 trivial tasks

- **Who / where:** workspace admin, evaluator · `maverick dashboard process`
- **User impact:** A single-user install needs a ~1 GB VPS before any agent work. A laptop evaluator gives up nearly half a GB to an idle dashboard.
- **Evidence (reproduced):**
  - cmd: /proc/<pid>/status after start: VmRSS 292-307 MB (6 starts)
  - after 4 tasks 407 MB; after 30 tasks 441 MB; after 52 tasks 442 MB (HWM 448 MB), 12 threads, 29-31 fds — plateau, no leak seen over 22 tasks

- Source: C4-012

#### UX-692 · P3 · Perf · /openapi.json is 2.4 MB with 2,386 paths and takes 5.5 s to build on first request; /docs is unusable as an API browser

- **Who / where:** developer · `/openapi.json, /docs`
- **User impact:** Integrators opening the API docs wait several seconds for a 2.4 MB spec, and the browser UI struggles to render it. There is no per-area spec to hand a partner.
- **Evidence (reproduced):**
  - cmd: pages.py -> /openapi.json first 5.48 s then 0.07-0.09 s, 2,395 KB
  - cmd: app.openapi() -> 2,386 paths, 2,610,690 bytes
- **Recommendation (effort M):** Publish tagged sub-specs (core goals/chat, governance, consent, …) at /openapi/{area}.json, pre-build the schema in the background after startup, and hide internal/admin-only routes from the public spec.
- Source: C4-009

### Kernel, models, safety and data (code defects) (67)

#### UX-124 · P2 · Trust · No default safety net for runaway tasks: with no caps and no step limit, a task that never finishes keeps calling the model until someone cancels it

- **Who / where:** workspace admin, evaluator, end user · `default Budget(); [budget] task_limits_enabled; installer budget step`
- **User impact:** An evaluator on a pay-per-token key, or a business user whose task loops (varying its tool calls so the identical-call guard never fires), can spend without limit until someone notices and cancels. No warning appears as spend climbs, and nothing on the task page shows 'this task has no limit'.
- **Evidence (code-verified):**
  - packages/maverick-core/maverick/budget.py:609-614 — every Budget cap defaults to None
  - packages/maverick-core/maverick/agent.py:1725-1726, 4346 — max_steps None → unbounded step range
  - packages/maverick-core/maverick/agent.py:4410-4413, tools/spawn.py:91-93 — synthesis reserve / spawn pause only act when max_dollars is set
  - docs/task-limits.md:3-5 — 'Ordinary goals no longer receive generated dollar, elapsed-time, token, tool-call or 25-step limits'; installer offers no task limit by default
- **Recommendation (effort M):** Keep 'no hard cap' if desired, but add a soft guard on by default: a per-task spend/step check-in (e.g. pause and ask after $X or N steps, configurable on Settings > Budget and in the wizard), and show running cost and 'no limit set' on the task page.
- Source: C5a-017

#### UX-128 · P2 · Trust · Retention enforcement at the operator level skips the shared workspace and per-user tenants whenever any registered tenant exists

- **Who / where:** compliance, workspace admin · `maverick retention enforce / scheduled retention (operator scope)`
- **User impact:** A privacy officer configures '90-day retention' and sees a successful run, but data in the default workspace and in per-user/channel tenants is kept indefinitely, which can breach the organisation's retention commitments.
- **Evidence (code-verified):** packages/maverick-core/maverick/audit/retention.py:452-474 — with no active tenant and a non-empty registry, enforce() loops only over list_tenants() and returns; the untenanted/shared store and per-user tenants (api:<p>, <channel>:<user>, not in the registry) are never purged
- **Recommendation (effort S):** Include the shared store and every data directory under tenants/ in the fleet sweep, and report per-store counts (including 'skipped') in the retention report shown in the Privacy workbench.
- Source: C5a-072 · prior audit: W1-57 (related: missing retention paths)

#### UX-129 · P2 · Trust · On shared Postgres in compatibility mode, several goal mutators can change legacy rows that belong to no tenant, and re-parenting ignores the new parent's tenant

- **Who / where:** IT/security · `Postgres backend without strict tenant mode`
- **User impact:** After a migration from single-tenant, legacy tasks without a tenant can be modified by any tenant's users, and a goal can be attached under another tenant's parent.
- **Evidence (code-verified):**
  - packages/maverick-core/maverick/world_model_backends/postgres.py:1555-1764 — set_goal_status, set_goal_partial_result, touch_goal, set_goal_domain, set_goal_title, set_goal_parent use _tenant_scope() (includes tenant_id IS NULL)
  - postgres.py:939-951 — _mutation_tenant_scope documents the exact scope; block_goal_admission, claim_goal_for_run, bind_goal_owner use it
- **Recommendation (effort S):** Use _mutation_tenant_scope for all mutators and verify the parent's tenant in set_goal_parent.
- Source: C5a-076

#### UX-138 · P2 · Trust · Approval delegation rules only add a text label, which is dropped for shell and connector approvals, and nobody is restricted to the delegate

- **Who / where:** workspace admin, compliance, IT/security · `[approval] delegation rules; Approvals page`
- **User impact:** An admin routes high-risk approvals to a named delegate (e.g. finance approvals to the controller). The approval still goes to everyone, anyone can approve it, and for the most sensitive approvals the note saying who should decide is not even shown.
- **Evidence (code-verified):**
  - packages/maverick-core/maverick/safety/consent.py:1238-1244 — delegate appended to detail as '[delegated to: X]'
  - packages/maverick-core/maverick/safety/consent.py:1255-1260 — when an approval_card is supplied (every require_operation_consent: shell, governed connectors) detail is replaced by encode_approval_detail(approval_card), dropping the label
  - consent.py:1235 cites '[governance.delegation]' while approval_delegation.py:63-70 reads '[approval] delegation'
- **Recommendation (effort M):** Store the delegate as a structured field on the approval, enforce it at decision time, keep it visible on the approval card, and fix the config name in the comment/docs.
- Source: C5a-042

#### UX-139 · P2 · Trust · Containment mode's 'commands get no network' is not enforced on the SSH and plugin (ep:) sandbox backends

- **Who / where:** IT/security, compliance · `[containment] enabled = true with [sandbox] backend = ssh or ep:<plugin>`
- **User impact:** During an incident an admin switches on containment expecting agent commands to be cut off from the network; on SSH or plugin sandboxes they keep full network access and (for SSH) the real workspace.
- **Evidence (code-verified):**
  - packages/maverick-core/maverick/sandbox/__init__.py:396-398 — containment only sets allow_network=False / network='egress-deny' in the backend config
  - packages/maverick-core/maverick/sandbox/__init__.py:588-604 — SSHBackend is built without any network setting; ep: backends likewise (475-484)
  - packages/maverick-core/maverick/containment.py:41-45 — 'commands get no network and a throwaway folder'
- **Recommendation (effort S):** Make _contain refuse (fail closed with a clear message) for backends that cannot honour no-network, as _offline_policy already does, and list supported backends on the containment screen.
- Source: C5a-045

#### UX-140 · P2 · Trust · A project's devcontainer spec with remoteUser '0' or 'root:root' runs the agent as root against the writable project mount

- **Who / where:** IT/security, developer · `[sandbox] backend = "devcontainer"`
- **User impact:** A repository the agent is asked to work on can ship a devcontainer.json that quietly makes the sandbox run as root on the host-mounted folder, defeating the non-root pin.
- **Evidence (code-verified):** packages/maverick-core/maverick/sandbox/devcontainer.py:240-243 — any remote_user != 'root' is passed verbatim as --user, so '0' or 'root:root' yields root
- **Recommendation (effort S):** Normalise remote_user (split on ':', treat 0/root case-insensitively as root) before the comparison and add tests for '0', '0:0', 'root:root'.
- Source: C5a-043 · prior audit: W1-88 (still present at HEAD)

#### UX-141 · P2 · Trust · System-prompt leak detection never runs on agent answers: the kernel's output scans don't pass the prompt to compare against

- **Who / where:** IT/security, compliance · `agent/orchestrator scan_output calls`
- **User impact:** A prompt-injection that makes an agent recite its system prompt, pack instructions or embedded policy text is not caught on the main chat/goal path, though the feature is advertised.
- **Evidence (code-verified):**
  - packages/maverick-shield/maverick_shield/guard.py:435-450 — scan_output(text, known_prompt=None) runs output_policy with known_prompt
  - packages/maverick-core/maverick/agent.py:1606, 3313; orchestrator.py:286, 547, 647, 1202, 2301 — none pass known_prompt
  - only ai_runtime_guardrails.py:533, 606 pass it
- **Recommendation (effort S):** Pass the agent's system prompt (or a hash-based fingerprint set) as known_prompt at agent.py:3313 and the orchestrator final-output scans.
- Source: C5a-047

#### UX-142 · P2 · Trust · The 'secure-by-default' tool risk ceiling blocks nothing: there is no 'critical' tier, and the default ceiling is already the top level

- **Who / where:** IT/security, workspace admin, compliance · `[security] max_risk; secure_defaults`
- **User impact:** Security teams are told funds movement, mass deletion and production writes are held back by default. In reality the default ceiling admits every tool, and anyone who writes max_risk='critical' gets a medium ceiling instead.
- **Evidence (reproduced):**
  - packages/maverick-core/maverick/safety/tool_risk.py:35 — RISK_LEVELS = ('low','medium','high')
  - packages/maverick-core/maverick/safety/tool_acl.py:31-35 — docstring: 'under secure-by-default the ceiling is high ... so CRITICAL-risk tools need an explicit raise'
  - cmd: python → RISK_LEVELS ('low','medium','high'); risk_rank('critical') = 1 (same as medium); tool_acl.resolve_max_risk() = 'high' (the top rank)
- **Recommendation (effort M):** Either add a real 'critical' tier with classified tools (payments, mass delete, prod writes) and keep the default at 'high', or correct the docs and reject unknown levels in config validation.
- Source: C5a-040

#### UX-146 · P2 · Trust · Salesforce and Stripe read ops interpolate model-supplied values into URL paths/queries unencoded, letting a prompt-injected agent read other endpoints with the company credential

- **Who / where:** IT/security · `salesforce (version), stripe customer_get / customer_search`
- **User impact:** Injected content can steer 'read one customer' calls to other API paths under the same Stripe or Salesforce key, and these reads are not governed.
- **Evidence (code-verified):**
  - packages/maverick-core/maverick/tools/salesforce_tool.py:86-88, 207 — version used in f'{url}/services/data/{version}' without validation (sobject/id are validated at 38-42)
  - packages/maverick-core/maverick/tools/stripe_tool.py:139-141 — _get(f'customers/{cid}'); 153-155 — email interpolated into a Stripe search query
  - tools/__init__.py:57-66 — notes httpx normalises '..' segments; safe_path_segment exists but is unused here
- **Recommendation (effort S):** Validate with safe_path_segment / strict id regexes and escape search-query values.
- Source: C5a-059

#### UX-147 · P2 · Trust · http_fetch lets the model send POST requests with arbitrary headers and body to any public host without approval

- **Who / where:** IT/security, compliance · `tool http_fetch (method POST)`
- **User impact:** A prompt-injected agent can post workspace data to an attacker's server in one call; data-loss controls rely only on egress allow-lists that are off by default.
- **Evidence (code-verified):** packages/maverick-core/maverick/tools/http_fetch.py (method/headers/body args; no consent call; only SSRF/egress checks) — per map/03t D19; tool_risk http_fetch='high' but no approval gate besides rehearsal
- **Recommendation (effort S):** Require approval (or an admin allow-list of POST destinations) for non-GET http_fetch, and redact secrets from bodies.
- Source: C5a-061

#### UX-148 · P2 · Trust · image_edit sends workspace images to Replicate using the operator's REPLICATE_API_TOKEN with no approval, while the equivalent replicate call requires one

- **Who / where:** IT/security, workspace admin, compliance · `tool image_edit ops inpaint / variation / upscale`
- **User impact:** Company images (screenshots, documents, product photos) can be uploaded to a third-party AI service and billed to the operator's account without anyone approving it, though the same action through the Replicate tool asks first.
- **Evidence (code-verified):**
  - packages/maverick-core/maverick/tools/image_edit.py:118-178 — remote ops post image bytes via replicate_tool helpers with the ambient token
  - tools/__init__.py:703-716 — replicate is in AUTHENTICATED_AMBIENT_CRED_TOOL_NAMES, image_edit is not; image_edit has no confirm and is not in the governed write set; tool_risk unclassified → 'medium'
- **Recommendation (effort S):** Govern image_edit's remote ops like replicate run (approval + ambient-credential rule) and classify it 'high'.
- Source: C5a-057

#### UX-149 · P2 · Trust · The model can hot-add an MCP server's tools with learn_capability without the authorisation, stale-binding and rate-limit guards applied to normally loaded MCP tools

- **Who / where:** IT/security, workspace admin · `tool learn_capability op add_mcp_server`
- **User impact:** Tools from an MCP server added mid-task run without the checks an admin relies on for MCP tools loaded at startup.
- **Evidence (code-verified):**
  - packages/maverick-core/maverick/tools/learn.py:124-127 — tools_from_mcp(client) then agent.tools.register(t) directly
  - packages/maverick-core/maverick/tools/__init__.py:1644-1667 — the normal _apply_mcp_tools path adds authorize, binding_guards, rate limits and governed wrapping
- **Recommendation (effort S):** Route hot registration through _apply_mcp_tools (same guards), or make hot-added servers available only on the next run after admin review.
- Source: C5a-060

#### UX-150 · P2 · Trust · lsp_bridge starts language servers on the host rooted at the server's working directory, not the agent's workspace

- **Who / where:** IT/security, developer · `tool lsp_bridge`
- **User impact:** Code-intelligence queries can index and reveal files from the server's own directory (possibly the installation or other users' data) rather than the task's workspace, outside any container sandbox.
- **Evidence (code-verified):**
  - packages/maverick-core/maverick/tools/lsp_bridge.py:236-238 — root = MAVERICK_WORKSPACE_ROOT or os.getcwd()
  - packages/maverick-core/maverick/tools/__init__.py:1288 — registered without a sandbox; lsp_bridge.py:81-88 host Popen
- **Recommendation (effort M):** Root the language server at sandbox.workdir and run it inside the sandbox (or disable lsp_bridge for non-local backends).
- Source: C5a-063

#### UX-151 · P2 · Trust · 174 of 274 built-in tools have no risk rating and default to 'medium', including network, cost and device tools

- **Who / where:** IT/security, workspace admin · `[security] max_risk ceilings; channel ceilings`
- **User impact:** An admin who limits a channel or role to 'medium' risk still exposes device control, paid third-party APIs and auth helpers, because they were never rated.

- **Recommendation (effort S):** Classify every registered tool and add the CI check proposed in W1-123 (every base_registry name must satisfy tool_risk_is_classified).

#### UX-152 · P2 · Trust · Swarm children quarantined for prompt injection still have their raw output sent to SUBAGENT_STOP hooks

- **Who / where:** IT/security, developer · `spawn_swarm + configured hooks (logging, routing, webhooks)`
- **User impact:** Attacker-controlled text from a sub-agent the shield sealed can reach hook consumers (SIEM, chat notifications, downstream automations) when work is fanned out as a swarm.
- **Evidence (code-verified):**
  - packages/maverick-core/maverick/tools/spawn.py:207-219 — single-child path withholds a sealed child's final from the hook ('must never surface -- not even inside a SUBAGENT_STOP hook payload')
  - packages/maverick-core/maverick/tools/spawn.py:636-644 — swarm path emits extra={'final': res.final} for every non-raising child with no sealed check
- **Recommendation (effort S):** Reuse _sealed_notice for each swarm child before emitting the hook, and add a swarm test mirroring the single-child one.
- Source: C5a-056

#### UX-204 · P2 · Bug · Hitting the emergency stop (HALT) between tool calls reports 'the assistant ran into an error ... maverick resume N' and records the run as a failure in the learning loop

- **October 4 source reconciliation:** The serial tool-call HALT return now sets `stop_kind="killswitch"` and `stop_detail`, matching the other HALT paths. The orchestrator's HALT branch therefore applies rather than the generic agent-error learning path. This was code-reviewed in the current branch; a live interrupted task has not been exercised here.
- **Who / where:** workspace admin, end user, IT/security · `goal result text (dashboard task view), learning signals (skills, reflexion, consequence)`
- **User impact:** When an operator halts the platform while an agent is between tool calls, the task shows a generic error and advises 'try again with maverick resume', which just halts again. The halted run is also scored as a genuine failure, so the skills and planning modes that were in use are down-weighted for something that was not their fault.
- **Evidence (code-verified):**
  - packages/maverick-core/maverick/agent.py:5408-5418 — serial per-tool halt check returns AgentResult(error=f'halted: {e}') WITHOUT stop_kind='killswitch'
  - packages/maverick-core/maverick/agent.py:4363-4366 and 5262-5266 — every other halt return sets stop_kind='killswitch'
  - packages/maverick-core/maverick/orchestrator.py:2213-2222 — only stop_kind=='killswitch' gets the 'Lightwork was halted ... maverick unhalt' message
  - packages/maverick-core/maverick/orchestrator.py:2235-2276 — otherwise: episode 'failure', reflexion 'agent_error', _record_skill_outcome(success=False), consequence.record_self_outcome(0.0), message 'Stopped: the assistant ran into an error ... You can try again with: maverick resume {goal_id}'
- **Recommendation (effort S):** Add stop_kind='killswitch', stop_detail=str(e) to the AgentResult at agent.py:5415. Add a test that trips killswitch between two serial tool calls and asserts the halted message and that no failure outcome is recorded.
- Source: C5a-002 · prior audit: W1-33 (related: halt/review-stop message misclassification)

#### UX-205 · P2 · Bug · CLI tasks silently get a learned dollar cap (0.25–100 USD) after about 8 runs of the same kind, contradicting 'ordinary goals no longer receive generated dollar limits'

- **October 4 source fix:** Learned task-class caps now require an explicit `true` opt-in. Settings > Spending & limits exposes the choice in plain language; the default is off, a malformed config value cannot enable it, and explicit limits keep precedence. The 25 focused budget/learning checks and the exact Settings catalog reader check passed locally; no installed CLI run has been verified.
- **Who / where:** developer, workspace admin · `maverick start (CLI); [budget] self_tuning (default on via governed_learning_default)`
- **User impact:** A developer running the same kind of task from the terminal finds later runs stopping with 'budget exceeded' at an amount nobody configured. Dashboard runs of the same task do not stop, so the behaviour looks random.
- **Evidence (code-verified):**
  - packages/maverick-core/maverick/self_tuning_budget.py:39-53 — enabled() defaults to governed_learning_default() (True)
  - packages/maverick-core/maverick/budget.py:1164-1166 — docstring 'Off by default ([budget] self_tuning)'; budget.py:1105 task_limits_enabled defaults True
  - packages/maverick-core/maverick/cli/__init__.py:3926-3933 — maverick start passes task_class, enabling the learned cap
  - docs/task-limits.md:3-5 — 'Ordinary goals no longer receive generated dollar ... limits'
- **Recommendation (effort S):** Make self-tuning caps opt-in (match the docstring and docs) or show them explicitly ('learned cap $X for this kind of task — change') in CLI output and Settings > Budget.
- Source: C5a-031

#### UX-206 · P2 · Bug · Free OpenRouter models still hit the 'unpriced model' refusal on the billing path, although the release notes say free OpenRouter models are priced at $0

- **October 4 source fix:** `OpenRouterClient` now supplies `openrouter:` to the shared response accounting path. A listed free model therefore reaches the verified $0 price rule under strict billing; unknown paid models remain refused. Focused response-accounting and budget checks passed locally (36 cases). A live OpenRouter response is still unverified.
- **Who / where:** evaluator, end user · `OpenRouter provider with a ':free' model under default strict pricing`
- **User impact:** A trial user who picks a free OpenRouter model to avoid cost sees the health check and estimates say $0, then the first task stops after one call with 'unpriced model'.
- **Evidence (reproduced):**

  - packages/maverick-core/maverick/budget.py:554-561 — $0 rule requires the 'openrouter:' prefix in the id
  - cmd: scratchpad/audit/C5a/llm/repro_llm.py with free_models patched → _lookup_price('openrouter:meta-llama/llama-3.3-70b-instruct:free') = (0.0, 0.0) but Budget().record_tokens(10,10, model='meta-llama/llama-3.3-70b-instruct:free') (the id the client records) → UnpricedModelError
- **Recommendation (effort S):** Set PRICE_MODEL_PREFIX='openrouter:' on OpenRouterClient (or pass the provider-qualified id to record_tokens) and add an end-to-end test through _from_response.
- Source: C5a-025

#### UX-212 · P2 · Bug · Settings 'Governed connector approver' ([governed_connectors] approver) has no effect on who approves connector writes

- **October 4 source fix:** A configured standing approver must now match the authenticated actor on the fresh decision before any PREPARE receipt or connector call. The approval card binds the configured approver into its exact target, so a change while waiting invalidates the permit. The governed-tool test file passed locally (126 cases); live two-person approval and provider writes remain unverified.
- **Who / where:** workspace admin, compliance · `Settings catalog governed_connectors.approver / MAVERICK_GOVERNED_APPROVER`
- **User impact:** An admin names the person who must approve CRM or database writes and believes the control is in place; any approver on the Approvals page can still approve them.

  - grep '_approver()' → only its definition (no production caller); approval identity is decision.actor or decision.source (governed_tools.py:688)
  - packages/maverick-dashboard/maverick_dashboard/settings_catalog.py:1333-1339 — setting says changes 'are approved against' this person
- **Recommendation (effort S):** Enforce it: require decision.actor == configured approver (or membership of an approver group) for governed writes; otherwise remove the setting.
- Source: C5a-041

#### UX-225 · P2 · Bug · The remember_outcome_key tool crashes on every call ('dict' object has no attribute 'strip'), so agents can never link work to a business outcome

- **Who / where:** end user, workspace admin · `tool remember_outcome_key (sent to the model by default)`
- **User impact:** When the assistant tries to tie a task to a business outcome (a renewal, a deal) so results can be measured later, the step always fails with a Python error. The outcome link that the learning and ROI features rely on is never stored, and the user sees an internal error in the task trace.
- **Evidence (reproduced):**
  - packages/maverick-core/maverick/tools/outcome_link.py:39-41 — `def run(key: str = '')` then `(key or '').strip()`
  - packages/maverick-core/maverick/tool_result_stream.py:252 — the registry calls every executor as fn(args) with ONE positional dict
  - tests/test_outcome_link_tool.py:27 — tests only call tool.fn(key=...), so the live calling convention is untested
  - cmd: scripted task calling remember_outcome_key {'key':'renewal-2026'} via run_goal_in_thread → tool result 'ERROR: AttributeError: \'dict\' object has no attribute \'strip\'' (scratchpad/audit/C5a/tools/out_tools.txt)
- **Recommendation (effort S):** Change the signature to run(args: dict) and read args.get('key'); add a test that goes through ToolRegistry.run with a dict payload. Consider a registry-level test that invokes every registered tool with its schema's minimal args to catch signature mismatches.
- Source: C5a-012

#### UX-244 · P2 · Reliability · Restarting the dashboard marks long-running background tasks run by another process as 'blocked [process restarted mid-run]' while they are still working

- **Who / where:** end user, workspace admin · `dashboard startup (app.py:1562 reclaim_orphan_goals), maverick serve, worker processes`
- **User impact:** In any deployment where a worker or `maverick serve` runs tasks and the dashboard restarts (upgrade, crash, scaling), non-chat tasks that have been working for over a minute suddenly show as blocked by a restart. Users re-run them (duplicate work and spend), and the status later changes back to done without explanation.
- **Evidence (reproduced):**
  - packages/maverick-core/maverick/world_model.py:1391-1410 — docstring: 'Live goals re-touch updated_at via set_goal_status(active) and via the runner's status writes'
  - grep touch_goal( → only external_agents.py:1047; agent loop writes goal status only at start/end; partial-answer streaming (agent.py:1614) only runs for chat goals with a conversation
  - packages/maverick-dashboard/maverick_dashboard/app.py:1562 — dashboard boot calls wm.reclaim_orphan_goals() (default window 60 s)
  - cmd: scratchpad/audit/C5a/k9 — goal '[slow] compile the weekly vendor summary' running in process A; at t=16 s process B ran reclaim_orphan_goals with MAVERICK_ORPHAN_RECLAIM_SECONDS=10 (shortened from 60 to save time) → 'before reclaim: active updated_at age=15.7s', 'reclaimed: 1', 'after reclaim: blocked \' [process restarted mid-run]\''; process A kept running and later set status 'done'
- **Recommendation (effort S):** Heartbeat the goal row from the agent loop (touch_goal every N seconds or each turn) and/or record the owning process lease so reclaim only targets goals whose lease holder is gone.
- Source: C5a-009

#### UX-245 · P2 · Reliability · Starting a task that is already running (double-click, retry, queue redelivery) flips the live task to 'blocked — internal error' while it keeps running

- **Who / where:** end user, workspace admin · `run_goal_in_thread (dashboard run/retry, API, worker)`
- **User impact:** A user who clicks run/retry twice, or a queue that redelivers a job, sees the task they are waiting on turn into 'blocked: internal error' even though it is still working. They may start it again or give up. A queue worker treats 'error' as retryable, so it can make more attempts against the same running task.
- **Evidence (reproduced):**
  - packages/maverick-core/maverick/orchestrator.py:2723 — run_goal enters task_file_recovery.run_scope
  - packages/maverick-core/maverick/task_file_recovery.py:56-79 — non-blocking lease raises RecoveryConflict('This task is running ...')
  - packages/maverick-core/maverick/runner.py:441-454 — any exception → world.set_goal_status(goal_id, 'blocked', result='internal error'); return 'error' (retryable)
  - packages/maverick-core/maverick/runner.py:252 — _allowance_admission admits status 'active'
  - cmd: scratchpad/audit/C5a/k7/repro_k7.py → while run #1 in flight status='active'; second run_goal_in_thread → 'goal #1 crashed inside run_goal_sync ... RecoveryConflict' and status='blocked' result='internal error'; run #1 later finished and overwrote status='done'
- **Recommendation (effort S):** Catch RecoveryConflict in run_goal_in_thread and return a distinct 'already_running' status without touching the goal row (and have the worker drop the job). Also reject 'active' goals in _allowance_admission or claim the goal atomically (claim_goal_for_run) before dispatch.
- Source: C5a-007

#### UX-248 · P2 · Reliability · A late or replayed Stripe webhook can suspend a tenant that has already paid (or restore one that hasn't): events are applied without event-id dedup or ordering

- **Who / where:** workspace admin, end user · `Stripe webhook → billing_stripe.handle_event`
- **User impact:** Stripe delivers events out of order and retries them. A delayed 'payment_failed' arriving after 'payment_succeeded' marks a paying customer past-due and downgrades their workspace; the reverse restores a non-paying one.
- **Evidence (code-verified):**
  - packages/maverick-core/maverick/billing_stripe.py:790-826 — billing_status is set purely from event type/status; no stored event id or created timestamp comparison
  - billing_stripe.py:729-732 — only the 300 s signature tolerance limits replay
- **Recommendation (effort S):** Persist processed event ids and the latest applied event 'created' per tenant/subscription; ignore duplicates and older events, or re-fetch the subscription state from Stripe before changing billing_status.
- Source: C5a-034

#### UX-249 · P2 · Reliability · Hitting a local provider spending cap (or a locked cost ledger) counts as a provider outage and trips the shared circuit breaker for every workspace for 30 s

- **Who / where:** workspace admin, end user · `llm.py dispatch; [providers] cost caps`
